(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_facet_long_short_edge_ratio"
A **tessellated_facet_long_short_edge_ratio** type specifies the maximum aspect ratio of any facet in a tessellated shape model. A **tessellated_facet_long_short_edge_ratio** is the ratio of the longest to shortest edge of a facet.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_facet_long_short_edge_ratio.__note"
*tessellated_facet_long_short_edge_ratio* is an easily calculated criterion used to verify that the individual facets in a tessellated geometry have edges of similar lengths.
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.boolean_operand"
A **boolean_operand** type identifies all those types of entities which may participate in a boolean operation to form a CSG solid. This includes provision for the special case of a two dimensional 'solid' which is an arcwise connected finite region in two dimensional space defined by boolean operations with 2D operands.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.boolean_operator"
A **boolean_operator** type defines the three boolean operators used in the definition of CSG solids.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.boolean_operator.union"
the operation of constructing the regularised set theoretic union of the volumes defined by two solids;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.boolean_operator.intersection"
the operation of constructing the regularised set theoretic intersection of the volumes defined by two solids;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.boolean_operator.difference"
the regularised set theoretic difference between the volumes defined by two solids;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.bounded_primitive_2d"
A **bounded_primitive_2d** extensible select type defines the set of two dimensional CSG primitives of finite size which may participate in boolean operations or be used as <<express:geometric_model_schema.csg_solid.tree_root_expression,tree_root_expression>> to directly define a two dimensional CSG solid.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.chordal_deviation"
A **chordal_deviation** type specifies the maximum chordal deviation of any facet in a tessellated shape model. Chordal deviation is the maximum value of the minimum distance from any point on the edge of a facet to the closest point on the surface being approximated by the facets.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.csg_primitive"
A **csg_primitive** select type defines the set of CSG primitives which may participate in boolean operations or be used as <<express:geometric_model_schema.csg_solid.tree_root_expression,tree_root_expression>> to directly define a CSG solid.

The 3D CSG primitives are <<express:geometric_model_schema.sphere,sphere>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.ellipsoid,ellipsoid>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.right_circular_cone,right_circular_cone>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.eccentric_cone,eccentric_cone>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.right_circular_cylinder,right_circular_cylinder>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.torus,torus>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.block,block>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.faceted_primitive,faceted_primitive>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.rectangular_pyramid,rectangular_pyramid>>, and <<express:geometric_model_schema.right_angular_wedge,right_angular_wedge>>. The <<express:geometric_model_schema.bounded_primitive_2d,bounded_primitive_2d>> instances which are all types of <<express:geometric_model_schema.primitive_2d,primitive_2d>> may participate in boolean operations with other two dimensional entities.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.csg_select"
A **csg_select** select type identifies the types of entity which may be selected as the root of a CSG tree including a single CSG primitive as a special case.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.edge_or_curve"
An **edge_or_curve** select type identifies the types of entity which may be selected as the underlying geometry of a tessellated edge.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.face_or_surface"
A **face_or_surface** select type identifies the types of entity which may be selected as the underlying geometry of a tessellated face.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.geometric_set_select"
A **geometric_set_select** type identifies the types of entities which can occur in a <<express:geometric_model_schema.geometric_set,geometric_set>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.length_to_height_ratio"
A **length_to_height_ratio** type specifies the maximum ratio of height to length of any facets in a tessellated shape model. The height is measured in a direction perpendicular to the longest edge of a facet.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.length_to_height_ratio.__note"
*length_to_height_ratio* is a criterion used to ensure reasonable proportions of the facets and thus, ensure the regularity of a set of facets in a tessellated geometry.
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.maximum_edge_length"
A **maximum_edge_length** type specifies the maximum length of any edge off any facet of a tessellated shape model.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.path_or_composite_curve"
A **path_or_composite_curve** select type identifies the types of entities in a geometric model which can be linked to a <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_wire,tessellated_wire>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.surface_model"
A **surface_model** select type collects all possible surface model entities.

Some product model representations consist of collections of surfaces which do not necessarily form the complete boundary of a solid. Such a model can be represented by a collection of <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> instances or <<express:topology_schema.shell,shell>> instances.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge_or_vertex"
A **tessellated_edge_or_vertex** select type identifies the types of entities that are used as items in the definition of a <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_wire,tessellated_wire>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellation_accuracy_parameter_item"
A **tessellation_accuracy_parameter_item** select type identifies the types of entities that are used as items in the definition of <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_shape_representation_with_accuracy_parameters.tessellation_accuracy_parameters,tessellation_accuracy_parameters>> of a <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_shape_representation_with_accuracy_parameters,tessellated_shape_representation_with_accuracy_parameters>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.wireframe_model"
A **wireframe_model** type collects all possible wireframe model entities.

A wireframe representation of a geometric model contains information only about the intersections of the surfaces forming the boundary but does not contain information about the surfaces themselves.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.solid_model"
A **solid_model** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>> which is a complete representation of the nominal shape of a product such that all points in the interior are connected. Any point can be classified as being inside, outside or on the boundary of a solid.

There are several different types of solid model representations including 'solid's defined as connected regions in two dimensional space.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep"
A **manifold_solid_brep** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.solid_model,solid_model>> which is is a finite, arcwise connected volume bounded by one or more surfaces, each of which is a connected, oriented, finite, closed 2-manifold. There is no restriction on the number of through holes, nor on the number of voids within the volume. The Boundary Representation (B-rep) of a manifold solid utilises a graph of edges and vertices embedded in a connected, oriented, finite, closed two manifold surface. The embedded graph divides the surface into arcwise connected areas known as faces. The edges and vertices, therefore, form the boundaries of the faces and the domain of a face does not include its boundaries. The embedded graph may be disconnected and may be a pseudograph. The graph is labelled; that is, each entity in the graph has a unique identity. The geometric surface definition used to specify the geometry of a face shall be 2-manifold embeddable in the plane within the domain of the face. In other words, it shall be connected, oriented, finite, non-self-intersecting, and of surface genus 0. Faces do not intersect except along their boundaries. Each edge along the boundary of a face is shared by at most one other face in the assemblage. The assemblage of edges in the B-rep do not intersect except at their boundaries (i.e., vertices). The geometric curve definition used to specify the geometry of an edge shall be arcwise connected and shall not self-intersect or overlap within the domain of the edge. The geometry of an edge shall be consistent with the geometry of the faces of which it forms a partial bound. The geometry used to define a vertex shall be consistent with the geometry of the faces and edges of which it forms a partial bound. A B-rep is represented by one or more <<express:topology_schema.closed_shell,closed_shell>> instances which shall be disjoint. One shell, the outer, shall completely enclose all the other shells and no other shell may enclose a shell. The facility to define a B-rep with one or more internal voids is provided by the <<express:geometric_model_schema.brep_with_voids,brep_with_voids>> subtype. The following version of the Euler formula shall be satisfied

[[eqnGM1]]

[stem]
++++
chi_{ms} = V - E + 2F - L_{l} - 2(S - G^{s}) = 0
++++

where stem:[V], stem:[E], stem:[F], stem:[L_{l}] and stem:[S] are the numbers of unique vertices, edges, faces, face bounds and shells in the model and stem:[G^s] is the sum of the genus of the shells. More specifically, the topological entities shall conform to the following constraints, where stem:[B] denotes a manifold solid B-rep:

* The shells shall be unique
[stem]
++++
(B)[S] = (B){S}
++++

* Each face in the B-rep is unique
[stem]
++++
((B)[S])[F] = ((B)[S]){F}
++++

* Each loop is unique
[stem]
++++
(((B)[S])[F])[L] = (((B)[S])[F]){L}
++++

* Each (edge + logical) pair is unique
[stem]
++++
((((B)[S])[F])[L])[E_{l}] = ((((B)[S])[F])[L]) E_{l}
++++

* Each edge in the B-rep is either used by exactly two loops or twice by one loop
[stem]
++++
|((((B)[S])[F])[L]){E_{l} }| = 2 |((((B)[S])[F])[L])[E_{l}]|
++++
+
That is, in the list stem:[((((B)[S\])[F\])[L\])[E\]] each edge appears exactly twice.

* Equation <<eqnGM1>> shall be satisfied
[stem]
++++
2|(B)[S]| - 2 Sigma G^{s} = |(((((B)[S])[F]){L ^{e} }){E}){V}| + |((((B)[S])[F]){L ^{v} } ){V}| - |((((B)[S])[F]){L}){E}| + 2|((B)[S])[F]| - |(((B)[S])[F])[L]|
++++

The topological normal of the B-rep at each point on its boundary is the surface normal direction that points away from the solid material. The <<express:topology_schema.closed_shell,closed_shell>> normals, as used, shall be consistent with the topological normal of the B-rep. The **manifold_solid_brep** has two subtypes, <<express:geometric_model_schema.faceted_brep,faceted_brep>> and <<express:geometric_model_schema.brep_with_voids,brep_with_voids>>, with which there exists a default ANDOR relationship. The following can all be instantiated:

* **manifold_solid_brep**
* <<express:geometric_model_schema.brep_with_voids,brep_with_voids>>
* <<express:geometric_model_schema.faceted_brep,faceted_brep>>
* <<express:geometric_model_schema.faceted_brep,faceted_brep>> AND <<express:geometric_model_schema.brep_with_voids,brep_with_voids>>
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.outer"
a <<express:topology_schema.closed_shell,closed_shell>> defining the exterior boundary of the solid; the shell normal shall point away from the interior of the solid
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.wr:IP1"
The dimensionality of a **manifold_solid_brep** shall be 3.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.wr:IP2"
The extent of the **manifold_solid_brep** shall be finite and non-zero.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.wr:IP3"
No <<express:topology_schema.vertex_point,vertex_point>>, undirected <<express:topology_schema.edge_curve,edge_curve>> (i.e., one which is not an <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>> ), or undirected <<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>> (i.e., one which is not an <<express:topology_schema.oriented_face,oriented_face>> ) referenced by a **manifold_solid_brep** shall intersect any other <<express:topology_schema.vertex_point,vertex_point>>, undirected <<express:topology_schema.edge_curve,edge_curve>>, or undirected <<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>> referenced by the same **manifold_solid_brep**.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.wr:IP4"
// Distinct

// <express_ref linkend="topology_schema:ir_express:topology_schema.loop"/>

// s referenced by the same

// <express_ref linkend="topology_schema:ir_express:topology_schema.face"/>

// shall have no common

// <express_ref linkend="topology_schema:ir_express:topology_schema.vertex"/>

No
// tessellated_vertex_point
<<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_vertex_point,tessellated_vertex_point>>, undirected
// tessellated_edge_curve
<<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge_curve,tessellated_edge_curve>> (i.e., one which is not an
// oriented_edge
<<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>>), or undirected
// tessellated_face_surface
<<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face_surface,tessellated_face_surface>> (i.e., one which is not an
// oriented_face
<<express:topology_schema.oriented_face,oriented_face>>) referenced by a **manifold_solid_brep** shall intersect any other
// tessellated_vertex_point
<<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_vertex_point,tessellated_vertex_point>>, undirected
// tessellated_edge_curve
<<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge_curve,tessellated_edge_curve>> , or undirected
// tessellated_face_surface
<<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face_surface,tessellated_face_surface>> referenced by the same **manifold_solid_brep**.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.wr:IP4.__note"
This implies that distinct loops of the same face have no common edges. If geometry is present, distinct loops of the same face do not intersect.
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.wr:IP5"
All topological elements of the **manifold_solid_brep** shall have defined associated geometry.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.wr:IP6"
The shell normals shall agree with the B-rep normal and point away from the solid represented by the B-rep.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.wr:IP7"
Each face shall be referenced only once by the shells of the **manifold_solid_brep**.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.wr:IP8"
Each <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>> in the **manifold_solid_brep** shall be referenced only once.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.wr:IP9"
Each undirected edge shall be referenced exactly twice by the loops in the faces of the **manifold_solid_brep**'s shells.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.wr:IP10"
The Euler equation shall be satisfied for the boundary representation, where the genus term shell-genus is the sum of the genus values for the shells of the B-rep.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.wr:IP11"
A **manifold_solid_brep**, which is not a <<express:geometric_model_schema.faceted_brep,faceted_brep>>, shall not reference <<express:topology_schema.poly_loop,poly_loop>> instances.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep.wr:IP12"
A <<express:geometric_model_schema.faceted_brep,faceted_brep>> can reference only <<express:topology_schema.poly_loop,poly_loop>> instances as face boundaries.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.brep_with_voids"
A **brep_with_voids** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep,manifold_solid_brep>> which contains one or more voids in its interior. The voids are represented by <<express:topology_schema.oriented_closed_shell,oriented_closed_shell>> instances which are defined so that the <<express:topology_schema.oriented_closed_shell,oriented_closed_shell>> normals point into the void, that is, with <<express:topology_schema.oriented_closed_shell.orientation,orientation>> FALSE. A **brep_with_voids** can also be a <<express:geometric_model_schema.faceted_brep,faceted_brep>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.brep_with_voids.voids"
a set of <<express:topology_schema.oriented_closed_shell,oriented_closed_shell>> instances defining voids within the solid. The set may contain one or more shells.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.brep_with_voids.wr:IP1"
Each void shell shall be disjoint from the outer shell and from every other void shell.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.brep_with_voids.wr:IP2"
Each void shell shall be enclosed within the outer shell but not within any other void shell. In particular, the outer shell is not in the set of void shells.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.brep_with_voids.wr:IP3"
Each shell in the **brep_with_voids** shall be referenced only once.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.faceted_brep"
A **faceted_brep** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep,manifold_solid_brep>> which is a simple form of boundary representation model in which all faces are planar and all edges are straight lines.

Unlike the B-rep model, edges and vertices are not represented explicitly in the model but are implicitly available through the <<express:topology_schema.poly_loop,poly_loop>> entity. A **faceted_brep** has to meet the same topological constraints as the <<express:geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep,manifold_solid_brep>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.faceted_brep.__note"
The *faceted_brep* has been introduced in order to support the large number of systems that allow boundary type solid representations with planar surfaces only. Faceted models may be represented by <<express:geometric_model_schema.manifold_solid_brep,manifold_solid_brep>> but their representation as a *faceted_brep* will be more compact.
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.faceted_brep.wr:IP1"
All the bounding loops of all the faces of all the shells in the **faceted_brep** shall be of type <<express:topology_schema.poly_loop,poly_loop>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.faceted_brep.wr:IP2"
The faces in the shells may have implicit or explicit surface geometry. If explicit, the face surface shall be a plane. All polyloops defining the face shall be coplanar.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.brep_2d"
A **brep_2d** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.solid_model,solid_model>> which is a bounded two-dimensional region defined by a face. Any two-dimensional point can be classified as being inside, outside or on the boundary of a **brep_2d**. A **brep_2d** shall have an outer boundary and may have any number of holes.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.brep_2d.extent"
the face which defines the region of two-dimensional space occupied by the **brep_2d** ;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.brep_2d.wr:WR1"
**extent** shall not be a <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> of type <<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>>, <<express:topology_schema.subface,subface>>, or
// oriented_face
<<express:topology_schema.oriented_face,oriented_face>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.brep_2d.wr:WR2"
Each <<express:topology_schema.face_bound,face_bound>> used to define the **extent** shall be of type <<express:topology_schema.edge_loop,edge_loop>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.brep_2d.wr:WR3"
Precisely one of the bounds of the <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> shall be of type <<express:topology_schema.face_outer_bound,face_outer_bound>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.brep_2d.wr:WR4"
Each <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> used to define the bounds shall be of type <<express:topology_schema.edge_curve,edge_curve>> and shall be two-dimensional.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.csg_solid"
A **csg_solid** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.solid_model,solid_model>> which is a solid represented as a CSG model defined by a collection of so-called primitive solids, combined using regularised boolean operations. The allowed operations are intersection, union and difference. As a special case a **csg_solid** can also consist of a single CSG primitive.

A regularised subset of space is the closure of its interior, where this phrase is interpreted in the usual sense of point set topology. For <<express:geometric_model_schema.boolean_result,boolean_result>> instances regularisation has the effect of removing dangling edges and other anomalies produced by the original operations.

A CSG solid requires two kinds of information for its complete definition: geometric and structural. The geometric information is conveyed by <<express:geometric_model_schema.solid_model,solid_model>> instances. These typically are primitive volumes such as cylinders, wedges and extrusions, but can include general B-rep models. <<express:geometric_model_schema.solid_model,solid_model>> instances can also be <<express:geometric_model_schema.solid_replica,solid_replica>> instances (transformed solids) and <<express:geometric_model_schema.half_space_solid,half_space_solid>> instances. The structural information is in a tree (strictly, an acyclic directed graph) of <<express:geometric_model_schema.boolean_result,boolean_result>> and CSG solids, which represent a `recipe' for building the solid. The terminal nodes are the geometric primitives and other solids. Every **csg_solid** has precisely one <<express:geometric_model_schema.boolean_result,boolean_result>> associated with it which is the root of the tree that defines the solid. (There may be further <<express:geometric_model_schema.boolean_result,boolean_result>> instances within the tree as operands). The significance of a **csg_solid** entity is that the solid defined by the associated tree is thus identified as a significant object in itself, and in this way it is distinguished from other <<express:geometric_model_schema.boolean_result,boolean_result>> entities representing intermediate results during the construction process.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.csg_solid.tree_root_expression"
a boolean expression of primitives and regularised operators describing the solid; the root of the tree of boolean expressions is given here explicitly as a <<express:geometric_model_schema.boolean_result,boolean_result>> entity, or as a <<express:geometric_model_schema.csg_primitive,csg_primitive>>;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.boolean_result"
A **boolean_result** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>> which is the result of a regularised operation on two solids to create a new solid. Valid operations are regularised union, regularised intersection, and regularised difference. For purposes of Boolean operations, a solid is considered to be a regularised set of points. The final **boolean_result** depends upon the operation and the two operands. In the case of the difference operator the order of the operands is also significant. The operator can be either union, intersection or difference. The effect of these operators is described below.

_union_ on two solids is the new solid that contains all the points that are in either the **first_operand** or the **second_operand** or both.

_intersection_ on two solids is the new solid that is the regularisation of the set of all points that are in both the **first_operand** and the **second_operand**.

The result of the _difference_ operation on two solids is the regularisation of the set of all points which are in the **first_operand**, but not in the **second_operand**.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.boolean_result.__note"
For example if the first operand is a block and the second operand is a solid cylinder of suitable dimensions and location the *boolean_result* produced with the difference operator would be a block with a circular hole.
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.boolean_result.operator"
the boolean operator used in the operation to create the result;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.boolean_result.first_operand"
the first operand to be operated upon by the boolean operation;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.boolean_result.second_operand"
the second operand to be operated upon by the boolean operation.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.block"
A **block** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>> which is a solid rectangular parallelepiped, defined with a locationand placement coordinate system. The **block** is specified by the positive lengths **x**, **y**, and **z** along the axes of the placement coordinate system, and has one vertex at the origin of the placement coordinate system.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.block.position"
the location and orientation of the axis system for the primitive; the block has one vertex at position.location and its edges aligned with the placement axes in the positive sense;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.block.x"
the size of the block along the placement X axis, (position.p[1]);
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.block.y"
the size of the block along the placement Y axis, (position.p[21]);
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.block.z"
the size of the block along the placement Z axis, (position.p[3]);
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.right_angular_wedge"
A **right_angular_wedge** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>> which can be envisioned as the result of intersecting a block with a plane perpendicular to one of its faces. It is defined with a location and local coordinate system. A triangular/trapezoidal face lies in the plane defined by the placement X and Y axes. This face is defined by positive lengths **x** and **y** along the placement X and Y axes, by the length **ltx** (if nonzero) parallel to the X axis at a distance **y** from the placement origin, and by the line connecting the ends of the **x** and **ltx** segments. The remainder of the wedge is specified by the positive length **z** along the placement Z axis which defines a distance through which the trapezoid or triangle is extruded. If **ltx** = 0, the wedge has five faces; otherwise, it has six faces.
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.right_angular_wedge.__figure"
[[figure-geometric_model_schema-GMfig24]]
.Right angular wedge and its attributes
====
image::GMfig24.gif[]
====
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.right_angular_wedge.__note"
See <<figure-geometric_model_schema-GMfig24>> for interpretation of attributes.
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.right_angular_wedge.position"
the location and orientation of the axis system for the primitive; the **right_angular_wedge** has one vertex at position.location and its edges aligned with the placement axes in the positive sense;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.right_angular_wedge.x"
the size of the **right_angular_wedge** along the placement X axis, (position.p[1]);
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.right_angular_wedge.y"
the size of the wedge along the placement Y axis, (position.p[21]);
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.right_angular_wedge.z"
the size of the wedge along the placement Z axis, (position.p[3]);
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.right_angular_wedge.ltx"
the length in the positive X direction of the smaller surface of the wedge;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.right_angular_wedge.wr:WR1"
**ltx** shall be non-negative and less than **x**.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.rectangular_pyramid"
A **rectangular_pyramid** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>> which is a solid pyramid with a rectangular base. The apex of the pyramid is directly above the centre point of the base. The **rectangular_pyramid** is specified by its position, which provides a placement coordinate system, its length, depth and height.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.rectangular_pyramid.position"

(*"geometric_model_schema.right_circular_cone"

(*"geometric_model_schema.right_circular_cone.height"

(*"geometric_model_schema.surface_curve_swept_face_solid"

// swept_face

// swept_face

// swept_face

The two trimming values for The two trimming values for stem:[u] shall be distinct.shall be distinct.
*)

*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.shell_based_surface_model"
A **shell_based_surface_model** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>> which is described by a set of open or closed shells of dimensionality 2. The shells shall not intersect except at edges and vertices. In particular, distinct faces shall not intersect. A complete face of one shell may be shared with another shell. Coincident portions of shells shall both reference the same faces, edges and vertices defining the coincident region.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.shell_based_surface_model.__note"
A <<express:topology_schema.shell,shell>> may exist independently of a *shell_based_surface_model*.

the set of <<express:topology_schema.shell,shell>> instances which define the **shell_based_surface_model**
*)

*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.shell_based_surface_model.wr:IP1"
The topological dimensionality of the **shell_based_surface_model** is 2.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.shell_based_surface_model.wr:IP2"
The <<express:topology_schema.shell,shell>> instances shall not overlap or intersect except at common <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> instances, <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> instances, or <<express:topology_schema.vertex,vertex>> instances.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.shell_based_surface_model.wr:IP3"

*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.face_based_surface_model"
A **face_based_surface_model** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>> which is described by a set of <<express:topology_schema.connected_face_set,connected_face_set>> instances of dimensionality 2. The <<express:topology_schema.connected_face_set,connected_face_set>> instances shall not intersect except at edges and vertices, except that a <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> in one connected face set may overlap a <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> in another connected face set, provided the face boundaries are identical. There shall be at least one <<express:topology_schema.connected_face_set,connected_face_set>>. A <<express:topology_schema.connected_face_set,connected_face_set>> may exist independently of a **face_based_surface_model**.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.face_based_surface_model.fbsm_faces"
the set of <<express:topology_schema.connected_face_set,connected_face_set>> instances which define the **face_based_surface_model** ;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.face_based_surface_model.wr:IP1"
The <<express:topology_schema.connected_face_set,connected_face_set>> instances shall not overlap or intersect except at common <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> instances, <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> instances or <<express:topology_schema.vertex,vertex>> instances.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.face_based_surface_model.wr:IP2"
The topological dimensionality of the **fbsm_faces** is 2.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.shell_based_wireframe_model"
A **shell_based_wireframe_model** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>> which is described by a graph of edges and vertices embedded in stem:[RR^3]. The graph may be disconnected. Within the graph the edges do not intersect except at their boundaries (i.e., vertices). The geometry associated with a vertex shall be consistent with the geometry associated with any of the edges of which the vertex forms a boundary. A **shell_based_wireframe_model** is represented by one or more <<express:topology_schema.shell,shell>> instances of dimensionality 0 or 1. There shall be at least one <<express:topology_schema.shell,shell>>. A <<express:topology_schema.shell,shell>> may exist independently of a **shell_based_wireframe_model**.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.shell_based_wireframe_model.sbwm_boundary"
the set of <<express:topology_schema.vertex_shell,vertex_shell>> instances and/or <<express:topology_schema.wire_shell,wire_shell>> instances which define the **shell_based_wireframe_model** ;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.shell_based_wireframe_model.wr:WR1"
Each <<express:topology_schema.shell,shell>> shall be either of type <<express:topology_schema.vertex_shell,vertex_shell>> or <<express:topology_schema.wire_shell,wire_shell>>. The function <<express:geometric_model_schema.constraints_geometry_shell_based_wireframe_model,constraints_geometry_shell_based_wireframe_model>> returns TRUE, where the function evaluates these geometric constraints and finds them satisfied.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.shell_based_wireframe_model.wr:IP1"
The topological dimensionality of **sbwm_boundary** is less than 2.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.shell_based_wireframe_model.wr:IP2"
The **shell_based_wireframe_model** has positive and finite extent.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.shell_based_wireframe_model.wr:IP3"
The <<express:topology_schema.shell,shell>> instances shall not overlap or intersect except at common <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> instances or <<express:topology_schema.vertex,vertex>> instances.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.edge_based_wireframe_model"
An **edge_based_wireframe_model** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>> which is described by a graph of edges and vertices embedded in stem:[RR^3]. The graph may be disconnected. Within the graph the edges do not intersect except at their boundaries (i.e., vertices). The geometry associated with a vertex shall be consistent with the geometry associated with any of the edges of which the vertex forms a boundary. An **edge_based_wireframe_model** is represented by one or more <<express:topology_schema.connected_edge_set,connected_edge_set>> instances of dimensionality 1. There shall be at least one <<express:topology_schema.connected_edge_set,connected_edge_set>>. A <<express:topology_schema.connected_edge_set,connected_edge_set>> may exist independently of an **edge_based_wireframe_model**.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.edge_based_wireframe_model.ebwm_boundary"
the set of <<express:topology_schema.connected_edge_set,connected_edge_set>> instances comprising the **edge_based_wireframe_model** ;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.edge_based_wireframe_model.wr:IP1"
The dimensionality of **edge_based_wireframe_model** is 1.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.edge_based_wireframe_model.wr:IP2"
The <<express:topology_schema.connected_edge_set,connected_edge_set>> instances shall not overlap or intersect except at common <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> instances or <<express:topology_schema.vertex,vertex>> instances.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.geometric_set"
A **geometric_set** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>> which is intended for the transfer of models when a topological structure is not available.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.geometric_set.elements"
the geometric elements which make up the **geometric_set**, these may be <<express:geometry_schema.point,point>> instances, <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>> instances or <<express:geometry_schema.surface,surface>> instances; but are required to be of the same coordinate space dimensionality;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.geometric_curve_set"
A **geometric_curve_set** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.geometric_set,geometric_set>> which is a collection of two-dimensional or three-dimensional <<express:geometry_schema.point,point>> instances and <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>> instances.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.geometric_curve_set.wr:WR1"
Only curves and points shall be included in a **geometric_curve_set**.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.sectioned_spine"
An **sectioned_spine** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.geometric_curve_set,geometric_curve_set>> which is a representation of the shape of a three dimensional object composed of a spine curve and a number of planar **cross_sections**. The shape is defined between the first element of **cross_sections** and the last element of this set.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.sectioned_spine.__note"
A *sectioned_spine* may be used to represent a surface or a solid but the interpolation of the shape between the cross-sections is not defined. For the representation of a solid all cross-sections are closed curves.
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.sectioned_spine.cross_sections"
the set of 2 or more planar cross-sections; each cross-section is defined in its correct location relative to the spine curve;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.sectioned_spine.spine_points"
the set of <<express:geometry_schema.point,point>> instances on the spine, each point lies in the plane of the corresponding cross-section;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.sectioned_spine.wr:WR1"
The <<express:geometric_model_schema.geometric_set.elements,elements>> set shall contain a single item.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.sectioned_spine.wr:WR2"
The <<express:geometric_model_schema.geometric_set.elements,elements>> set shall contain a single item.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.sectioned_spine.wr:WR3"
The set of **cross_sections** and the set of **spine_points** shall be of the same size.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.sectioned_spine.wr:WR4"
The space dimensionality of the **sectioned_spine** shall be 3.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.sectioned_spine.wr:IP1"
Each curve in the **cross_sections** set shall be a planar curve.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.sectioned_spine.wr:IP2"
Each point in the **spine_points** set shall lie in the plane of the corresponding curve from the **cross_sections**.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.geometric_set_replica"
An **geometric_set_replica** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.geometric_set,geometric_set>> which defines a replica of a <<express:geometric_model_schema.geometric_set,geometric_set>> in a different location. (*"geometric_model_schema.geometric_set_replica.parent_set"

*)

a Cartesian transformation operator which defines the location and orientation of the **geometric_set_replica** ;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.geometric_set_replica.elements"
the set of elements resulting from the transformation of the **parent_set** ;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.geometric_set_replica.wr:WR1"
A **geometric_set_replica** shall not participate in its own definition.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_shape_representation"

The context of the **tessellated_shape_representation** shall be a <<express:measure_schema.global_unit_assigned_context,global_unit_assigned_context>>. This ensures that the coordinates used to define the points of the tessellated geometry have defined units.

(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_shape_representation.wr:WR2"

*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_shape_representation_with_accuracy_parameters"
A **tessellated_shape_representation_with_accuracy_parameters** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_shape_representation,tessellated_shape_representation>> which has additional parameters to define the accuracy of the tessellated approximation to the corresponding exact geometric shape.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_shape_representation_with_accuracy_parameters.tessellation_accuracy_parameters"
the set of parameters defining the accuracy of the <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_shape_representation_with_accuracy_parameters,tessellated_shape_representation_with_accuracy_parameters>>.

(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_item"
A **tessellated_item** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>> used in the description of a tessellated shape.

(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_item.wr:WR1"

(*"geometric_model_schema.repositioned_tessellated_item"
A **repositioned_tessellated_item** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_item,tessellated_item>> which has been re-postioned by defining the coordinates with respect to a new axis system.

(*"geometric_model_schema.repositioned_tessellated_item.location"
an <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d,axis2_placement_3d>> defining the origin and axis direction for the coordinates of the referenced points in the **repositioned_tessellated_item** ;

(*"geometric_model_schema.repositioned_tessellated_item.wr:WR1"

<<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_curve_set,tessellated_curve_set>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_geometric_set,tessellated_geometric_set>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_point_set,tessellated_point_set>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_surface_set,tessellated_surface_set>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_shell,tessellated_shell>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_solid,tessellated_solid>>, <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_wire,tessellated_wire>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_structured_item"
A **tessellated_structured_item** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.geometric_set,geometric_set>> which has a topological structure. The links to topological components of an exact geometric model are defined with the subtypes.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.coordinates_list"
A **coordinates_list** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_item,tessellated_item>> that defines the coordinate values for points used in a <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_shape_representation,tessellated_shape_representation>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.coordinates_list.npoints"
the number of points with coordinates in the list;
*)

the list of real triples defining the coordinates of the points;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.coordinates_list.position_coords.__note"
These real triples have the semantics of <<express:measure_schema.length_measure,length_measure>> instances, but are not formally defined as such, the units for these are defined since a <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_item,tessellated_item>> is required to be used in a <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_shape_representation,tessellated_shape_representation>> having a <<express:measure_schema.global_unit_assigned_context,global_unit_assigned_context>>.

(*"geometric_model_schema.coordinates_list.wr:WR1"
The value of **npoints** shall be equal to the size of the **position_coords** list.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.coordinates_list.wr:WR2"

(*"geometric_model_schema.coordinates_list.wr:WR2.__note"
This rule together with the ONEOF rule on the supertype <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_item,tessellated_item>> ensures that it is not instantiated with any subtype of <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_item,tessellated_item>>.
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_vertex"
A **tessellated_vertex** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_structured_item,tessellated_structured_item>> and is a single vertex in a tessellated model.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_vertex.coordinates"
the <<express:geometric_model_schema.coordinates_list,coordinates_list>> giving the vertex coordinate values;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_vertex.topological_link"
an optional link to a topological <<express:topology_schema.vertex_point,vertex_point>> entity;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_vertex.point_index"
the location in the **coordinates** list of the coordinates for this vertex;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge"
A **tessellated_edge** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_structured_item,tessellated_structured_item>>. The geometry of the **tessellated_edge** is approximated by straight line segments joining the points listed.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge.__note"
A *tessellated_edge* may be used as the boundary between two <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face,tessellated_face>> instances.
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge.coordinates"
the <<express:geometric_model_schema.coordinates_list,coordinates_list>> giving the coordinate values for points of the **tessellated_edge**
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge.geometric_link"
the <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> or <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>> of an exact model to which this **tessellated_edge** corresponds;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge.line_strip"
the list of integers giving the locations in the **coordinates** list of consecutive points of this edge;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_connecting_edge"
A **tessellated_connecting_edge** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge,tessellated_edge>>. The **tessellated_connecting_edge** connects two faces and contains information relating to the face normals at corresponding points on the 2 faces.

(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_connecting_edge.smooth"
a LOGICAL variable; if TRUE, there is tangent continuity where two faces join along this edge
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_connecting_edge.face1"
the first <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face,tessellated_face>> using this edge;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_connecting_edge.face2"
the second <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face,tessellated_face>> using this edge;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_connecting_edge.line_strip_face1"
the list of integers giving the locations in the normals list of **face1** of the normals on the **face1** side at consecutive points of this edge, and, for connection checking, if required, the locations in the **face1** coordinates list or **face1** pnindex of consecutive points of this edge; in cases where normals are not defined for **face1** the locations in the coordinates list are given;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_connecting_edge.line_strip_face2"
the list of integers giving the locations in the normals list of **face2** of the normals on the **face2** side at consecutive points of this edge, and, for connection checking, if required, the locations in the **face2** coordinates list or **face2** pnindex of consecutive points of this edge; in cases where normals are not defined for **face2** the locations in the coordinates list are given.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_connecting_edge.wr:WR1"
**line_strip_face1** and **line_strip_face2** shall be of the same size.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_connecting_edge.wr:WR2"
**line_strip_face1** shall be of the same size as the inherited <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge.line_strip,line_strip>> attribute.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_connecting_edge.wr:WR3"
**face1** shall not be of type <<express:geometric_model_schema.cubic_bezier_triangulated_face,cubic_bezier_triangulated_face>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_connecting_edge.wr:WR4"
**face2** shall not be of type <<express:geometric_model_schema.cubic_bezier_triangulated_face,cubic_bezier_triangulated_face>>.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.cubic_bezier_tessellated_edge"
A **cubic_bezier_tessellated_edge** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge,tessellated_edge>> which takes the form of a piecewise cubic bezier curve. The **cubic_bezier_tessellated_edge** has its geometry defined by a list of control points, referenced by the inherited <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge.line_strip,line_strip>> attribute; in this list only the points corresponding to ends of segments lie on the edge and the list of pointers is of length 3n +1, where n is the number of segments.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.cubic_bezier_tessellated_edge.line_strip"
the list of 3n + 1 integers, where n is the number of cubic segments, giving the locations in the <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge.coordinates,coordinates>> list of consecutive control points points of this edge.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.cubic_tessellated_connecting_edge"
A **cubic_tessellated_connecting_edge** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.cubic_bezier_tessellated_edge,cubic_bezier_tessellated_edge>> which takes the form of a cubic curve and connects two <<express:geometric_model_schema.cubic_bezier_triangulated_face,cubic_bezier_triangulated_face>> instances. The **cubic_tessellated_connecting_edge** has its geometry defined by a list of control points contained in the inherited <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_edge.line_strip,line_strip>> attribute; in this list only the points corresponding to vertices of the cubic triangles of the adjacent faces lie on the edge and the list of pointers is of length 3n +1, where n is the number of triangles with adjacent edges on each side of the connecting edge.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.cubic_tessellated_connecting_edge.smooth"
a LOGICAL variable; if TRUE, there is tangent continuity where two faces join along this edge;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.cubic_tessellated_connecting_edge.face1"
the <<express:geometric_model_schema.cubic_bezier_triangulated_face,cubic_bezier_triangulated_face>> to the left of this edge;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.cubic_tessellated_connecting_edge.face2"
the <<express:geometric_model_schema.cubic_bezier_triangulated_face,cubic_bezier_triangulated_face>> to the right of this edge.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face"
A **tessellated_face** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_structured_item,tessellated_structured_item>> that represents a face of a tessellated model.
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face.coordinates"
the <<express:geometric_model_schema.coordinates_list,coordinates_list>> giving the coordinate values for points of the **tessellated_face**
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face.pnmax"
the larger of the number of points defined with the face or the number of unique point and normal combinations in the face;

(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face.normals"
the list of REAL triples defining the normals at the points of the face. If the size of this list is greater than one the ordering of the normals is the same as the ordering used for the points via <<express:geometric_model_schema.triangulated_face.pnindex,pnindex>> in one of the subtypes.

(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face.geometric_link"
the <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> or <<express:geometry_schema.surface,surface>> of an exact model to which this **tessellated_face** corresponds;
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face.wr:WR1"
The size of **normals** shall be 0, 1 or equal to **pnmax**.

(*"geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face.wr:WR1.__note"
If size = 0 normals are undefined at all face points, if size = 1 the normal has the same value at each face point and the underlying surface is planar, if size is greater than 1 each point on the face has an individual underlying surface normal defined.

(*"geometric_model_schema.triangulated_face"
A **triangulated_face** is a type of <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face,tessellated_face>> that has its geometry defined by a set of triangles.

====
image::GMfig28.gif[]
====
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.triangulated_face.pnindex"
the list of integers defining the locations in the <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face.coordinates,coordinates>> list of the points and normals of the triangles of the face
*)


(*"geometric_model_schema.triangulated_face.triangles"
the list of INTEGER triples, in the range 1 to pnmax, giving the locations of the coordinate values in the <<express:geometric_model_schema.tessellated_face.coordinates,coordinates>> list or in **pnindex** for each triangle. *)


(*"geometric_model_schema.triangulated_face.triangles.__note"
See <<figure-geometric_model_schema-GMfig28>> for further details of use of pnindex.

(*"geometry_schema"
// Note schema EXPRESS are in ..\resources\resource_name name_of_schema.xml

The subject of the *geometry_schema* is the geometry of parametric curves and surfaces. The *representation_schema* (see ISO 10303-43) and the *geometric_representation_context* defined in this document, provide the context in which the geometry is defined. The *geometric_representation_context* enables a distinction to be made between those items which are in the same context, and thus geometrically related, and those existing in independent coordinate spaces. In particular, each *geometric_representation_item* has a *geometric_representation_context* which includes as an attribute the Euclidean dimension of its coordinate space. The coordinate system for this space is referred to as the geometric coordinate system in this clause. Units associated with **length_measure**s and **plane_angle_measure**s are assumed to be assigned globally within this context. A global rule ({blank}*compatible_dimension*{blank}) ensures that all **geometric_representation_item**s in the same *geometric_representation_context* have the same space dimensionality. The space dimensionality *dim* is a derived attribute of all subtypes of *geometric_representation_item*.

*)
(*"geometry_schema.__fund_cons"

[[sec_4.2.1]]
==== Space Dimensionality

All geometry shall be defined in a right-handed rectangular Cartesian coordinate system with the same units on each axis. A common scheme has been used for the definition of both two-dimensional and three-dimensional geometry. Points and directions exist in both a two-dimensional and a three-dimensional form; these forms are distinguished solely by the presence, or absence, of a third coordinate value. Complex geometric entities are all defined using points and directions from which their space dimensionality can be deduced.

[[sec_4.2.2]]
==== Geometric relationships

All **geometric_representation_item**s which are included as *items* in a *representation* having a *geometric_representation_context* are geometrically related. Any such *geometric_representation_item* is said to be geometrically founded in the context of that *representation*. No geometric relationship, such as distance between points, is assumed to exist for **geometric_representation_item**s occurring as *items* in different **representation**s.

[[sec_4.2.3]]
==== Parametrisation of analytic curves and surfaces

Each curve or surface specified here has a defined parametrisation. In some instances the definitions are in parametric terms. In others, the conic curves and elementary surfaces, the definitions are in geometric terms. In this latter case a placement coordinate system is used to define the parametrisation. The geometric definitions contain some, but not all, of the data required for this. The relevant data to define this placement coordinate system is contained in the *axis2_placement* associated with the individual curve and surface entities. Where the curve or surface parameterisation uses trigonometric functions, the parameter for the function behaves like an angle and can be considered to be an angular parameter. Numerical values for such angular parameters shall use the current units for *plane_angle_measure*.

[[sec_4.2.4]]
==== Curves

The curve entities defined in this schema include lines, elementary conics, a general parametric polynominal curve, and some referentially or procedurally defined curves. All the curves have a well defined parametrisation which makes it possible to trim a curve or identify points on the curve by parameter value. The geometric direction of a curve is the direction of increasing parameter value. For the conic curves, a method of representation is used which separates their geometric form from their orientation and position in space. In each case, the position and orientation information is conveyed by an *axis2_placement*. The general purpose parametric curve is represented by the *b_spline_curve* entity. This was selected as the most stable form of representation for the communication of all types of polynomial and rational parametric curves. With appropriate attribute values and subtypes, a *b_spline_curve* entity is capable of representing single span or spline curves of explicit polynomial, rational, Bézier or B-spline type. A *composite_curve* entity, which includes the facility to communicate continuity information at the curve-to-curve transition points, is provided for the construction of more complex curves.

The *offset_curve* and *curve_on_surface* types are curves defined with reference to other geometry. Separate offset_curve entities exist for 2D and 3D applications. The curve on surface entities include an *intersection_curve* which represents the intersection of two surfaces. Such a curve may be represented in 3D space or in the 2D parameter space of either of the surfaces.

[[sec_4.2.5]]
==== Surfaces

The surface entities support the requirements of simple boundary representation (B-rep) solid modelling system and enable the communication of general polynomial and rational parametric surfaces. The simple surfaces are the planar, spherical, cylindrical, conical and toroidal surfaces, a *surface_of_revolution* and a *surface_of_linear_extrusion*. As with curves, all surfaces have an associated standard parametrisation. In many cases the surfaces, as defined, are unbounded; it is assumed that they will be bounded either explicitly or implicitly. Explicit bounding is achieved with the *rectangular_trimmed_surface* or *curve_bounded_surface* entities; implicit bounding requires the association of additional topological information to define a *face*.

The *b_spline_surface* entity and its subtypes provide the most general capability for the communication of all types of polynomial and rational biparametric surfaces. This entity uses control points as the most stable form of representation for the surface geometry. The *offset_surface* entity is intended for the communication of a surface obtained as a simple normal offset from a given surface. The *rectangular_composite_surface* entity provides the basic capability to connect together a rectangular mesh of distinct surface patches, specifying the degree of continuity from patch to patch.

[[sec_4.2.6]]
==== Preferred form

Some of the geometric entities provide the potential capability of defining an item of geometry in more than one way. Such multiple representations are accommodated by requiring the nomination of a `preferred form' or `master representation'. This is the form which is used to determine the parametrisation.

[NOTE]
--
The *master_representation* attribute acknowledges the impracticality of ensuring that multiple forms are indeed identical and allows the indication of a preferred form. This would probably be determined by the creator of the data. All characteristics, such as parametrisation, domain, and results of evaluation, for an entity having multiple representations, are derived from the master representation. Any use of the other representations is a compromise for practical considerations.
--

(*"geometric_model_schema.non_manifold_surface_shape_representation"
A **non_manifold_surface_shape_representation** is a type of
// shape_representation
<<express:product_property_representation_schema.shape_representation,shape_representation>> that describes the shape or portions of the shape of a product using non-manifolds with boundaries.

A **non_manifold_surface_shape_representation** is a
// shape_representation
<<express:product_property_representation_schema.shape_representation,shape_representation>> that consists of one or many
// face_based_surface_models
<<express:geometric_model_schema.face_based_surface_model,face_based_surface_model>> instances. Each
// face_based_surface_model
<<express:geometric_model_schema.face_based_surface_model,face_based_surface_model>> is built up of
// connected_face_sets
<<express:topology_schema.connected_face_set,connected_face_set>> instances, which in the context of this document may be instantiated as a
// connected_face_set
<<express:topology_schema.connected_face_set,connected_face_set>> or as one of its subtypes
// open_shells
<<express:topology_schema.open_shell,open_shell>> or
// closed_shell
<<express:topology_schema.closed_shell,closed_shell>>.
// connected_face_sets
All <<express:topology_schema.connected_face_set,connected_face_set>> instaces consist of
// faces
<<express:topology_schema.face,face>> instances which use
// edges
<<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> instances and
// vertexs
<<express:topology_schema.vertex,vertex>> instances; the latter three shall reference geometric entities, such as
// points
<<express:geometry_schema.point,point>> instances,
// curves
<<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>> instances, and
// surfaces
<<express:geometry_schema.surface,surface>> instances. The link between topology and geometry may be established by either using
// face_surface
<<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>> or
// advanced_face
<<express:topology_schema.advanced_face,advanced_face>>. The two options differ both in the selection of valid
// point
<<express:geometry_schema.point,point>>,
// curve
<<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>>, and
// surface
<<express:geometry_schema.surface,surface>> subtypes and in constraints on references to underlying geometry.

All geometric entities shall be of dimensionality three except for two-dimensional geometry that is used for the purpose of defining
// pcurve
<<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>> instances. The use of one-dimensional
// cartesian_point
<<express:geometry_schema.cartesian_point,cartesian_point>> instances is excluded.

All unbounded geometry shall be trimmed by using topological constructs.

The
// items
<<express:representation_schema.representation.items,items>> of a **non_manifold_surface_shape_representation** may also be of type
// mapped_item
<<express:representation_schema.mapped_item,mapped_item>>, or
// axis2_placement_3d
<<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d,axis2_placement_3d>>. These are used to assemble one or several **non_manifold_surface_shape_representation** instances into one other **non_manifold_surface_shape_representation** instances.

In WR4, WR5 and WR9, these functions validate the
// curves
<<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>> instances and
// surface
<<express:geometry_schema.surface,surface>> instances of all
// edge
<<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> instances and
// faces
<<express:topology_schema.face,face>> instances that are in the scope of a **non_manifold_surface_shape_representation** except for those that are in the reference tree of an
// advanced_face
<<express:topology_schema.advanced_face,advanced_face>>; the geometry of an
// advanced_face
<<express:topology_schema.advanced_face,advanced_face>> is validated by a different set of rules. The functions automatically assess all underlying geometry; for this they are called recursively.
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.non_manifold_surface_shape_representation.__example"
A
// pcurve
<<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>> references both a
// curve
<<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>> and a
// surface
<<express:geometry_schema.surface,surface>>. The function
// nmsf_curve_check
<<express:geometric_model_schema.nmsf_curve_check,nmsf_curve_check>> validates not only the
// pcurve
<<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>>, but also the
// curve
<<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>> and the
// surface
<<express:geometry_schema.surface,surface>>. It will, therefore, not only call itself, but also
// nmsf_surface_check
<<express:geometric_model_schema.nmsf_surface_check,nmsf_surface_check>>.
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.non_manifold_surface_shape_representation.__note"
Non-manifolds are topologically less constrained than manifolds. For example, the restriction that only a maximum of two
// faces
<<express:topology_schema.face,face>> instances may share the same
// edge
<<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> instance does not apply. They are, therefore, not necessarily suitable for building solid models. They are, however, often found in applications that support the finite element analysis method.
*)

(*"geometric_model_schema.non_manifold_surface_shape_representation.__note"
A *non_manifold_surface_shape_representation* may well hold a manifold surface model, but not vice versa.

The representation of
// face_surfaces
<<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>> instances as
// advanced_faces
<<express:topology_schema.advanced_face,advanced_face>> instances is recommended for non-manifold surface models that are intended to be used together with boundary-representation solid models to reduce integration complexity.

ENTITY cartesian_point

                       polar_point,
                       spherical_point))

ENTITY cylindrical_point
  SUBTYPE OF (cartesian_point);
  r : length_measure;
  theta : plane_angle_measure;
  z : length_measure;
DERIVE
  SELF\cartesian_point.coordinates : LIST[3:3] OF length_measure := [r*cos(theta), r*sin(theta), z];
WHERE
  WR1: r >= 0.0;
  --IP1:
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY spherical_point
  SUBTYPE OF (cartesian_point);
  r : length_measure;
  theta : plane_angle_measure;
  phi : plane_angle_measure;
DERIVE
  SELF\cartesian_point.coordinates : LIST[3:3] OF length_measure := [r*sin(theta)*cos(phi), r*sin(theta)*sin(phi), r*cos(theta)];
WHERE
  WR1: r >= 0.0;
  --IP1:
  --IP2:
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY polar_point
  SUBTYPE OF (cartesian_point);
  r : length_measure;
  theta : plane_angle_measure;
DERIVE
  SELF\cartesian_point.coordinates : LIST[2:2] OF length_measure := [r*cos(theta), r*sin(theta)];

  WR1: r >= 0.0;
  --IP1:

ENTITY placement
  SUPERTYPE OF (ONEOF (axis1_placement,
                       axis2_placement_2d,
                       axis2_placement_3d))
  SUBTYPE OF (geometric_representation_item);
  location : cartesian_point;
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY axis1_placement
  SUBTYPE OF (placement);
  axis : OPTIONAL direction;
DERIVE
  z : direction := NVL(normalise(axis), dummy_gri || direction([0.0,0.0,1.0]));
WHERE
  WR1: SELF\geometric_representation_item.dim = 3;
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY axis2_placement_2d
  SUBTYPE OF (placement);
  ref_direction : OPTIONAL direction;
DERIVE
  p : LIST[2:2] OF direction := build_2axes(ref_direction);
WHERE
  WR1: SELF\geometric_representation_item.dim = 2;
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY axis2_placement_3d
  SUBTYPE OF (placement);
  axis : OPTIONAL direction;
  ref_direction : OPTIONAL direction;
DERIVE
  p : LIST[3:3] OF direction := build_axes(axis,ref_direction);
WHERE
  WR1: SELF\placement.location.dim = 3;
  WR2: (NOT (EXISTS (axis))) OR (axis.dim = 3);
  WR3: (NOT (EXISTS (ref_direction))) OR (ref_direction.dim = 3);
  WR4: (NOT (EXISTS (axis))) OR (NOT (EXISTS (ref_direction))) OR (cross_product(axis,ref_direction).magnitude > 0.0);
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY cartesian_transformation_operator
  SUPERTYPE OF (ONEOF (cartesian_transformation_operator_2d,
                       cartesian_transformation_operator_3d))
  SUBTYPE OF (geometric_representation_item, functionally_defined_transformation);
  axis1 : OPTIONAL direction;
  axis2 : OPTIONAL direction;
  local_origin : cartesian_point;
  scale : OPTIONAL REAL;
DERIVE
  scl : REAL := NVL(scale, 1.0);
WHERE
  WR1: scl > 0.0;
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY cartesian_transformation_operator_3d

  WR1: SELF\geometric_representation_item.dim = 3;

ENTITY cartesian_transformation_operator_2d

  WR1: SELF\geometric_representation_item.dim = 2;

  SUBTYPE OF (bounded_curve);

DERIVE

  control_points : ARRAY[0:upper_index_on_control_points] OF cartesian_point := list_to_array(control_points_list,0, upper_index_on_control_points);

  WR1: ('GEOMETRY_SCHEMA.UNIFORM_CURVE' IN TYPEOF(self)) OR ('GEOMETRY_SCHEMA.QUASI_UNIFORM_CURVE' IN TYPEOF(self)) OR ('GEOMETRY_SCHEMA.BEZIER_CURVE' IN TYPEOF(self)) OR ('GEOMETRY_SCHEMA.B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS' IN TYPEOF(self));

DERIVE
  upper_index_on_knots : INTEGER := SIZEOF(knots);
WHERE
  WR1: constraints_param_b_spline(SELF\b_spline_curve.degree, upper_index_on_knots, SELF\b_spline_curve.upper_index_on_control_points, knot_multiplicities, knots);

ENTITY composite_curve
  SUBTYPE OF (bounded_curve);

  self_intersect : LOGICAL;
DERIVE
  n_segments : INTEGER := SIZEOF(segments);
  closed_curve : LOGICAL := segments[n_segments].transition <> discontinuous;
WHERE
  WR1: ((NOT closed_curve) AND (SIZEOF(QUERY(temp <* segments | temp.transition = discontinuous)) = 1)) OR ((closed_curve) AND (SIZEOF(QUERY(temp <* segments | temp.transition = discontinuous)) = 0));

  SUPERTYPE OF (ONEOF (b_spline_surface_with_knots,

  SUBTYPE OF (bounded_surface);
