(*"geometry_schema.local_b_spline"
A **local_b_spline** is a type of <<express:representation_schema.representation_item,representation_item>> that is polynomial B-spline of degree d in one parameter defined over a list of knot values with associated multiplicities. The knot list is a list of distinct strictly increasing real values, the list of multiplicities defines the multiplicity of each knot. To ensure that all related **local_b_spline** functions refer to the same knot list the explicit knot list is defined with the entities, such as <<express:geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface,locally_refined_spline_surface>> , which use **local_b_spline** functions. Let stem:[m_j] denote the multiplicity (i.e. the number of repetitions) of the distinct knot number stem:[j] , and stem:[L] denote the size of the knot list. Then

.local_b_spline equation
[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sum_{i=1}^{L} m_i = d + k + 2
++++

[%key]
stem:[k]:: <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_curve.upper_index_on_control_points,upper index on control points>>;
stem:[d]:: <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_curve.degree,degree>>;

All knot multiplicities except the first and the last shall be in the range stem:[1,..., d]; the first and last may have a maximum value of stem:[d+1]. The continuity of local B-spline at knot stem:[j] in the current parameter direction is stem:[d"-"m _j].
*)

(*"geometry_schema.local_b_spline.wr:WR3"
The values of the knots and multiplicities shall be compatible with the degree and the continuity requirements for a B-spline function. The function <<express:geometry_schema.constraints_param_local_b_spline,constraints_param_local_b_spline>> applies the following tests:

the sum of knot multiplicities = degree + 2,

for the first and last knot the multiplicity is bounded by 1 and (degree+1),

the consecutive knots are increasing in value.

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_curve"
A **locally_refined_spline_curve** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_curve,bounded_curve>> that is a piecewise parametric polynomial or rational curve described in terms of control points and local B-spline functions. If the set of B-spline functions are linearly independent, they will form a basis. With appropriate attribute values, the curve is capable of representing single span or spline curves of explicit polynomial, rational, Bézier or B-spline type. Furthermore, the degree of the curve can vary as the B-splines from which it is defined, need not to have the same polynomial degree.

Interpretation of the data is as follows:

--
[%key]
stem:[K]:: <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_curve.upper_index_on_control_points,upper index on control points>>,
stem:[d_i]:: <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_curve.degree,degree>> of b-spline i,
stem:[bb P_{i}]:: <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_curve.control_points_list,control points>>,
stem:[s_{i}]:: <<express:geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_curve.scaling_factors,scaling factors>>,
stem:[N_{i}]:: <<express:geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_curve.b_splines,locally defined b-splines>>,
stem:[w_{i}]:: <<express:geometry_schema.rational_b_spline_curve.weights_data,weights>>.
--

The curve, in the polynomial case, is given by:
--
[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u) = sum_(i=1)^K ( P_i s_i N_i^(d_i)(u) )
++++
--

//prior representation:image::LRcurve.gif[]

In the rational case all weights shall be positive and the curve is given by:
--
[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u) = (
  sum_(i=1)^K (w_i P_i s_i N_i^(d_i)(u))
) / (
  sum_(i=1)^K (w_i s_i N_i^(d_i)(u))
)
++++
--

//prior representation:image::RationalLRcurve.gif[]

The knot values are defined in the <<express:geometry_schema.spline_knot_values,spline_knot_values>> type, and the knot multiplicity is defined in the entity <<express:geometry_schema.local_b_spline,local_b_spline>>.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_curve.__note"
A locally refined spline curve is rational if and only if the weights are not all identical; this can be represented by the <<express:geometry_schema.rational_locally_refined_spline_curve,rational_locally_refined_spline_curve>> subtype. If it is polynomial, the weights may be defaulted to all being 1.

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_curve.__note"
The degree is associated with the local B-spline and does not need to be constant throughout the curve.

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_curve.__note"
When the polynomial degree is the same for all B-splines and no knot lines exist that do not cross the entire parameter domain, the *locally_refined_spline_curve* will coincide with <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_curve_with_knots,b_spline_curve_with_knots>>. In that case <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_curve_with_knots,b_spline_curve_with_knots>> has the simplest and most compact representation.

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_curve.__note"
A *locally_refined_spline_curve* can be of type analysis suitable T-spline, hierarchical B-spline, LR-spline, semi standard T-spline or standard T-spline. The type is given by the enumeration <<express:geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_type_enum,locally_refined_spline_type_enum>>, and the packing and unpacking of the curve will depend on this type.

the local B-spline functions from which the curve is defined. If they are linearly independent, the set of B-splines will form a basis. The **b_splines** and consequently also the **control_points_list** and **scaling_factors**, are ordered according to the first knot in the local B-spline function. In case of ambiguities, the sorting factors are the last knot in the B-spline function and finally the multiplicity of the first knot.

the list of scaling factors, these factors are used to ensure that the non-zero B-splines at all points in the domain add up to unity (partition of unity). LR B-splines, hierarchical B-splines and some variants of T-splines ensure partition of unity by scaling. Other variants of T-splines use rational scaling.

the parameter domain corresponding to the curve. domain(1) is the minimum parameter value , domain(2) is the maximum parameter value. (*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve"
A **trimmed_curve** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_curve,bounded_curve>>, which is created by taking a selected portion, between two identified points, of the associated basis curve. The basis curve itself is unaltered and more than one trimmed curve may reference the same basis curve. Trimming points for the curve may be identified:

by parametric value;

by geometric position;

by both of the above.

At least one of these shall be specified at each end of the curve. The **sense** makes it possible to unambiguously define any segment of a closed curve such as a circle. The combinations of sense and ordered end points make it possible to define four distinct directed segments connecting two different points on a circle or other closed curve. For this purpose cyclic properties of the parameter range are assumed; for example, 370 degrees is equivalent to 10 degrees. The trimmed curve has a parametrisation which is inherited from that of the particular basis curve referenced. More precisely the parameter stem:[s] of the trimmed curve is derived from the parameter stem:[t] of the basis curve as follows:

If sense is TRUE: stem:[s = t - t_1].

If sense is FALSE: stem:[s = t_1 - t].

In the above equations stem:[t_1] is the value given by **trim_1** or the parameter value corresponding to **point_1** and stem:[t_2] is the parameter value given by **trim_2** or the parameter corresponding to **point_2**. The resultant trimmed curve has a parameter stem:[s] ranging from 0 at the first trimming point to stem:[|t_2 - t_1|] at the second trimming point.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.__note"
In the case of a closed basis curve, it may be necessary to increment stem:[1] or stem:[2] by the parametric length for consistency with the sense flag.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.__note"
For example:

. If *sense_agreement* = TRUE and stem:[t_2 < t_1, t_2] should be increased by the parametric length.

. If *sense_agreement* = FALSE and stem:[t_1 > t_2], stem:[t_1] should be increased by the parametric length.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.basis_curve"
the <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>> to be trimmed. For curves with multiple representations any parameter values given as **trim_1** or **trim_2** refer to the master representation of the **basis_curve** only;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.trim_1"
the first trimming point which may be specified as a <<express:geometry_schema.cartesian_point,cartesian_point>> (point_1), as a real parameter value (stem:["parameter"_1 = t_1]), or both;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.trim_2"
the second trimming point which may be specified as a <<express:geometry_schema.cartesian_point,cartesian_point>> (point_2), as a real parameter value (stem:["parameter"_2 = t_2]), or both;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.sense_agreement"
flag to indicate whether the direction of the trimmed curve agrees with or is opposed to the direction of **basis_curve**.

**sense_ agreement** = TRUE if the curve is being traversed in the direction of increasing parametric value;

**sense_agreement** = FALSE otherwise.

For an open curve, `sense_agreement = FALSE` if stem:[t_1 > t_2].

If stem:[t_2 > t_1], `sense_agreement = TRUE`.

The sense information is redundant in this case but is essential for a closed curve.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.master_representation"
where both parameter and point are present at either end of the curve this indicates the preferred form. Multiple representations provide the ability to communicate data in more than one form, even though the data are expected to be geometrically identical.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.master_representation.__note"
The *master_representation* attribute acknowledges the impracticality of ensuring that multiple forms are indeed identical and allows the indication of a preferred form. This would probably be determined by the creator of the data. All characteristics, such as parametrisation, domain, and results of evaluation, for an entity having multiple representations, are derived from the master representation. Any use of the other representations is a compromise for practical considerations.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.wr:WR1"
Either a single value is specified for **trim_1**, or, the two trimming values are of different types (point and parameter).
*)


(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.wr:WR2"
Either a single value is specified for **trim_2**, or, the two trimming values are of different types (point and parameter).
*)


(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.wr:IP1"
Where both the parameter value and the cartesian point exist for **trim_1** or **trim_2** they shall be consistent, i.e., the **basis_curve** evaluated at the parameter value shall coincide with the specified point.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.wr:IP2"
When a cartesian point is specified by **trim_1** or by **trim_2**, it shall lie on the **basis_curve**.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.wr:IP3"
Except in the case of a closed **basis_curve**, where both parameter_1 and parameter_2 exist,
they shall be consistent with the sense flag, i.e., stem:["sense" = "parameter"_1 < "parameter"_2].
*)


(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.wr:IP4"
If both parameter_1 and parameter_2 exist, stem:["parameter"_1 ne "parameter"_2].
*)


(*"geometry_schema.trimmed_curve.wr:IP5"
When a parameter value is specified by **trim_1** or **trim_2**, it shall lie within the parametric range of the **basis_curve**.

(*"geometry_schema.composite_curve"
A **composite_curve** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_curve,bounded_curve>>, that is a collection of curves joined end-to-end. The individual segments of the curve are themselves defined as <<express:geometry_schema.composite_curve_segment,composite_curve_segment>>s. The parametrisation of the composite curve is an accumulation of the parametric ranges of the referenced bounded curves. The first segment is parametrised from 0 to stem:[l_1], and, for stem:[i ge 2], the stem:[i] th segment is parametrised from

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sum_(k=1)^{i-1}l_k "to" sum_(k=1)^{i}l_k
++++

//prior representation::image::CompC1.gif[]

where stem:[l_k] is the parametric length (i.e., difference between maximum and minimum parameter values) of the curve underlying the stem:[k] th segment.

Let stem:[T] denote the parameter for the **composite_curve**.

Then, if the stem:[i"th"] segment is not a **reparametrised_composite_curve_segment**, stem:[T] is related to the parameter stem:[t_1, t_{i0}, le t_1, le t_{i1}] for the stem:[i"th"] segment by the equation:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
T = sum_(k=1)^{i-1} l_k + t_i - t_(i0)
++++

//prior representation::image::CompC2a.gif[]

if **segments[i].same_sense** = TRUE;

or by the equation:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
T = sum_(k=1)^{i-1}l_k + t_(i1) - t_i
++++

//prior representation::image::CompC2b.gif[]

if **segments[i].same_sense** = FALSE.

If **segments[i]** is of type **reparametrised_composite_curve_segment**,

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
T = Sigma_{k=1}^{i-1} l_{k} + tau
++++

(*"geometry_schema.pcurve"
A **pcurve** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>>, that is a 3D curve defined by means of a 2D curve in the parameter space of a surface. If the curve is parametrised by the function stem:[(u,v) = f(t)], and the surface is parametrised by the function stem:[(x,y,z) = g(u,v)], the **pcurve** is parametrised by the function stem:[(x,y,z) = g(f(t))].

A **pcurve** definition contains a reference to its **basis_surface** and an indirect reference to a 2D curve through a <<express:representation_schema.definitional_representation,definitional_representation>> entity. The 2D curve, being in parameter space, is not in the context of the basis surface. Thus a direct reference is not possible. For the 2D curve the variables involved are stem:[u] and stem:[v], which occur in the parametric representation of the **basis_surface** rather than _x,y_ Cartesian coordinates. The curve is only defined within the parametric range of the surface.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.pcurve.basis_surface"
the surface in whose parameter space the curve is defined;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.pcurve.reference_to_curve"
the reference to the parameter space curve which defines the **pcurve** ;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.pcurve.wr:WR1"
The set of items in the <<express:representation_schema.definitional_representation,definitional_representation>> entity corresponding to the **reference_to_curve** shall have exactly one element.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.pcurve.wr:WR2"
The unique item in the set shall be a curve.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.pcurve.wr:WR3"
The dimensionality of this parameter space curve shall be 2.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.bounded_pcurve"
A **bounded_pcurve** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>>, which also has the properties of a <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_curve,bounded_curve>>.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.bounded_pcurve.wr:WR1"
The referenced curve of the <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>> supertype shall be of type <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_curve,bounded_curve>>. This ensures that the **bounded_pcurve** is of finite arc length.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_curve"
A **surface_curve** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>>, that is a curve on a surface. The curve is represented as a curve ({blank} **curve_3d** {blank}) in three-dimensional space and possibly as a curve, corresponding to a <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>>, in the two-dimensional parametric space of a surface. The ability of this curve to reference a list of 1 or 2 <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve_or_surface,pcurve_or_surface>>s enables this entity to define either a curve on a single surface, or an intersection curve which has two distinct surface associations. A `seam' on a closed surface can also be represented by this entity; in this case each **associated_geometry** will be a pcurve lying on the same surface. Each <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>>, if it exists, shall be parametrised to have the same sense as **curve_3d**. The **surface_curve** takes its parametrisation directly from either **curve_3d** or <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>> as indicated by the attribute master representation.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_curve.__note"
Because of the ANDOR relationship with the *bounded_surface_curve* subtype an instance of a *surface_curve* may be any one of the following:



*  a *surface_curve;*
*  a <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_surface_curve,bounded_surface_curve>>;
*  an <<express:geometry_schema.intersection_curve,intersection_curve>>;
*  an <<express:geometry_schema.intersection_curve,intersection_curve>> AND <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_surface_curve,bounded_surface_curve>>;
*  a <<express:geometry_schema.seam_curve,seam_curve>>;
*  a <<express:geometry_schema.seam_curve,seam_curve>> AND <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_surface_curve,bounded_surface_curve>>.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.surface_curve.curve_3d"
the curve which is the three-dimensional representation of the **surface_curve** ;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_curve.associated_geometry"
a list of one or two pcurves or surfaces which define the surface or surfaces associated with the surface curve. Two elements in this list indicate that the curve has two surface associations which need not be two distinct surfaces. When a pcurve is selected, it identifies a surface and also associates a basis curve in the parameter space of this surface;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_curve.master_representation"
the **master_representation** defines the curve used to determine the unique parametrisation of the **surface_curve**.

The **master_representation** takes one of the values **curve_3d**, **pcurve_s1** or **pcurve_s2** to indicate a preference for the 3D curve, or the first or second pcurve, in the associated geometry list, respectively. Multiple representations provide the ability to communicate data in more than one form, even though the data is expected to be geometrically identical.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_curve.master_representation.__note"
The *master_representation* attribute acknowledges the impracticality of ensuring that multiple forms are indeed identical and allows the indication of a preferred form. This would probably be determined by the creator of the data. All characteristics, such as parametrisation, domain, and results of evaluation, for an entity having multiple representations, are derived from the master representation. Any use of the other representations is a compromise for practical considerations.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.surface_curve.basis_surface"
the surface, or surfaces on which the **surface_curve** lies. This is determined from the **associated_geometry** list.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_curve.wr:WR1"
The currve **curve_3d** shall be defined in three-dimensional space.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_curve.wr:WR2"
The value **pcurve_s1** shall only be nominated as the master representation if the first element of the associated geometry list is a <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>>.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_curve.wr:WR3"
The value **pcurve_s2** shall only be nominated as the master representation if the second element of the associated geometry list is a pcurve. This also requires that **pcurve_s2** shall not be nominated when the associated geometry list contains a single element.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_curve.wr:WR4"
The curve **curve_3d** shall not be a <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>>.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_curve.wr:IP1"
Where **curve_3d** and one or more <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>>s exist they shall represent the same mathematical point set. (i.e., They shall coincide geometrically but may differ in parametrisation.)
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_curve.wr:IP2"
**curve_3d** and any associated <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>>s shall agree with respect to their senses.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.intersection_curve"
A **intersection_curve** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve,surface_curve>>, which results from the intersection of two surfaces. It is represented as a special subtype of the <<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve,surface_curve>> entity having two distinct surface associations defined via the associated geometry list.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.intersection_curve.wr:WR1"
The intersection curve shall have precisely two associated geometry elements.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.intersection_curve.wr:WR2"
The two associated geometry elements shall be related to distinct surfaces. These are the surfaces which define the intersection curve.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.seam_curve"
A **seam_curve** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve,surface_curve>>, that is a curve on a closed parametric surface which has two distinct representations as constant parameter curves at the two extremes of the parameter range for the surface.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.seam_curve.__example"
The `seam' on a cylinder has representations as the lines stem:[u = 0] or  stem:[u = 360] degrees in parameter space.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.seam_curve.wr:WR1"
The seam curve shall have precisely two <<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve.associated_geometry,associated_geometry>>s.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.seam_curve.wr:WR2"
The two <<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve.associated_geometry,associated_geometry>>s shall be related to the same surface.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.seam_curve.wr:WR3"
The first <<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve.associated_geometry,associated_geometry>> shall be a <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>>.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.seam_curve.wr:WR4"
The second <<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve.associated_geometry,associated_geometry>> shall be a <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>>.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.bounded_surface_curve"
A **bounded_surface_curve** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve,surface_curve>>, which also has the properties of a <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_curve,bounded_curve>>.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.bounded_surface_curve.wr:WR1"
The <<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve.curve_3d,curve_3d>> attribute of the <<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve,surface_curve>> supertype shall be a <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_curve,bounded_curve>>.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.composite_curve_on_surface"
A **composite_curve_on_surface** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.composite_curve,composite_curve>>, that is a collection of segments which are curves on a surface. Each segment shall lie on the basis surface, and shall reference a <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_surface_curve,bounded_surface_curve>>, or a <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_pcurve,bounded_pcurve>>, or a <<express:geometry_schema.composite_curve_on_surface,composite_curve_on_surface>>.

There shall be at least positional continuity between adjacent segments. The parametrisation of the composite curve is obtained from the accumulation of the parametric ranges of the segments. The first segment is parametrised from 0 to stem:[l_1], and, for stem:[i ge 2], the stem:[i"th"] segment is parametrised from

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sum_(k=1)^(i-1) l_k " to " sum_(k=1)^(i) l_k ,
++++

where stem:[l_k] is the parametric length (i.e., difference between maximum and minimum parameter values) of the stem:[k^{th}] curve segment.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.composite_curve_on_surface.__note"
A <<express:geometry_schema.composite_curve_on_surface,composite_curve_on_surface>> can be included as the <<express:geometry_schema.composite_curve_segment.parent_curve,parent_curve>> attribute of a <<express:geometry_schema.composite_curve_segment,composite_curve_segment>> since it is a bounded curve subtype.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.composite_curve_on_surface.basis_surface"
the surface on which the composite curve is defined.;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.composite_curve_on_surface\composite_curve.n_segments"
The component bounded curves, their transitions and senses. The transition for the last segment defines the transition between the end of the last segment and the start of the first; this element may take the value **discontinuous**, which indicates an open curve. For each segment the **parent_curve** shall be either a **bounded_pcurve**, a **bounded_surface_curve**, or a **composite_curve_on_surface**.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.composite_curve_on_surface\composite_curve.self_intersec"
Indication of whether the curve intersects itself or not.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.composite_curve_on_surface\composite_curve.dim"
The dimensionality of the coordinate space for the composite curve.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.composite_curve_on_surface\composite_curve.closed_curve"
Indication of whether the curve is closed or not.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.composite_curve_on_surface.wr:WR1"
The **basis_surface** SET shall contain at least one surface. This ensures that all segments reference curves on the same surface.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.composite_curve_on_surface.wr:WR2"
Each segment shall reference a <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>>, or a <<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve,surface_curve>>, or a <<express:geometry_schema.composite_curve_on_surface,composite_curve_on_surface>>.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.composite_curve_on_surface.wr:IP1"
Each <<express:geometry_schema.composite_curve_segment.parent_curve,parent_curve>> referenced by a **composite_curve_on_surface** segment shall be a curve on surface and a bounded curve.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_2d"
A **offset_curve_2d** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>>, at a constant distance from a basis curve in two-dimensional space. This entity defines a simple plane-offset curve by offsetting by **distance** along the normal to **basis_curve** in the plane of **basis_curve**.

The underlying curve shall have a well-defined tangent direction at every point. In the case of a composite curve, the transition code between each segment shall be **cont_same_gradient** or **cont_same_gradient_same_curvature**.

The **offset_curve_2d** takes its parametrisation from the **basis_curve**. The **offset_curve_2d** is parametrised as

--
[stem%unnumbered]
++++
lambda(u) = C(u) + d cdot O(t)
++++

[%key]
stem:[bb C(u)]:: <<express:geometry_schema.offset_curve_2d.basis_curve,basis curve>> at location stem:[u];
stem:[bb t]:: Unit-vector tangent to the basis curve at parameter u;
stem:[bb O(bb t)]:: <<express:geometry_schema.orthogonal_complement,orthogonal complement>> of stem:[bb t];
stem:[d]:: <<express:geometry_schema.offset_curve_2d.distance,distance>>;
--


The underlying curve shall be two-dimensional.,
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_2d.__note"
The *offset_curve_2d* may differ in nature from the *basis_curve*; the offset of a non self-intersecting curve can be self-intersecting. Care should be taken to ensure that the offset to a continuous curve does not become discontinuous.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_2d.basis_curve"
the curve that is being offset;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_2d.distance"
the distance of the offset curve from the basis curve. **distance** may be positive, negative or zero. A positive value of **distance** defines an offset in the direction which is normal to the curve in the sense of an anti-clockwise rotation through 90 degrees from the tangent vector **T** at the given point. (This is in the direction of <<express:geometry_schema.orthogonal_complement,orthogonal_complement>>(t).)
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_2d.self_intersect"
an indication of whether the offset curve self-intersects; this is for information only.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_2d.wr:WR1"
The The underlying **basis_curve** shall be defined in two-dimensional space..
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_3d"
An **offset_curve_3d** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>>, at a constant distance from a basis curve in three-dimensional space. The underlying curve shall have a well-defined tangent direction at every point. In the case of a composite curve the transition code between each segment shall be **cont_same_gradient** or **cont_same_gradient_same_curvature**. The offset curve at any point (parameter) on the basis curve is in the direction stem:[langle v xx t rangle ] where stem:[v] is the fixed reference direction and stem:[t] is the unit tangent to the **basis_curve**. For the offset direction to be well defined, stem:[t] shall not at any point of the curve be in the same, or opposite, direction as stem:[v].

The **offset_curve_3d** takes its parametrisation from the **basis_curve**. The **offset_curve_3d** is parametrised as

--
[stem%unnumbered]
++++
lambda(u) = C(u) + d <<v xx t>>,
++++

[%key]
stem:[C(u)]:: <<express:geometry_schema.offset_curve_3d.basis_curve,basis curve at location u>>;
stem:[bb t]:: Unit-vector tangent to the basis curve at parameter u.
stem:[d]:: <<express:geometry_schema.offset_curve_3d.distance,distance>>;
stem:[v]:: <<express:geometry_schema.offset_curve_3d.ref_direction,reference distance>>;
-- *)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_3d.__note"
The *offset_curve_3d* may differ in nature from the *basis_curve*; the offset of a non-self-intersecting curve can be self-intersecting. Care should be taken to ensure that the offset to a continuous curve does not become discontinuous.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_3d.basis_curve"
the curve that is being offset;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_3d.distance"
the distance of the offset curve from the basis curve; **distance** may be positive, negative or zero;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_3d.self_intersect"
an indication of whether the offset curve self-intersects; this is for information only;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_3d.ref_direction"
the <<express:geometry_schema.direction,direction>> used to define the direction of the **offset_curve_3d** from the **basis_curve**.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_3d.wr:WR1"
Both the underlying curve and the reference direction shall be in three-dimensional space.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_curve_3d.wr:IP1"
At no point on the curve shall **ref_direction** be parallel, or opposite to, the direction of the tangent vector.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.curve_replica"
A **curve_replica** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>>, and is a replica of a curve in a different location. It is defined by referencing the parent curve and a transformation. The geometric form of the curve produced will be the same as the parent curve, but, where the transformation includes scaling, the dimensions will differ. The curve replica takes its parametric range and parametrisation directly from the parent curve. Where the parent curve is a curve on surface, the replica will not in general share the property of lying on the surface.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.curve_replica.parent_curve"
the curve that is being copied;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.curve_replica.transformation"
the <<express:geometry_schema.cartesian_transformation_operator,cartesian_transformation_operator>> which defines the location of the curve replica. This transformation may include scaling.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.curve_replica.wr:WR1"
The coordinate space dimensionality of the **transformation** attribute shall be the same as that of the **parent_curve**.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.curve_replica.wr:WR2"
A **curve_replica** shall not participate in its own definition.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface"
A **surface** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>>, that can be envisioned as a set of connected points in 3-dimensional space which is always locally 2-dimensional, but need not be a manifold. A surface shall not be a single point or in part, or entirely, a curve.

Each surface has a parametric representation of the form
[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u,v),
++++

where stem:[u] and stem:[v] are independent dimensionless parameters. The unit normal **N**, at any point on the surface, is given by the equation

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
N(u,v) = (del sigma)/(del u) xx (del sigma)/(del u);
++++
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface.wr:IP1"
A **surface** has non-zero area.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface.wr:IP2"
A **surface** is arcwise connected.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.elementary_surface"
A **elementary_surface** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.surface,surface>>, that is a simple analytic surface with defined parametric representation.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.elementary_surface.position"
the location and orientation of the surface,this attribute is used in the definition of the parametrisation of the surface.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.plane"
A **plane** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.elementary_surface,elementary_surface>>, that is an unbounded surface with a constant normal. A **plane** is defined by a point on the plane and the normal direction to the plane.

The data is to be interpreted as follows:

[%key]
stem:[C]:: <<express:geometry_schema.placement.location,location>>;
stem:[bb x]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[1]>>;
stem:[bb y]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[2]>>;
stem:[bb z]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[3]>> ("normal to plane");

and the surface is parametrised as

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u,v) = C + ux + vy
++++

where the parametrisation range is stem:[-oo < u, v < oo].

In the above parametrisation, the length unit for the unit vectors **x** and **y** is derived from the context of the **plane**.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.plane\elementary_surface.position"
The location and orientation of the surface. This attribute is inherited from the **elementary_surface** supertype.

**position.location** A point in the plane.

**position.p[3]** This direction, which is equal to **position.axis**, defines the normal to the plane.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.cylindrical_surface"
A **cylindrical_surface** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.elementary_surface,elementary_surface>>, that is a surface at a constant distance (the **radius** {blank})from a straight line. A **cylindrical_surface** is defined by its radius and its orientation and location.

The data is to be interpreted as follows:

[%key]
stem:[C]:: <<express:geometry_schema.placement.location,location>>;
stem:[bb x]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[1]>>;
stem:[bb y]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[2]>>;
stem:[bb z]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[3]>>;
stem:[R]:: <<express:geometry_schema.conical_surface.radius,radius>>;

and the surface is parametrised as

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u,v) = C + R((cos u)x + (sin u)y) + vz
++++

where the parametrisation range is stem:[0 le u le 360] degrees and stem:[-oo < v < oo]. In the above parametrisation the length unit for the unit vector stem:[bb z] is equal to that of the **radius**. stem:[u] is an angular parameter and when a numerical value is specified it shall use the current units for <<express:measure_schema.plane_angle_measure,plane_angle_measure>>.

In the placement coordinate system defined above, the surface is represented by the equation stem:[S = 0], where

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
S(x, y, z) = x^{2} + y^{2} - R^{2}
++++

The positive direction of the normal to the surface at any point on the surface is given by:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
( S_{x}, S_{y}, S_{z} ).
++++

The unit normal is given by

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
N(u,v) = (cos(u))x + (sin (u))y.
++++

The sense of this normal is away from the axis of the cylinder.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.cylindrical_surface\elementary_surface.position"
The location and orientation of the surface. This attribute is inherited from the **elementary_surface** supertype.

**position.location** A point on the axis of the cylinder.

**position.p[3]** The direction of the axis of the cylinder.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.cylindrical_surface.radius"
the radius of the cylinder.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.conical_surface"
A **conical_surface** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.elementary_surface,elementary_surface>>, which could be produced by revolving a line in 3-dimensional space about any intersecting line.
The data is to be interpreted as follows:

[%key]
stem:[C]:: <<express:geometry_schema.placement.location,location>>;
stem:[bb x]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[1]>>;
stem:[bb y]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[2]>>;
stem:[bb z]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[3]>> ("axis of conical_surface");
stem:[R]:: <<express:geometry_schema.conical_surface.radius,radius>>;
stem:[alpha]:: <<express:geometry_schema.conical_surface.semi_angle,semi_angle>>;

and the surface is parametrised as

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u,v) = C + (R + v tan(alpha))((cos u)x + (sin u)y) + v * z
++++

where the parametrisation range is stem:[0 le u le 360] degrees and stem:[-oo < v < oo]. In the above parametrisation the length unit for the unit vector stem:[bb z] is equal to that of the **radius**.

stem:[u] is an angular parameter and when a numerical value is specified it shall use the current units for <<express:measure_schema.plane_angle_measure,plane_angle_measure>>. In the placement coordinate system defined above, the surface is represented by the equation stem:[S = 0], where

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
S(x, y, z) = x^{2} + y^{2} - (R + z * tan(alpha))^{2}
++++

The positive direction of the normal to the surface at any point on the surface is given by

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
( S_{x}, S_{y}, S_{z} ).
++++

The unit normal is given by

//N(u,v) = ((cos u)x + (sin u)y - (tan(alpha))z)/( (√(1 + (tan(alpha))^{2})), if R + v tan(alpha) > 0.0
//rewritten for clarity
[stem%unnumbered]
++++
N(u,v) = ((cos u) x + (sin u) y - (tan(alpha)) z) / sqrt(1 + (tan(alpha))^2),
where (R + v tan(alpha)) > 0
++++

//rewritten for clarity
[stem%unnumbered]
++++
N(u,v) = - ((cos u)x + (sin u)y - (tan(alpha))z)/ (sqrt(1 + (tan(alpha))^{2})),
if (R + v tan(alpha)) < 0.0.
++++

The sense of the normal is away from the axis of the cone. If the radius is zero, the cone apex is at the point stem:[(0, 0, 0)] in the placement coordinate system (i.e., at **SELF\elementary_surface.position.location** {blank}).
*)

(*"geometry_schema.conical_surface.__figure"
[[figure-geometry_schema-Geomfig13]]
.Conical_surface
====
image::Geomfig13.gif[]
====
*)

(*"geometry_schema.conical_surface.__note"
This form of representation is designed to provide the greatest geometric precision for those parts of the surface which are close to the location point *C*. For this reason the apex should only be selected as location point if the region of the surface close to the apex is of interest.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.conical_surface.__note"
The normal to the surface is undefined at the point where  stem:[R + v tan(alpha) = 0.0].
*)

(*"geometry_schema.conical_surface\elementary_surface.position"
//tttt this is wrong. we don't reference supertype attributes like this.
The location and orientation of the surface. This attribute is inherited from the **elementary_surface** supertype.

**position.location** A point on the axis of the cone.

**position.p[3]** The direction of the axis of the cone.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.conical_surface.radius"
the radius of the circular curve of intersection between the cone and a plane perpendicular to the axis of the cone passing through the location point (i.e., **SELF\elementary_surface.position.location** {blank});
*)


(*"geometry_schema.conical_surface.semi_angle"
the cone semi-angle.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.conical_surface.semi_angle.__note"
See <<figure-geometry_schema-Geomfig13>> 14 for illustration of the attributes.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.conical_surface.wr:WR1"
The radius shall not be negative.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.conical_surfacee.wr:WR2"
The semi-angle shall be between 0 and 90 degrees.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.spherical_surface"
A **spherical_surface** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.elementary_surface,elementary_surface>>, which is at a constant distance (the **radius** {blank}) from a central point. A **spherical_surface** is defined by the radius and the location and orientation of the surface.

The data is to be interpreted as follows:


[%key]
stem:[C]:: <<express:geometry_schema.placement.location,location>>;
stem:[R]:: <<express:geometry_schema.spherical_surface.radius,radius>>;
stem:[bb x]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[1]>>;
stem:[bb y]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[2]>>;
stem:[bb z]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[3]>>;

and the surface is parametrised as

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u,v) = C + R cos v ((cos u) x + (sin u) y) + R(sin v) z
++++

where the parametrisation range is stem:[0 le u le 360] degrees and _stem:[-90 le v le 90] degrees.

stem:[u] and stem:[v] are angular parameters and when numerical values are specified they shall use the current units for **plane_angle_measure.**

In the placement coordinate system defined above, the surface is represented by the equation stem:[S = 0], where
[stem%unnumbered]
++++
S(x, y, z) = x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} - R^{2}.

The positive direction of the normal to the surface at any point on the surface is given by

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
( S_{x}, S_{y}, S_{z} ).
++++

The unit normal is given by

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
N(u,v) = cos v((cos u)x + (sin u)y) + (sin v)z,
++++

(*"geometry_schema.toroidal_surface"
A **toroidal_surface** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.elementary_surface,elementary_surface>>, which could be produced by revolving a circle about a line in its plane. The radius of the circle being revolved is referred to here as the **minor_radius** and the **major_radius** is the distance from the centre of this circle to the axis of revolution. A **toroidal_surface** is defined by the major and minor radii and the position and orientation of the surface.

The data is to be interpreted as follows:

[%key]
stem:[C]:: <<express:geometry_schema.placement.location,location>>;
stem:[bb x]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[1]>>;
stem:[bb y]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[2]>>;
stem:[bb z]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[3]>> ("axis of toroidal_surface");
stem:[R]:: <<express:geometry_schema.conical_surface.radius,radius>>;
stem:[r]:: "minor_radius";

and the surface is parametrised as

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u,v) = C + (R + rcos v)((cos u)x + (sin u))y) + r(sin v)z
++++

where the parametrisation range is stem:[0 le u], stem:[v le 360] degrees.

stem:[u] and stem:[v] are angular parameters and when numerical values are specified they shall use the current units for **plane_angle_measure.**

In the placement coordinate system defined above, the surface is represented by the equation stem:[S = 0], where

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
S(x, y, z) = x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} -2R * sqrt(x^{2}+y^{2}) - r^{2} + R^{2}.
++++

The positive direction of the normal to the surface at any point on the surface is given by

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
( S_{x}, S_{y}, S_{z} ).
++++

The unit normal is given by

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
N(u,v) = cosv((cos u)x + (sin u)y) + (sin v)z.
++++

The sense of this normal is away from the nearest point on the circle of radius stem:[R] with centre stem:[C]anifold surface will be produced if the major radius is greater than the minor radius. If this condition is not fulfilled, the resulting surface will be self-intersecting.
*)

the major-radius of the torus;

(*"geometry_schema.toroidal_surface.minor_radius"
the minor-radius of the torus.

The data is to be interpreted as follows:

(*"geometry_schema.dupin_cyclide_surface"
A **dupin_cyclide_surface** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.elementary_surface,elementary_surface>>, that is a generalisation of a <<express:geometry_schema.toroidal_surface,toroidal_surface>> in which the radius of the generatrix varies as it is swept around the directrix, passing through a maximum and a minimum value. The directrix is in general an ellipse, though that fact is not germane to the definition given here. The surface has two orthogonal planes of symmetry, and in both of them its cross-section is a pair of circles.

As with the <<express:geometry_schema.toroidal_surface,toroidal_surface>>, self-intersecting forms occur. The Dupin cyclides are special cases of a more general class of surfaces known as _generalized cyclides_ (or sometimes simply _cyclides_). The present specification does not cover the wider class.

The interpretation of the data is as follows:


[%key]
stem:[C]:: <<express:geometry_schema.placement.location,location>> (centre);
stem:[bb x]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[1]>>;
stem:[bb y]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[2]>>;
stem:[bb z]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[3]>>;
stem:[R]:: <<express:geometry_schema.dupin_cyclide_surface.generalised_major_radius,generalised_major_radius>>;
stem:[r]:: <<express:geometry_schema.dupin_cyclide_surface.generalised_minor_radius,generalised_minor_radius>>;
stem:[s]:: <<express:geometry_schema.dupin_cyclide_surface.skewness,skewness>> != ss;

and the surface is parametrised as

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u,v) = ((x),(y),(z)) = C + 1/{R + s cosu cosv} ((r(s + R cosu cosv) + (R^2 - s^2)cosu),(sqrt(R^2 - s^2) sin u(R + cosv)),(sqrt(R^2 - s^2) sin v(r - s cosu)))
++++

//prior representation:: image::Dupc1.gif[]

where the domain of parametrisation is stem:[0 "P{degree}" le u,v le 360 "P{degree}"] , and stem:[sqrt] denotes the positive square root. stem:[u] and stem:[v] are angular parameters and when numerical values are specified they shall use the current units for <<express:measure_schema.plane_angle_measure,plane_angle_measure>>.

In the placement coordinate system defined above the Dupin cyclide surface has the algebraic representation stem:[S = 0], where

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
S = (x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} + R^{2} - r^{2} - s^{2})^{2} - 4(Rx - rs)^{2}- 4(R^{2} - s^{2})y^{2}.
++++

The positive direction of the normal vector at any point on the surface is given by

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
(S_{x},S_{y},S_{z}).
++++

In parametric terms, the unit surface normal vector is

//N(u,v) = (R cos(u) cos(v) + s)x + (√(R^{2} - s^{2}) sin(u) cos(v))y + (√(R^{2} - s^{2}) sin(v))z
[stem%unnumbered]
++++
N(u,v) = (R cos(u) cos(v) + s)x + (sqrt(R^{2} - s^{2}) sin(u) cos(v))y + (sqrt(R^{2} - s^{2}) sin(v))z
++++

This enables the parametric surface representation to be rewritten as

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u,v) = sigma_{0}(u,v) + rN(u,v),
++++

which shows that any Dupin cyclide with given values of stem:[R] and stem:[s] is a parallel offset from a base Dupin cyclide stem:[sigma_0(u,v)] with the same values of _R,s_ but with stem:[r = 0].

Further, the offset distance is precisely stem:[r]. This generalizes an important property of the torus.

The Dupin cyclide is a manifold surface under the conditions stem:[0 le s < r < R]. This form is known as a _ring cyclide_. Self-intersecting forms arise when the circles in either plane of symmetry intersect. The conditions stem:[0 < r le s < R] give a _horned cyclide_ and the conditions stem:[0 le s le R < r] a _spindle cyclide_. The sense of the surface normal given above is outwards from both circles in the upper view and from the annular region in the lower cross-sectional view in Figure 15. For the ring cyclide this means that it is outwards-pointing over the entire surface. For the horned cyclide the normal is inward-pointing over the smaller portion of the surface lying between the two self-intersection points. For the spindle cyclide the `spindle' corresponds to the `lemon' solid arising in the case of a self-intersecting torus. For this case of the Dupin cyclide the normal is outward-pointing over both the `apple' and 'lemon' solids enclosed by the surface.
*)

.Cross-sections of a Dupin cyclide with C = 0
====
image::Geomfig15.gif[]
====
*)

Further details of the properties and applications of this useful but unfamiliar surface may be found in PRATT [13],[14], and the further references they contain.

(*"geometry_schema.dupin_cyclide_surface.__note"
The three parameters stem:[r], stem:[R] and stem:[s] determine the centres and radii of the circles in the planes of symmetry, as shown in Figure 15. Conversely, knowledge of the geometry of these circles allows the defining cyclide parameters to be determined. In the upper and lower diagrams respectively of Figure 15 the circles have parameter values stem:[u = 0 * "deg"] (right), stem:[u = 180 * "deg"] (left), stem:[v = 0 "deg"] (inner) and stem:[v = 180 "deg"] (outer). The point with parameter values (0,0) is the extreme point on the positive x-axis. The parameter stem:[u] runs anticlockwise around both circles in the lower diagram, and the parameter stem:[v] runs clockwise round the left-hand circle and anticlockwise round the right-hand circle in the upper diagram.

For ISO 10303 purposes, the values of stem:[R] and stem:[r] are of type *positive_length_measure* and stem:[s] is non-negative. The surface defined by the foregoing equations when one or more of stem:[R], stem:[r] and stem:[s] is negative corresponds to a reparametrisation of a Dupin cyclide for which these constants are all non-negative.

(*"geometry_schema.dupin_cyclide_surface.__note"
Both families of isoparametric curves of the Dupin cyclide consist of circles.

(*"geometry_schema.dupin_cyclide_surface.__note"
Dupin cyclides can be used to construct smooth joins between cylindrical and/or conical surfaces whose (possibly skew) axes have arbitrary relative orientations. Additionally, smooth T-junctions between cones and cylinders can be designed using Dupin cyclides.

(*"geometry_schema.dupin_cyclide_surface.__note"

The Dupin cyclide as defined here is a quartic (degree four) algebraic surface of bounded extent. There also exists a cubic Dupin cyclide of infinite extent, not currently defined in this document.

stem:[C]:: <<express:geometry_schema.placement.location,location>>;
stem:[K1]:: <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_surface.u_upper,upper index on u control points>>;
stem:[K2]:: <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_surface.v_upper,upper index on v control points>>;
stem:[bb P_{ij}]:: <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_surface.control_points,control_points>>;
stem:[w_{ij}]:: <<express:geometry_schema.rational_b_spline_surface.weights,weights>>;
stem:[d1]:: <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_surface.u_degree,u_degree>>;
stem:[d2]:: <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_surface.v_degree,v_degree>>;


The control points are ordered as

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
P_{00}, P_{01}, P_{02}, ldots P_{K1K2-1}, P_{K1K2}.
++++

The weights, in the case of the rational subtype, are ordered similarly.

For each parameter, stem:[s = u] or stem:[v], if stem:[k] is the upper index on the control points and stem:[d] is the degree for stem:[s], the knot array is an array of stem:[(k + d + 2)] real numbers stem:[[s_{-d}, ldots ,s_{k+1}\]]_, such that for all indices stem:[j in [-d, k\], s_j le s_{j+1}]. This array is obtained from the appropriate **u_knots** or **v_knots** list by repeating each multiple knot according to the multiplicity.

stem:[N_i^d], the stem:[i"th"] normalised B-spline basis function of degree stem:[d], is defined on the subset:

stem:[[s_{i-d}, ldots ,s_{i+1}\]] of this array.

Let stem:[L] denote the number of distinct values amongst the knots in the knot list; stem:[L] will be referred to as the 'upper index on knots'. Let stem:[m_j] denote the multiplicity (i.e., number of repetitions) of the stem:[j"th"] distinct knot value. Then:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sum_(i=1)^{L} m_i = d + k + 2
++++

All knot multiplicities except the first and the last shall be in the range stem:[1, ldots, d]; the first and last may have a maximum value of stem:[d + 1].

The **surface_form** is used to identify specific quadric surface types (which shall have degree two), ruled surfaces and surfaces of revolution. As with the **b_spline_curve**, the **surface_form** is informational only and the spline data takes precedence.

The surface is to be interpreted as follows:

In the polynomial case the surface is given by the equation:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u,v) = sum_(i=0)^{K1} sum_(j=0)^{K2} (P_(i j) N_i^(d_1)(u) N_j^(d_2)(v))
++++

In the rational case the surface equation is:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u,v) = (sum_(i=0)^{K1} sum_(j=0)^{K2}
(w_(i j) P_(i j) N_i^(d_1)(u) N_j^(d_2)(v))) / (sum_(i=0)^{K1}
sum_(j=0)^{K2} (w_(i j) N_i^(d_1)(u) N_j^(d_2)(v)))
++++

*)

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface"
A **locally_refined_spline_surface** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_surface,bounded_surface>> that is a piecewise parametric polynomial or rational surface described in terms of control points and local B-spline functions. If the set of B-spline functions are linearly independent, they will form a basis. With appropriate attribute values, the surface is capable of representing single span or spline surfaces of explicit polynomial, rational, Bézier or B-spline type. However, the **locally_ refined_spline_surface** entity is intended for spline surfaces that do not have a tensor product structure. The degree of the surface can vary as the B-splines from which it is defined, need not to have the same polynomial degree.

The entity **locally_refined_spline_surface** can, with proper pre and post processing, be used to represent surfaces of the types: analysis suitable T-spline, standard T-spline, semi-standard T-spline, hierarchical B-spline and LR B-spline. Interpretation of the data is as follows: The surface, in the polynomial case, is given by:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u,v) = sum_(i=1)^K( P_i s_i N_i^(d_1)(u) N_i^(d_2)(v) )
++++

//prior representation::image::LRsurface.gif[]

In the rational case all weights shall be positive and the surface is given by:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u,v) = (
  sum_(i=1)^K ( w_i P_i s_i N_i^(d_1)(u) N_i^(d_2)(v) )
) / (
  sum_(i=1)^K ( w_i s_i N_i^(d_1)(u) N_i^(d_2)(v) )
)
++++

//prior representation::image::RationalLRsurf.gif[]

where (in both equations)
[stem%unnumbered]
++++
K = number of control points,
++++

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
P_{i} = control points(i),
++++

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
s_{i}= "scaling_factors"(i),
++++

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
w_{i} = "weights_data"(i),
++++

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
N_{i}^{d1}(u) = "u_bspline"(i), and
++++

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
d1="u_degree".
++++

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
N_{i}^{d2}(v) = "v_bspline"(i), and
++++

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
d2="v_degree".
++++

The weights, in the case of the rational subtype, are given in the same sequence as the coefficients. The knot values and multiplicities are defined in the entity <<express:geometry_schema.local_b_spline,local_b_spline>>. The B-splines are defined over a domain described by knot vectors in the parameter directions of the surface. However, in contrast to B-bspline surfaces, the basis functions or B-splines do not need to adapt to all knot lines in their supports. This facilitates the definition of a spline surface on a box partition.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.__note"
A B-spline surface compactly represents a large smooth area. However, if the shape is mainly smooth, but with some areas of higher complexity, the data size of a B-spline surface tends to be high. Due to the tensor product construction of the B-spline surface the knot lines are global and high data size in one area of the surface cannot be kept locally. The following approaches to define a B-spline surface with the property of local refinement have been pursued:



*  PHT splines,
*  General T-splines,
*  Analysis suitable T-splines,
*  Standard and semi-standard T-splines,
*  Hierarchical B-splines,
*  LR B-splines.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.__note"
A locally refined spline surface is rational if and only if the weights are not all identical; this can be represented by the <<express:geometry_schema.rational_locally_refined_spline_surface,rational_locally_refined_spline_surface>> subtype. If it is polynomial, the weights may be defaulted to all being 1.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.__note"
The degrees are associated with the local_b_splines and do not need to be constant throughout the surface.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.__note"
When the polynomial degree is the same for all B-splines and no knot lines exist that do not cross the entire parameter domain, the *locally_refined_spline_surface* will coincide with <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_surface_with_knots,b_spline_surface_with_knots>>. In that case <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_surface_with_knots,b_spline_surface_with_knots>>. has the simplest and most compact representation.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.__note"
A *locally_refined_spline_surface* can be of type analysis suitable T-spline, hierarchical B-spline, LR-spline, semi standard T-spline or standard T-spline. The type is given by the enumeration <<express:geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_type_enum,locally_refined_spline_type_enum>>, and the packing and unpacking of the surface will depend on this type.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.u_b_splines"
the <<express:geometry_schema.local_b_spline,local_b_spline>> functions in the first (stem:[u]) parameter direction from which the surface is defined. These functions refer to the **u_knots** list for their knot parameter values;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.v_b_splines"
the <<express:geometry_schema.local_b_spline,local_b_spline>> functions in the second (stem:[v]) parameter direction from which the surface is defined. These functions refer to the **v_knots** list for their knot parameter values;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.v_b_splines.__note"
There may be some repetitions in the 2 lists of local_b_splines.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.u_knots"
the list of knot values for parameter stem:[u];
*)


(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.v_knots"
the list of knot values for parameter stem:[v];
*)


(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.control_points_list"
the list of control points. The **control_points_list** and consequently also the **u_b_splines**, the **v_b_splines** and **scaling_factors**, are ordered according to the knot values of the the combined B-spline coefficient constructed by multiplying corresponding univariate B-splines starting from the lowest knot value for each parameter. The knots in the v-parameter are the major sorting factor while the knots in the u-parameter the minor sorting factor. In case of ambiguities, the lists are sorted according to the upper knot value pair of the combined B-splines and the multiplicities of the first knots of the univariate B-splines.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.scaling_factors"
the list of scaling factors used to ensure that the non-zero B-spline basis functions add up to unity (partition of unity) at all points in the domain. Scaling factors not equal to 1.0 are sometimes needed for semi_standard_t_spline and lr_b_spline definitions to ensure that the collection of B-spline basis functions form a partition of unity. For analysis_suitable_t_spline and standard_t_spline definitions, partition of unity is achieved without use of scaling factors (i.e., the scaling factor is always equal to 1.0). For hierarchical_b_spline definitions, a scaling factor equal to 1.0 is used, although there is no partition of unity achieved.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.linearly_independent"
indicates whether this property has been tested for and in that case the result of the test; this is for information only;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.linearly_independent.__note"
The test is applied to the set of products of <<express:geometry_schema.local_b_spline,local_b_spline>>s used as coefficients of the control points . Not all types of locally refined surfaces are linearly independent by default.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.locally_refined_spline_type"
the type of the initial locally refined spline surface that provides rules for how the stored surface can be unpacked to its original format;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.self_intersect"
indication whether the surface is self-intersecting; this is for information only.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.surface_form"
indication of special surface types.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.u_closed"
indication whether the surface is closedin the stem:[u] direction; this is for information only;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.v_closed"
indication whether the surface is closedin the stem:[v] direction; this is for information only;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.domain"
the parameter domain corresponding to the surface. domain(1),(1) is the minimum parameter value in the stem:[u] direction; domain(1),(2) is the maximum parameter value in the stem:[u] direction; domain(2),(1) and domain (2),(2) gives the minimum and maximum parameter values in the stem:[v] direction. If all B-splines at the boundary have a knot multiplicity equal to the degree+1 at this boundary, the domain will coincide with the domain given by the minimum and maximum values in **u_knots** and **v_knots**. Otherwise, it will be coincide with a domain given by nearby knots depending on knot multiplicities.

the number of **u_b_splines** shall be equal to the number of control points;

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.wr:WR2"
the number of **v_b_splines** shall be equal to the number of control points;

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.wr:WR3"
the number of **scaling_factors** shall be equal to the number of control points;

(*"geometry_schema.locally_refined_spline_surface.wr:WR4"
all **scaling_factors** shall be positive and not greater than 1.0.

(*"geometry_schema.curve_bounded_surface"
A **curve_bounded_surface** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_surface,bounded_surface>>, and is a parametric surface with curved boundaries defined by one or more <<express:geometry_schema.boundary_curve,boundary_curve>>s or <<express:geometry_schema.degenerate_pcurve,degenerate_pcurve>>s. One of the <<express:geometry_schema.boundary_curve,boundary_curve>>s may be the outer boundary; any number of inner boundaries is permissible. The region of the **curve_bounded_surface** in the **basis_surface** is defined to be the portion of the basis surface in the direction of stem:[n xx t] from any point on the boundary, where stem:[n] is the surface normal and stem:[t] the boundary curve tangent vector at this point. (*"geometry_schema.rectangular_composite_surface"
A **rectangular_composite_surface** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_surface,bounded_surface>> composed of a rectangular array of **n_u** by **n_v** segments or patches. Each segment shall be finite and topologically rectangular (i.e., it corresponds to a rectangle in parameter space). The segment shall be either a <<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_surface,b_spline_surface>> or a <<express:geometry_schema.rectangular_trimmed_surface,rectangular_trimmed_surface>>. There shall be at least positional continuity between adjacent segments in both directions; the composite surface may be open or closed in the stem:[u] direction and open or closed in the stem:[v] direction.

For a particular segment stem:[S_{ij} = bb"segments" [i\][j\]]:

The preceding segment in the stem:[u] direction is stem:[S_{(i-1)j}] and the preceding segment in the stem:[v] direction is stem:[S_{i(j-1)}]; similarly for following segments.

If **segments[i][j].u_sense** is TRUE, the boundary of stem:[S_{ij}] where it adjoins stem:[S_{(i=1)j}] is that where the stem:[u] parameter (of the underlying bounded surface) is high.

If **segments[i][j].u_sense** is FALSE, it is at the low stem:[u] boundary; similarly for the **v_sense** indicator.

The stem:[u] parametrisation of stem:[S_{ij}] in the composite surface is from stem:[i-1] to stem:[i], mapped linearly from the parametrisation of the underlying bounded surface.

If stem:[U] is the stem:[u] parameter for the **rectangular_composite_surface** and stem:[u_{ij0} le u_{ij} ij le u_{ij1}], is the stem:[u] parameter for **segments[i][j]**, these parameters are related by the equations:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
U = (i - 1) + (u_{ij} - u_{ij0})/(u_{ij1} - u_{ij0}), u_{ij} = u_{ij0} + (U -(i-1))(u_{ij1} - u_{ij0}),
++++

if **segments[i][j].u_sense** = TRUE;

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
U = i - (u_{ij} - u_{ij0})/(u_{ij1} - u_{ij0}), u_{ij} = u_{ij0} - (U -i)(u_{ij1} - u_{ij0}),
++++

if **segments[i][j].u_sense** = FALSE.

The stem:[v] parametrisation is obtained in a similar way.

Thus the composite surface has parametric range 0 to **n_u**, 0 to **n_v**.

The degree of continuity of the joint between stem:[S_{ij}] and stem:[S_{(i+1)j}] is given by **segments[i][j].u_transition**.

For the last patch in a row stem:[S_{(n_u)j}] this may take the value **discontinuous**, if the composite surface is open in the stem:[u] direction; otherwise it is closed here, and the transition code relates to the continuity to stem:[S_{1j}]; similarly for **v_transition**. **discontinuous** shall not occur elsewhere in the **segments surface_patch** transition codes.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.rectangular_composite_surface.segments"
a rectangular array (represented by a list of list) of component surface patches. Each such patch contains information on the senses and transitions.

**segments[i][j].u_transition** refers to the state of continuity between **segments[i][j]** and **segments[i+1][j]**. The last column ({blank}**segments[n_u][j].u_transition**{blank}) may contain the value **discontinuous**, meaning that (that row of) the surface is not closed in the stem:[u] direction; the rest of the list shall not contain this value.

The last row ({blank}**segments[i][n_v].v_transition**{blank}) may contain the value **discontinuous**, meaning that (that column of) the surface is not closed in the stem:[v] direction; the rest of the list shall not contain this value.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.rectangular_composite_surface.n_u"
the number of surface oatches in the stem:[u] parameter direction;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.rectangular_composite_surface.n_v"
the number of surface oatches in the stem:[v] parameter direction.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.rectangular_composite_surface.wr:WR1"
Each sub-list in the **segments** list shall contain **n_v** <<express:geometry_schema.surface_patch,surface_patch>>es.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.rectangular_composite_surface.wr:WR2"
Other constraints on the segments (veriofied by <<express:geometry_schema.constraints_rectangular_composite_surface,constraints_rectangular_composite_surface>> function are:

that the component surfaces are all either rectangular trimmed surfaces or B-spline surfaces;

that the <<express:geometry_schema.transition_code,transition_code>>s in the **segments** list do not contain the value **discontinuous** except for the last row or column; when this occurs, it indicates that the surface is not closed in the appropriate direction.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.rectangular_composite_surface.wr:IP1"
The senses of the component surfaces are as specified in the <<express:geometry_schema.surface_patch.u_sense,u_sense>> and <<express:geometry_schema.surface_patch.v_sense,v_sense>> attributes of each element of **segments**.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_patch"
A **surface_patch** is a type of <<express:representation_schema.founded_item,founded_item>> and is a bounded surface with additional transition and sense information which is used to define a <<express:geometry_schema.rectangular_composite_surface,rectangular_composite_surface>>.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_patch.parent_surface"
the surface which defines the geometry and boundaries of the surface patch;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_patch.parent_surface.__note"
Since *surface_patch* is not a subtype of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>> the instance of <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_surface,bounded_surface>> used as *parent_surface* is not automatically associated with the <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_context,geometric_representation_context>> of the <<express:representation_schema.representation,representation>> using a <<express:geometry_schema.rectangular_composite_surface,rectangular_composite_surface>> containing this *surface_patch*. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the <<express:geometry_schema.bounded_surface,bounded_surface>> instance is explicitly included in a <<express:representation_schema.representation,representation>> with the appropriate <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_context,geometric_representation_context>>.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.surface_patch.u_transition"
the minimum state of geometric continuity along the second stem:[u] boundary of the patch as it joins the first stem:[u] boundary of its neighbour. In the case of the last patch, this defines the state of continuity between the first stem:[u] boundary and last stem:[u] boundary of the <<express:geometry_schema.rectangular_composite_surface,rectangular_composite_surface>>;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_patch.v_transition"
the minimum state of geometric continuity along the second stem:[v] boundary of the patch as it joins the first stem:[v] boundary of its neighbour. In the case of the last patch, this defines the state of continuity between the first stem:[v] boundary and last stem:[v] boundary of the <<express:geometry_schema.rectangular_composite_surface,rectangular_composite_surface>>;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_patch.u_sense"
the relationship between the sense (increasing parameter value) of the patch and the sense of the **parent_surface**. If **u_sense** is TRUE, the first stem:[u] boundary of the patch is the one where the parameter stem:[u] takes its lowest value; it is the highest value boundary if sense is FALSE.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_patch.v_sense"
the relationship between the sense (increasing parameter value) of the patch and the sense of the **parent_surface**. If **v_sense** is TRUE, the first stem:[v] boundary of the patch is the one where the parameter stem:[v] takes its lowest value; it is the highest value boundary if sense is FALSE.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_patch.using_surfaces"
the bag of <<express:geometry_schema.rectangular_composite_surface,rectangular_composite_surface>>s which use this **surface_patch** in their definition. This bag shall not be empty.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.surface_patch.wr:WR1"
A curve bounded surface shall not be used to define a surface patch.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_surface"
A **offset_surface** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.surface,surface>> and is a procedural definition of a simple offset surface at a normal distance from the originating surface. **distance** may be positive, negative or zero to indicate the preferred side of the surface. The positive side and the resultant offset surface are defined as follows:

Define unit tangent vectors of the base surface in the stem:[u] and stem:[v] directions; denote these by stem:[sigma_u] and stem:[sigma_v].

Take the cross product, stem:[N = sigma_u xx sigma_v], of these (which shall be linearly independent, or there is no offset surface).

stem:[N] shall be extended by continuity at singular points, if possible.

Normalise stem:[N] to get a unit normal (to the surface) vector.

Move the offset distance (which may be zero) along that vector to find the point on the offset surface.

The offset surface takes its parametrisation directly from that of the basis surface, corresponding points having identical parameter values. The **offset_surface** is parametrised as

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
sigma(u,v) = S(u,v) + dN.
++++

Where stem:[N] is the unit normal vector to the basis surface stem:[S (u,v)] at parameter values stem:[(u,v)], and stem:[d] is **distance**.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_surface.__note"
The definition allows the *offset_surface* to be self-intersecting.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.offset_surface.__note"
Care should be taken when using this entity to ensure that the offset distance never exceeds the radius of curvature in any direction at any point of the basis surface. In particular, the surface should not contain any ridge or singular point.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.offset_surface.basis_surface"
the surface that is to be offset;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_surface.distance"
the offset distance, which may be positive, negative or zero. A positive offset distance is measured in the direction of the surface normal;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.offset_surface.self_intersect"
a flag to indicate whether or not the surface is self-intersecting; this is for information only.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.oriented_surface"
A **oriented_surface** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.surface,surface>> for which the direction of the surface normal may be reversed.

The unit normal **N**, at any point on the **oriented_surface** is defined by the eqations:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
N (u,v) = ((del sigma)/(del  u) xx (del sigma)/(del v)), "if orientation = .TRUE.",
++++

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
N (u,v) = - ((del sigma)/(del  u) xx (del sigma)/(del v)), "if orientation = .FALSE.",
++++
*)


(*"geometry_schema.oriented_surface.__note"
An *oriented_surface* may be instantiated with other subtypes of surface. For example a complex instance of *oriented_surface*, with *orientation* = .FALSE., and *spherical_surface* defines a spherical surface with an inward pointing normal.
*)

(*"geometry_schema.oriented_surface.orientation"
a flag which indicates whether, or not, the direction of the surface normal is reversed.
*)

It is defined by referencing the parent surface and a transformation which gives the new position and possible scaling. The original surface is not affected. The geometric characteristics of the surface produced will be identical to that of the parent surface, but, where the transformation includes scaling, the size may differ.

(*"geometry_schema.volume"
A **volume** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.geometric_representation_item,geometric_representation_item>> that is a three dimensional solid of finite volume with a tri-parametric representation.

Each volume has a parametric representation
[stem%unnumbered]
++++
V(u,v,w)
++++

where stem:[u, v, w] are independent dimensionless parameters. For each stem:[(u,v,w)] within the parameter range:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
r = V(u,v,w),
++++

gives the coordinates of a point within the volume.
*)


(*"geometry_schema.volume.__note"

(*"geometry_schema.block_volume"
A **block_volume** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.volume,volume>> in the form of a solid rectangular parallelepiped, defined with a location and placement coordinate system.
The **block_volume** is specified by the positive lengths **x**, **y**, and **z** along the axes of the placement coordinate system, and has one vertex at the origin of the placement coordinate system.

The data is to be interpreted as follows:

[%key]
stem:[C]:: <<express:geometry_schema.placement.location,location>> (corner),
stem:[x]:: <<express:geometry_schema.block_volume.p,x>> (length),
stem:[y]:: <<express:geometry_schema.block_volume.p,y>> (depth),
stem:[z]:: <<express:geometry_schema.block_volume.p,z>> (height).

and the volume is parametrised as:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
V(u,v,w) = C + x + vdy + whz
++++

where the parametrisation range is stem:[0 le u le 1], stem:[0 le v le 1] , and stem:[0 le w le 1].
*)


(*"geometry_schema.block_volume.position"
the location and orientation of the axis system for the primitive. The block has one vertex at **position.location** and its edges aligned with the placement axes in the positive sense;
*)


(*"geometry_schema.block_volume.x"
the size of the block along the placement X axis, ({blank}**position.p[1]**{blank});
*)


(*"geometry_schema.block_volume.y"
the size of the block along the placement Y axis, ({blank}**position.p[2]**{blank});
*)


(*"geometry_schema.block_volume.z"
the size of the block along the placement Z axis, ({blank}**position.p[3]**{blank}).
*)


(*"geometry_schema.wedge_volume"
A **wedge_volume** is a type of <<express:geometry_schema.volume,volume>> which can be envisioned as the result of intersecting a block with a plane perpendicular to one of its faces. It is defined with a location and local coordinate system. A triangular/trapezoidal face lies in the plane defined by the placement X and Y axes. This face is defined by positive lengths **x** and **y** along the placement X and Y axes, by the length **ltx** (if non-zero) parallel to the X axis at a distance **y** from the placement origin, and by the line connecting the ends of the **x** and **ltx** segments.

The remainder of the wedge is specified by the positive length **z** along the placement Z axis which defines a distance through which the trapezoid or triangle is extruded. If **ltx** = 0, the wedge has five faces; otherwise, it has six faces.

The data is to be interpreted as follows:

[%key]
stem:[C]:: <<express:geometry_schema.placement.location,location>> (corner);
stem:[bb x]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[1]>>;
stem:[bb y]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[2]>>;
stem:[bb z]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[3]>>;
stem:[l]:: x ("length");
stem:[d]:: y ("depth");
stem:[h]:: z ("height");
stem:[l_{min}]:: ("length");

and the volume is parametrised as:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
V(u,v,w) = C + u((1 - v)l + vl_{min}) x + vdy + whz
++++

where the parametrisation range is stem:[0 le u le 1], stem:[0 le v le 1] , and stem:[0 le w le 1].
*)

The **eccentric_conical_volume** may have an elliptic cross section, and may have a central axis which is not perpendicular to the base. Depending upon the value of the **ratio** attribute it may be truncated, or may take the form of a generalised cylinder. When truncated the top face of the cone is parallel to the plane of the base and has a similar cross section.

stem:[C]:: <<express:geometry_schema.placement.location,location>>;

stem:[bb y]:: <<express:geometry_schema.axis2_placement_3d.p,p[2]>>;

stem:[o_y]:: <<express:geometry_schema.eccentric_conical_volume.y_offset,y_offset>>;
stem:[s]:: "ratio";

and the volume is parametrised as:

[stem%unnumbered]
++++
V(u,v,w) = C + v(o_{x}x + o_{y}y)+ w(1 + v(s - 1))( R_{1}((2 * pi * u))x + R_{2} (sin(2 * pi * u)y)) + vHz

(*"geometry_schema.eccentric_conical_volume.__note"
