.Example of datum and datum feature
====
image::example_of_datum_and_datum_feature.gif[]
====
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_modifier_with_value"
A **datum_reference_modifier_with_value** is an association between a **modifier_type** and a **modifier_value** that defines the specific boundary size of the associated feature for establishing a datum. In the case of a circular, cylindrical, or spherical boundary type the value represents the diameter of the boundary. In the case of a distance the value represents the distance between two parallel planes.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_modifier_with_value.__note"
When used for ASME Y14.5-2009 a *datum_reference_modifier_with_value* represents the datum feature simulator boundary.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_modifier_with_value.__note"
When used for ASME Y14.5-2018 a *datum_reference_modifier_with_value* represents the true geometric counterpart boundary.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_modifier_with_value.modifier_type"
specifies the role of the <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_modifier_type,datum_reference_modifier_type>> for the **datum_reference_modifier_with_value**.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_modifier_with_value.modifier_value"
specifies the role of the <<express:measure_schema.length_measure_with_unit,length_measure_with_unit>> for the **datum_reference_modifier_with_value**.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_modifier_with_value.wr:WR1"
The <<express:measure_schema.measure_with_unit.value_component,value_component>> shall be greater than zero.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.dimensional_location_with_datum_feature"
A **dimensional_location_with_datum_feature** is a type of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_feature,datum_feature>> and of <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location,dimensional_location>> that shall be used when the datum is established from two opposing <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>s that define a feature of size.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.dimensional_size_with_datum_feature"
A **dimensional_size_with_datum_feature** is a type of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_feature,datum_feature>> and of <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size,dimensional_size>>. The spatial characteristic provided is that of the <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_feature,datum_feature>> that is part of the **dimensional_size_with_datum_feature** itself.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.dimensional_size_with_datum_feature.wr:WR1"
The inherited attribute <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size.applies_to,applies_to>> shall specify the **dimensional_size_with_datum_feature** itself.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference"
A **datum_reference** is the specification of the use of a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum,datum>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference.__note"
The entity *datum_reference* is deprecated. For new implementations it is recommended that <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_system,datum_system>> together with <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_compartment,datum_reference_compartment>> and as needed <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_element,datum_reference_element>> be used.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference.precedence"
the priority that is assigned to a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum,datum>> for a specific use.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference.precedence.__note"
A <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum,datum>> may have multiple and distinct uses and have different *precedence* for each use.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference.referenced_datum"
the <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum,datum>> that participates in a geometrical tolerance of a product feature.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference.wr:WR1"
The value of **precedence** shall be greater than zero.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_compartment"
A **datum_reference_compartment** is a type of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.general_datum_reference,general_datum_reference>> that represents the compartment of either the primary, secondary or tertiary datum in a feature control frame.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_compartment.owner"
specifies an inverse relationship indicating that the existence of the **datum_reference_compartment** is dependent on the existence of the <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_system,datum_system>> that specifies the **datum_reference_compartment** as its <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_system.constituents,constituents>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_element"
A **datum_reference_element** is a type of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.general_datum_reference,general_datum_reference>> that represents a single datum reference of a common datum with a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_compartment,datum_reference_compartment>>. The rules governing common datum defined in ISO 5459, or ASME Y14.5-2009 or later editions of that standard shall apply.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_element.owner"
specifies an inverse relationship indicating that the existence of the **datum_reference_element** is dependent on the existence of the <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_compartment,datum_reference_compartment>> or <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_element,datum_reference_element>> that specifieds the **datum_reference_element** as its <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.general_datum_reference.base,base>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_element.wr:WR1"
The **owner** shall not be the same instance of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_element,datum_reference_element>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_element.wr:WR2"
The **owner** shall exist.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_element.wr:WR3"
The inherited attribute <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect.of_shape,of_shape>> of this and the owning instance shall refer to the same <<express:product_property_definition_schema.product_definition_shape,product_definition_shape>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_system"
A **datum_system** is a type of <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> that represents the ordered collection of one to three datum reference compartments within a geometric tolerance frame. A **datum_system** shall be used in accordance to the ISO 5459 definitions for single datum and datum system.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_system.__note"
Alternatively, *datum_system* can be used for the corresponding concept in ASME Y14.5-2009 or any later edition of this standard.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_system.__note"
A *datum_system* can be associated with a model coordinate system and can be shared by several <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance,geometric_tolerance>>s.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_system.constituents"
the ordered list of one to three <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_compartment,datum_reference_compartment>>s representing the primary and the optional secondary and tertiary datums of a tolerance frame.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_system.ur:UR1"
The combination of <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect.of_shape,of_shape>> and <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect.name,name>> shall be unique within a population of **datum_system**.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_system.wr:WR1"
A **datum_system** is not part of the physical boundary of the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.product_definition_shape,product_definition_shape>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target"
A **datum_target** is a type of <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> that indicates a datum target on the boundary of a product shape. The <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> may be a point, line, or an area. The **datum_target** is defined in addition to the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> elements that define the product shape.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.__note"
The use and application of datum targets is described in ISO 5459. Alternatively, *datum_target* can be used according to the specifications given in ASME Y14.5-2009 or later editions of that standard.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.target_id"
the name by which the identification of the datum target number is referred.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.target_basis_relationship"
the relationship to the <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum,datum>> that the **datum_target** defines; it is achieved through the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship,shape_aspect_relationship>>. There shall exist one or more <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship,shape_aspect_relationship>> for the **datum_target**.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.the_datum"
specifies the datum for which the target is a target.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.combined_datum_target_string"
specifies the string that is the concatenation of the datum identifier and the <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.target_id,target_id>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.ur:UR1"
No more than one **datum_target** shall have a specific <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.combined_datum_target_string,combined_datum_target_string>> in the context of a <<express:product_property_definition_schema.product_definition_shape,product_definition_shape>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.wr:WR1"
A **datum_target** shall be referenced by exactly one <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum,datum>> through a <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship,shape_aspect_relationship>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.wr:WR2"
A **datum_target** lies on the physical boundary of the shape that defines the product.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.wr:WR3"
The value of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.target_id,target_id>> shall be 1 or more.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.wr:WR4"
The name attribute inherited from <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> shall be a blank string.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_target.wr:WR5"
The description attribute inherited from <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> shall not be provided.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect"
A **derived_shape_aspect** is a type of <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> that depends on the definition of one or more specific shapes. The existence of the **derived_shape_aspect** depends on and relates to other <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>.

A **derived_shape_aspect** may be either an <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.apex,apex>> or a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.centre_of_symmetry,centre_of_symmetry>>, or a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_alignment,geometric_alignment>>, or a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_contact,geometric_contact>>, or a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_intersection,geometric_intersection>>, or a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.parallel_offset,parallel_offset>>, or a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.perpendicular_to,perpendicular_to>>, or an <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.extension,extension>>, or a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.tangent,tangent>>.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect.__example"
Consider the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> of a cylindrical hole. It is symmetric about an axis, and this axis exists only when the hole exists. The axis is a *derived_shape_aspect*.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect.__note"
A *derived_shape_aspect* might not be on the physical boundary of the product. Its intended purpose is to relate product dimensions and tolerances with the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> or features of the part.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect.deriving_relationships"
the identification of <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship,shape_aspect_relationship>> that define the **derived_shape_aspect**. There shall exist one or more <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship,shape_aspect_relationship>> for the **derived_shape_aspect**.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.extension"
An **extension** is a type of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect,derived_shape_aspect>> that corresponds to the extension of a curve or surface <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> element.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.extension.__example"
Consider the rounded edge of a block as shown in figure 5. To define the square corner at this edge, the two adjacent faces are extended until they intersect. Each of these is an *extension*.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.extension.wr:WR1"
There shall be one member in the set of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect.deriving_relationships,deriving_relationships>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.face_surface_shape_aspect"
A **face_surface_shape_aspect** is a type of <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> that provides the identification for a <<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>> in the context of a <<express:product_definition_schema.product_definition,product_definition>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.face_surface_shape_aspect.wr:WR1"
The context for the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> shall be a <<express:product_definition_schema.product_definition,product_definition>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.face_surface_shape_aspect.wr:WR2"
The **face_surface_shape_aspect** shall be on the surface of the product.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.face_surface_shape_aspect.wr:IP1"
A **face_surface_shape_aspect** shall be the identification of a <<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>> in a geometric model of the product.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.face_surface_shape_aspect.wr:IP2"
A **face_surface_shape_aspect** shall not be in a complex instance with any other subtype of <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.feature_definition"
A **feature_definition** is a type of <<express:product_property_definition_schema.characterized_object,characterized_object>> that is a preconceived form pattern.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.general_datum_reference"
A **general_datum_reference** is a type of <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> that represents the occurrence of a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum,datum>> within a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_system,datum_system>>. A **general_datum_reference** is either a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_compartment,datum_reference_compartment>> or a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_element,datum_reference_element>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.general_datum_reference.base"
specifies the used <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum,datum>> or <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.common_datum_list,common_datum_list>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.general_datum_reference.modifiers"
specifies the role of the <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_modifier,datum_reference_modifier>> for the **general_datum_reference**. There shall exist more than one <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_modifier,datum_reference_modifier>> for the **general_datum_reference**. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.general_datum_reference.ur:UR1"
The combination of <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect.of_shape,of_shape>> and <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect.name,name>> shall be unique within a population of **general_datum_reference**.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.general_datum_reference.wr:WR1"
The <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect.name,name>> shall be an empty string.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.general_datum_reference.wr:WR2"
The <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect.description,description>> shall not be populated.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.general_datum_reference.wr:WR3"
The <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect.id,id>> shall not be populated.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.general_datum_reference.wr:WR4"
A **general_datum_reference** is not part of the physical boundary of the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.product_definition_shape,product_definition_shape>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.general_datum_reference.wr:WR5"
If **base** is a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum,datum>> the inherited attribute <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect.of_shape,of_shape>> of this instance and base shall refer to the same <<express:product_property_definition_schema.product_definition_shape,product_definition_shape>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.general_datum_reference.wr:WR6"
If **base** is a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.common_datum_list,common_datum_list>> the inherited attribute <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect.of_shape,of_shape>> of this instance and the first element of base shall refer to the same <<express:product_property_definition_schema.product_definition_shape,product_definition_shape>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_alignment"
A **geometric_alignment** is a type of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect,derived_shape_aspect>> that defines a planar or linear feature that requires two or more features lying in the same plane or along the same line.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_alignment.wr:WR1"
There shall be two or more elements in the set of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect.deriving_relationships,deriving_relationships>>.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_alignment.wr:WR1.__figure"
[[figure-shape_aspect_definition_schema-fig_geometric_alignment]]
.Geometric alignment
====
image::geometric_alignment.gif[]
====
*)
(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_alignment.wr:WR1.__example"
Figure 4 illustrates an axis of a cylinder as a linear feature and the face of a cutout as a planar feature. When two or more aligned parallel axes are used for the purpose of dimensioning, a plane may be established to which a dimension is attached, as shown in figure 4.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_contact"
A **geometric_contact** is a type of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect,derived_shape_aspect>> that represents the common contact region between two <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>s. The involved <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>s shall not intersect with each other.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_contact.wr:WR1"
There shall be exactly two members in the set of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect.deriving_relationships,deriving_relationships>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_intersection"
A **geometric_intersection** is a type of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect,derived_shape_aspect>> that is the common intersection of two or more <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> elements.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_intersection.__figure"
[[figure-shape_aspect_definition_schema-fig_geometric_intersection]]
.Geometric intersection
====
image::geometric_intersection.gif[]
====
*)
(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_intersection.__example"
A *geometric_intersection* is established by the intersection of two planar extensions from the adjacent sides of the block. This *geometric_intersection* may be used as the participating <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> in dimensioning the location of the right or bottom planar surfaces as shown in figure 5.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_intersection.__note"
Since a *geometric_intersection* is a derived shape, the use of intersection here is independent of any specific representation.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_intersection.wr:WR1"
There shall be two or more members in the set of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect.deriving_relationships,deriving_relationships>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.geometric_intersection.wr:IP1"
The <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>s that participate as <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship.relating_shape_aspect,relating_shape_aspect>> shall intersect.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.instanced_feature"
An **instanced_feature** is a type of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.feature_definition,feature_definition>> and of a <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> that is the identification of a preconceived form pattern on a <<express:product_definition_schema.product_definition,product_definition>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.instanced_feature.wr:WR1"
The **instanced_feature** shall be an aspect of the shape of a <<express:product_definition_schema.product_definition,product_definition>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.instanced_feature.wr:WR2"
A **instanced_feature** shall lie on the physical boundary of the shape that defines the product.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.parallel_offset"
A **parallel_offset** is a type of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect,derived_shape_aspect>> that is located at a constant distance from a <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship.related_shape_aspect,related_shape_aspect>>. If the basis is two dimensional, then all associated <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> elements (the parallel offset and the basis shape aspect) lie in some common plane. If the basis is a surface, then all <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> elements are embedded in three-dimensional space.

The **parallel_offset** is formed by the offset of each point of the basis, in a direction perpendicular to the basis by the offset distance (See figure 6).
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.parallel_offset.__figure"
[[figure-shape_aspect_definition_schema-fig_parallel_offset]]
.Parallel offset
====
image::parallel_offset.gif[]
====
*)
(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.parallel_offset.__example"
Figure 6 is a partial view of apart; not all details are shown. The <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> is the basis <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship.related_shape_aspect,related_shape_aspect>> for the parallel-offset. The *offset* is the distance the *parallel_offset* is positioned from its basis.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.parallel_offset.__note"
The basis shape aspect of a surface divides the space in which it is embedded into two half-spaces.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.parallel_offset.offset"
the distance between the **parallel_offset** and its basis.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.parallel_offset.wr:WR1"
There shall be one member in the set of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect.deriving_relationships,deriving_relationships>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.perpendicular_to"
A **perpendicular_to** is a type of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect,derived_shape_aspect>> that is oriented orthogonally to another <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.perpendicular_to.__note"
The *perpendicular_to* need not intersect the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> from which it is established.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.perpendicular_to.wr:WR1"
There shall be one member in the set of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect.deriving_relationships,deriving_relationships>>.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.referenced_modified_datum"
A **referenced_modified_datum** is a type of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference,datum_reference>> where the referenced datum may vary within the specified limits of size.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.referenced_modified_datum.__note"
A <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum,datum>> may be modified if the <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_feature,datum_feature>> that produced it is a product feature which has size characteristics.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.referenced_modified_datum.__note"
The use and application of a modified <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum,datum>> are described in ISO 2692.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.referenced_modified_datum.__note"
The entity *referenced_modified_datum* is deprecated. For new implementations it is recommended that <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_compartment,datum_reference_compartment>> or <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference_element,datum_reference_element>> be used.
*)

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.referenced_modified_datum.modifier"

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.shape_aspect_deriving_relationship"

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.shape_aspect_deriving_relationship.__note"

The <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship.related_shape_aspect,related_shape_aspect>> are the other <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> that are the basis for the <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect,derived_shape_aspect>>.

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.shape_aspect_deriving_relationship.relating_shape_aspect"
an attribute inherited from the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship,shape_aspect_relationship>> shall be redeclared as the <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.derived_shape_aspect,derived_shape_aspect>> for the **shape_aspect_deriving_relationship**.
*)


(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.shape_representation_with_parameters"

(*"shape_aspect_definition_schema.shape_representation_with_parameters.items"
an attribute inherited from the <<express:representation_schema.representation,representation>> shall be redeclared as the <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.shape_representation_with_parameters_items,shape_representation_with_parameters_items>> for the **shape_representation_with_parameters**. SCHEMA shape_dimension_schema '{iso standard 10303 part(47) version(5) object(1) shape-dimension-schema(2)}';

REFERENCE FROM basic_attribute_schema -- ISO 10303-41
  (get_id_value,
  id_attribute,
  id_attribute_select);

REFERENCE FROM geometry_schema (  -- ISO 10303-42
       cartesian_point,
       geometric_representation_item,
       line,
       placement);

REFERENCE FROM measure_schema   -- ISO 10303-41
  (measure_with_unit);

REFERENCE FROM product_property_definition_schema   -- ISO 10303-41
  (shape_aspect,
   shape_aspect_relationship);

REFERENCE FROM product_property_representation_schema   -- ISO 10303-41
  (item_identified_representation_usage_definition,
   shape_representation);

REFERENCE FROM qualified_measure_schema   -- ISO 10303-45
  (descriptive_representation_item,
   measure_representation_item,
   qualified_representation_item);

REFERENCE FROM representation_schema   -- ISO 10303-43
  (representation,
   compound_representation_item,
   using_representations);

REFERENCE FROM shape_aspect_definition_schema  -- ISO 10303-47
  (face_surface_shape_aspect,
   surface_shape_aspect);

REFERENCE FROM shape_tolerance_schema  -- ISO 10303-47
  (geometric_tolerance);

REFERENCE FROM support_resource_schema   -- ISO 10303-41
  (identifier,
   label,
   text);

REFERENCE FROM topology_schema  -- ISO 10303-42
   (edge_curve,
   vertex_point);

TYPE sd_id_attribute_select = SELECT BASED_ON id_attribute_select WITH (
    dimensional_size);
END_TYPE;

TYPE angle_relator = ENUMERATION OF
   (equal,
    large,
    small);
END_TYPE;

TYPE dimensional_characteristic = SELECT
   (dimensional_location,
    dimensional_size);
END_TYPE;

TYPE dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint_type = ENUMERATION OF
   (uniform_thickness_cone_cone, --coaxial having same apex angle having different apexes and different material senses.
    uniform_thickness_cylinder_cylinder, --coaxial features having different diameters and different material senses.
    uniform_thickness_face_surface_face_surface, -- face_surfaces on opposing surfaces of a body.
    uniform_thickness_plane_plane, -- planes on opposing surfaces of a body.
    uniform_thickness_revolute_revolute, -- coaxial features having same circle diameter delta in any cross section and different material senses.
    uniform_thickness_sphere_sphere, --concentric features having different diameters and different material senses.
    uniform_thickness_surface_surface, -- generic opposing surfaces of a body.
    uniform_thickness_torus_torus); -- coaxial and concentric features having same small diameter and different material senses.
END_TYPE;

TYPE sds_item_identified_representation_usage_definition = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT BASED_ON item_identified_representation_usage_definition WITH
   (dimensional_size);
END_TYPE;

TYPE shape_dimension_representation_item = SELECT
   (compound_representation_item,
    descriptive_representation_item,
    measure_representation_item,
    placement);
END_TYPE;

TYPE surface_or_face_surface_shape_aspect = SELECT
    (face_surface_shape_aspect,
     surface_shape_aspect);
END_TYPE;

ENTITY angular_location
  SUBTYPE OF (dimensional_location);
  angle_selection : angle_relator;
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY angular_size
  SUBTYPE OF (dimensional_size);
  angle_selection : angle_relator;
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY dimensional_characteristic_representation;
  dimension : dimensional_characteristic;
  representation : shape_dimension_representation;
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY dimensional_location
  SUPERTYPE OF (ONEOF (angular_location,
                       dimensional_location_with_path))
  SUBTYPE OF (shape_aspect_relationship);
WHERE
  WR1: SELF\shape_aspect_relationship.relating_shape_aspect :<>: SELF\shape_aspect_relationship.related_shape_aspect;
  WR2: SELF\shape_aspect_relationship.relating_shape_aspect.of_shape :=: SELF\shape_aspect_relationship.related_shape_aspect.of_shape;
  WR3: (SELF\shape_aspect_relationship.relating_shape_aspect\shape_aspect.product_definitional <> UNKNOWN)
        AND
       (SELF\shape_aspect_relationship.related_shape_aspect\shape_aspect.product_definitional <> UNKNOWN);
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY dimensional_location_with_path
  SUBTYPE OF (dimensional_location);
  path : shape_aspect;
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint
  SUBTYPE OF (directed_dimensional_location);
  classification : dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint_type;
  SELF\shape_aspect_relationship.relating_shape_aspect RENAMED surface1 : surface_or_face_surface_shape_aspect;
  SELF\shape_aspect_relationship.related_shape_aspect RENAMED surface2 : surface_or_face_surface_shape_aspect;
INVERSE
 associated_geometric_tolerance : SET [0:0] OF geometric_tolerance FOR toleranced_shape_aspect;
WHERE
 WR1 : TYPEOF(surface1) = TYPEOF(surface2);
 WR2 : surface1 :<>: surface2;
END_ENTITY;
--IP1:
--IP2:
--IP3:
--IP4:
--IP5:
--IP6:
--IP7:
--IP8:

ENTITY dimensional_size
  SUPERTYPE OF (ONEOF (angular_size,
                       dimensional_size_with_path));
  applies_to : shape_aspect;
  name : label;
 DERIVE
  id : identifier := get_id_value(SELF);
UNIQUE
  UR1: id, applies_to;
WHERE
  WR1: applies_to\shape_aspect.product_definitional = TRUE;
  WR2: SIZEOF(USEDIN(SELF, 'BASIC_ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.' + 'ID_ATTRIBUTE.IDENTIFIED_ITEM')) <= 1;
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY dimensional_size_with_path
  SUBTYPE OF (dimensional_size);
  path : shape_aspect;
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY directed_dimensional_location
  SUBTYPE OF (dimensional_location);
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY independent_limits_of_linear_dimensional_size_characteristic_representation
SUBTYPE OF (dimensional_characteristic_representation);
    SELF\dimensional_characteristic_representation.dimension : dimensional_size;
    limits : LIST  [2:?] OF UNIQUE shape_dimension_representation;
WHERE
WR1:SIZEOF(['SHAPE_DIMENSION_SCHEMA.ANGULAR_SIZE', 'SHAPE_DIMENSION_SCHEMA.DIMENSIONAL_SIZE_WITH_PATH'] * TYPEOF(dimension)) =0;
--IP1:
--IP2:
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY shape_dimension_representation
  SUBTYPE OF (shape_representation);
  SELF\representation.items : SET[1:?] OF shape_dimension_representation_item;
END_ENTITY;

END_SCHEMA;  -- shape_dimension_schema

(*"shape_dimension_schema"
// Note schema EXPRESS are in ..\resources\resource_name name_of_schema.xml

The *shape_dimension_schema* provides a representation for the description of location and size dimensions. The measure of a dimension may be either assigned to or derived from other *shape_aspect* elements. The supported types of measurement path for applying a dimension are:

* a linear path;
* a curved path;
* an angular path.

*)
(*"shape_dimension_schema.__fund_cons"

Dimensions that are derived from the geometric representations of **shape_aspect**s are considered to be implicitly defined. Dimensions that are assigned to a *shape_aspect*, which may or may not have associated geometric representation, are considered to be explicitly defined. A size or location dimension may be both implicitly and explicitly defined for a given *shape_aspect*.

[NOTE]
--
The lower limit of a limit dimension can be represented by either an explicit or assigned, dimension, while the upper limit value may be on an implicit or explicit dimension.
--

[NOTE]
--
Legal values that are computer sensible for attributes of entities in this schema may be specified in application protocols.
--

This document does not distinguish between intended values and actual values for either dimensions or tolerances. Geometrical tolerances and plus-minus tolerances may be applied to a dimension. Dimensions need not have a tolerance value.

This document does not distinguish between uses of dimensions. Uses of dimensions are defined in application protocols using this document.

[example]
====
One instance of a dimension defines a portion of the as-designed product shape. A second instance of a dimension describes a portion of the as-manufactured product shape.
====

This document provides for the representation of dimensions in a manner that is independent of any requirements for draughting presentation.

[NOTE]
--
The application and use of basic dimensions or reference dimensions are specified in an application protocol.
--

A *dimensional_location* is a relationship between two *shape_aspect* elements that identifies a spatial constraint that shall be maintained during any physical transformation, translation, or rotation of the *shape_aspect* elements together. This relationship is either directed from the origin *shape_aspect* or *datum* to the target *shape_aspect*, or it is non-directed. Only non-directed dimensional location is addressed in document.

[NOTE]
--
The decision as to whether the *dimensional_location* is directed or non-directed is specified in an application protocol.
--

A *dimensional_size* of a *shape_aspect* identifies a constraint between the relative position of the boundary of the *shape_aspect* with either its axis of symmetry or another boundary of the same *shape_aspect*. The *dimensional_size* is unaffected by any translation or rotation of the *shape_aspect*.

A dimension is applied along a specific measuring path. When the measuring path is not explicitly identified, the dimension will apply along an implicit path. The definition of an implicit measuring path is dependent on the context of use and is specified in an application protocol.

Unless otherwise specified dimensions shall be interpreted in accordance with ISO 8015, ISO/TS 17450-1, ISO 17450-2, ISO 14405-1 and ISO 14405-2.

[NOTE]
--
Alternatively dimensions can be used according to the specifications given in ASME Y14.5-2009 [11].
--

// EXPRESS-G

*)

A **dimensional_location** is a type of <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship,shape_aspect_relationship>>. A **dimensional_location** specifies that a spatial constraint exists between two <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> elements that are represented as a non-directed measure applied along a measurement path. A **dimensional_location** may be either an <<express:shape_dimension_schema.angular_location,angular_location>> or a <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_path,dimensional_location_with_path>>.

Representation of a <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> participating in the *dimensional_location* relationship implies a measuring direction for the *dimensional_location* through the related and relating <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>. The meaning of the direction is specified in an application protocol.
*)

(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location.__note"
The application and use of *dimensional_location* and <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size,dimensional_size>> are shown in figure 18.

(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location.wr:WR2"

(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_path"
A **dimensional_location_with_path** is a type of <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location,dimensional_location>>. A **dimensional_location_with_path** specifies that a spatial constraint exists between two <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> elements along an explicit path. The **dimensional_location_with_path** is a <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location,dimensional_location>> applied along an explicit path that is defined between the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> elements.
*)

The location of hole H2 from hole H1 may be defined with either <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location,dimensional_location>>, X1 and Y1 or, *dimensional_location_with_path*, D1. <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location,dimensional_location>> X1 and Y1 use implicit measuring paths defined by a coordinate system associated with the product. A *dimensional_location_with_path* applies along the explicit measuring path defined by the line intersecting the centres of the 2 holes.
*)

(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_path.path"
the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> defining the measurement path for the dimension.

(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint"
A **dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint** is a type of <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location,dimensional_location>>. A **dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint** specifies that the direction of the dimension is normal to the surfaces.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.classification"
an indication of the specific thickness feature type.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.surface1"
specifies the surface that is the origin for the **dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint**.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.surface2"
specifies the surface that is the target for the **dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint**.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.associated_geometric_tolerance"
an inverse relationship where the existence of **dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint** is depend on the existence of <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance,geometric_tolerance>> that specifies the **dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint** as its <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance.toleranced_shape_aspect,toleranced_shape_aspect>>. There should be no <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance,geometric_tolerance>> for this **dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint**.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.wr:WR1"
The type of **surface1** and the type of **surface2** shall be the same.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.wr:WR2"
The members of **surface1** and **surface2** shall be different.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.wr:IP1"
The dot product of the measurement vector and the normal vector to **surface1** at the measurement location shall be -1, under the conditions that the vectors are unit length.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.wr:IP2"
The measurement geometry shall be a straight line starting at **surface1** and terminating on **surface2**.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.wr:IP3"
The members of **surface1** and **surface2** are on opposing faces of the solid.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.wr:IP4"
When the solid is revolute, the **surface1** shall be the identification of a <<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>> or <<express:topology_schema.connected_face_sub_set,connected_face_sub_set>> whose elements are all in the domain of the outer surface of the solid.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.wr:IP5"
When the solid is revolute, the **surface2** shall be the identification of a <<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>> or <<express:topology_schema.connected_face_sub_set,connected_face_sub_set>> whose elements are all in the domain of the inner surface of the solid.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.wr:IP6"
When the solid is revolute, the surface2 shall be the identification of a face_surface or connected_face_subset whose elements are all in the domain of the inner surface of the solid.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.wr:IP7"
The type of **surface1** and of **surface2** shall be consistent with the type specified in **classification**.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint.wr:IP8"
The **dimensional_location_with_normal_constraint** shall not be any other subtype of <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location,dimensional_location>>.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size"
A **dimensional_size** is a spatial characteristic of a <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> that is represented by a measure. This magnitude is independent of the location of the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> on or within the product. A **dimensional_size** may be either an <<express:shape_dimension_schema.angular_size,angular_size>> or a <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size_with_path,dimensional_size_with_path>>.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size.name"
the identification of the application use of the dimension.
*)

(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size.name.__example"
A size characteristic may be either a radius, a diameter, a length constraint, an angular constraint, a curve <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>, an axisymmetric <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>, or a circular <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>. Use of the *name* attribute with a value of "radius" clarifies the application use of this dimension.
*)

(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size.applies_to"
the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> being dimensioned.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size.id"
the <<express:support_resource_schema.identifier,identifier>> that distinguishes the **dimensional_size**.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size.wr:WR1"
A **dimensional_size** shall lie on the physical boundary of the shape that defines the product.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size.wr:WR2"
Each **dimensional_size** shall be the <<express:basic_attribute_schema.id_attribute.identified_item,identified_item>> in at most one <<express:basic_attribute_schema.id_attribute,id_attribute>>.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size.ur:UR1"
The id shall be unique for the applied <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size_with_path"
A **dimensional_size_with_path** is a type of <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size,dimensional_size>>. A **dimensional_size_with_path** defines a spatial characteristic of a <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>. A **dimensional_size_with_path** is represented by a single magnitude and is independent of the location of the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> on or within the product. It is the non-directed measure derived along an explicit curve path that is defined between the two boundaries of the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size_with_path.path"
the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> defining the measurement path for the dimension.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.directed_dimensional_location"
A **directed_dimensional_location** is a type of <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location,dimensional_location>> that shall be measured from the origin, given by <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship.relating_shape_aspect,relating_shape_aspect>>, to the target, given by <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship.related_shape_aspect,related_shape_aspect>>.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.shape_dimension_representation"
A **shape_dimension_representation** is a type of <<express:product_property_representation_schema.shape_representation,shape_representation>>. A **shape_dimension_representation** is a representation of either <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location,dimensional_location>> or <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size,dimensional_size>>. It is a representation that explicitly describes a dimension of a <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> with either a value or a range of values and needed specification modifiers. Unless otherwise specified the values and specification modifiers shall be used in accordance with ISO/TS 17450-2, ISO 14405-1, and ISO 14405-2.

A <<express:product_property_representation_schema.shape_representation,shape_representation>> may have many <<express:representation_schema.representation_item,representation_item>>, but two of the <<express:representation_schema.representation_item,representation_item>> shall define a specific **shape_dimension_representation**. Unless otherwise specified upper and lower limits of dimensions shall be used in accordance with ISO 129-1.
*)

(*"shape_dimension_schema.shape_dimension_representation.__example"
A cylindrical <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> is prescribed to have a diameter of 10 centimetres. This specification, "10cm diameter", is a *shape_dimension_representation* that defines a size characteristic of the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> without requiring a geometric representation.
*)
(*"shape_dimension_schema.shape_dimension_representation.__example"
The diameter of a hole is defined to allow a physical instance of the hole to vary between 2.00 cm and 2.01 cm. In the product description, the lower and upper allowable diameters of the hole are represented by a 2.00 cm, geometric cylinder, and another representation item with a value of 2.01 cm.
*)

(*"shape_dimension_schema.shape_dimension_representation.items"
an attribute inherited from the <<express:product_property_representation_schema.shape_representation,shape_representation>> shall be redeclared as the <<express:shape_dimension_schema.shape_dimension_representation_item,shape_dimension_representation_item>> for the **shape_dimension_representation**. There shall exist at least one <<express:shape_dimension_schema.shape_dimension_representation_item,shape_dimension_representation_item>> for the **shape_dimension_representation**.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.shape_dimension_representation.wr:WR1"
The <<express:representation_schema.representation_item,representation_item>> in the set of items for a **shape_dimension_representation** shall be of type <<express:qualified_measure_schema.measure_representation_item,measure_representation_item>>.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.shape_dimension_representation.wr:WR2"
There shall be at most two <<express:representation_schema.representation_item,representation_item>> in the set of items for a **shape_dimension_representation**.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.shape_dimension_representation.wr:WR3"
The <<express:measure_schema.measure_with_unit.value_component,value_component>> of the <<express:representation_schema.representation_item,representation_item>> in the set of items for a **shape_dimension_representation** shall be a positive real number.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.independent_limits_of_linear_dimensional_size_characteristic_representation"
An **independent_limits_of_linear_dimensional_size_characteristic_representation** is a type of **dimensional_characteristic_representation** that suppors size dimensions and that provides independent properties of a sequence of limits of size to support use cases where predefined explicit data structure is infeasible. It removes the limitation in the **dimensional_characteristic_representation** that only a pair of values is supported by providing a separate list mechanism.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.independent_limits_of_linear_dimensional_size_characteristic_representation.dimension"
specifies the dimensional_size for which data is provided.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.independent_limits_of_linear_dimensional_size_characteristic_representation.limits"
specifies the values for the limits.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.independent_limits_of_linear_dimensional_size_characteristic_representation.wr:WR1"
A dimensional_size_with_path shall not be provided in the role of dimension.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.independent_limits_of_linear_dimensional_size_characteristic_representation.wr:IP1"
If there are only two elements in the list, the first element in the list shall be interpreted as the lower limit.
*)


(*"shape_dimension_schema.independent_limits_of_linear_dimensional_size_characteristic_representation.wr:IP2"
If there are only two elements in the list, the second element in the list shall be interpreted as the upper limit.
*)

  indicated_datum : datum := SELF\tolerance_zone_with_datum.datum_reference\datum_system.constituents[1]\general_datum_reference.base;
WHERE

  WR2 : 'SHAPE_ASPECT_DEFINITION_SCHEMA.DATUM' IN TYPEOF(indicated_datum);
  WR3: (width_direction <> direction_feature_application_type.inclined) XOR EXISTS(angle);
  WR4: SELF\tolerance_zone.form\tolerance_zone_form.name IN [
            'between two coaxial cylinders',

ENTITY geometric_tolerance
  ABSTRACT SUPERTYPE OF (geometric_tolerance_with_datum_reference
                         ANDOR geometric_tolerance_with_defined_unit
                        ANDOR ONEOF (geometric_tolerance_with_modifiers,
                             modified_geometric_tolerance)
                      ANDOR unequally_disposed_geometric_tolerance
                     ANDOR ONEOF (cylindricity_tolerance,
                          flatness_tolerance,
                          line_profile_tolerance,
                          position_tolerance,
                          roundness_tolerance,
                          straightness_tolerance,
                          surface_profile_tolerance));
  name : label;
  description : OPTIONAL text;
  magnitude : OPTIONAL length_measure_with_unit;
  toleranced_shape_aspect : geometric_tolerance_target;
DERIVE
  controlling_shape : product_definition_shape := sts_get_product_definition_shape(toleranced_shape_aspect);
    id : identifier := get_id_value(SELF);
INVERSE
	auxiliary_classification : SET [0:?] OF geometric_tolerance_auxiliary_classification FOR described_item;
	tolerance_relationship   : SET [0:?] OF geometric_tolerance_relationship for relating_geometric_tolerance;
UNIQUE
  UR1: id, controlling_shape;
WHERE
  WR1: magnitude\measure_with_unit.value_component >= 0.0;
  WR2: EXISTS(controlling_shape);
  WR3: NOT ('PRODUCT_PROPERTY_DEFINITION_SCHEMA.SHAPE_ASPECT_RELATIONSHIP' IN TYPEOF(toleranced_shape_aspect))
       OR (toleranced_shape_aspect\shape_aspect_relationship.relating_shape_aspect.of_shape :=:
            toleranced_shape_aspect\shape_aspect_relationship.related_shape_aspect.of_shape);
  WR4: SIZEOF(USEDIN(SELF, 'BASIC_ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.' + 'ID_ATTRIBUTE.IDENTIFIED_ITEM')) <= 1;
  WR5: SIZEOF(QUERY( tr <* tolerance_relationship | tr.name = 'composite tolerance')) <= 1;
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY geometric_tolerance_auxiliary_classification;
 attribute_value : geometric_tolerance_auxiliary_classification_enum;
 described_item : geometric_tolerance;
 END_ENTITY;

ENTITY geometric_tolerance_relationship;
  name : label;
  description : text;
  relating_geometric_tolerance : geometric_tolerance;
  related_geometric_tolerance : geometric_tolerance;
 WHERE
  WR1: NOT(name = 'composite tolerance') OR
       (('SHAPE_TOLERANCE_SCHEMA.POSITION_TOLERANCE' IN TYPEOF(relating_geometric_tolerance)) AND
        ('SHAPE_TOLERANCE_SCHEMA.POSITION_TOLERANCE' IN TYPEOF(related_geometric_tolerance))) OR
       (('SHAPE_TOLERANCE_SCHEMA.LINE_PROFILE_TOLERANCE' IN TYPEOF(relating_geometric_tolerance)) AND
        ('SHAPE_TOLERANCE_SCHEMA.LINE_PROFILE_TOLERANCE' IN TYPEOF(related_geometric_tolerance))) OR
       (('SHAPE_TOLERANCE_SCHEMA.SURFACE_PROFILE_TOLERANCE' IN TYPEOF(relating_geometric_tolerance)) AND
        ('SHAPE_TOLERANCE_SCHEMA.SURFACE_PROFILE_TOLERANCE' IN TYPEOF(related_geometric_tolerance)));
--description   b) For a geometric_tolerance_relationship with the name "composite tolerance"
--             the related and the relating subtype should be both either position_tolerance or line_profile_tolerance or surface_profile_tolerance

 WR2: NOT(name = 'composite tolerance') OR
  (relating_geometric_tolerance\geometric_tolerance.toleranced_shape_aspect :=:
  related_geometric_tolerance\geometric_tolerance.toleranced_shape_aspect);
--description c) For a geometric_tolerance_relationship with the name "composite tolerance"
--            the the related and relating geometric_tolerances shall refer to the same target.

 WR3: acyclic_geometric_tolerance_relationship(SELF, [related_geometric_tolerance],
       'SHAPE_TOLERANCE_SCHEMA.GEOMETRIC_TOLERANCE');
--The geometric_tolerance_relationship structure shall be acylic.
END_ENTITY;

ENTITY geometric_tolerance_with_datum_reference

  SUBTYPE OF (geometric_tolerance_with_defined_unit);
  area_type : area_unit_type;
  second_unit_size : OPTIONAL length_or_plane_angle_measure_with_unit_select;
WHERE
  WR1: NOT (EXISTS(second_unit_size) XOR (area_type IN [area_unit_type.rectangular, area_unit_type.cylindrical, area_unit_type.spherical]));
  WR2: NOT(area_type = area_unit_type.cylindrical)
	   OR  ('MEASURE_SCHEMA.LENGTH_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT' IN TYPEOF(SELF\geometric_tolerance_with_defined_unit.unit_size))
	   AND ('MEASURE_SCHEMA.PLANE_ANGLE_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT' IN TYPEOF(second_unit_size));
  WR3: NOT (area_type =  area_unit_type.rectangular)
       OR ('MEASURE_SCHEMA.LENGTH_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT' IN TYPEOF(SELF\geometric_tolerance_with_defined_unit.unit_size))
	   AND ('MEASURE_SCHEMA.LENGTH_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT' IN TYPEOF(second_unit_size));
  WR4: NOT(area_type = area_unit_type.spherical)
	   OR  ('MEASURE_SCHEMA.PLANE_ANGLE_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT' IN TYPEOF(SELF\geometric_tolerance_with_defined_unit.unit_size))
	   AND ('MEASURE_SCHEMA.PLANE_ANGLE_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT' IN TYPEOF(second_unit_size));
  WR5: NOT(area_type =  area_unit_type.spherical)
	   OR  (SIZEOF(QUERY (tz <* USEDIN(SELF,'SHAPE_TOLERANCE_SCHEMA.TOLERANCE_ZONE.DEFINING_TOLERANCE') |
	       ('SHAPE_TOLERANCE_SCHEMA.ORIENTED_TOLERANCE_ZONE' IN TYPEOF(tz))
	       )) <> 0 );

  WR2: (maximum_upper_tolerance\measure_with_unit.unit_component = SELF\geometric_tolerance.magnitude\measure_with_unit.unit_component) AND (maximum_upper_tolerance\measure_with_unit.value_component > SELF\geometric_tolerance.magnitude\measure_with_unit.value_component);

ENTITY geometric_tolerance_with_modifiers
  SUBTYPE OF (geometric_tolerance);
  modifiers : SET[1:?] OF geometric_tolerance_modifier;
WHERE
  WR1: NOT (geometric_tolerance_modifier.circle_a IN modifiers) OR
           (('PRODUCT_PROPERTY_DEFINITION_SCHEMA.CENTRE_OF_SYMMETRY' IN TYPEOF(SELF\geometric_tolerance.toleranced_shape_aspect)) AND
            (SELF\geometric_tolerance.toleranced_shape_aspect\shape_aspect.product_definitional = FALSE));
  WR2: NOT (geometric_tolerance_modifier.circle_a IN modifiers) OR
           (('PRODUCT_PROPERTY_DEFINITION_SCHEMA.DERIVED_SHAPE_ASPECT' IN TYPEOF(SELF\geometric_tolerance.toleranced_shape_aspect)) AND
           (SIZEOF(SELF\geometric_tolerance.toleranced_shape_aspect\derived_shape_aspect.deriving_relationships) = 1));
  WR3: NOT(SIZEOF([
    geometric_tolerance_modifier.individually,
    geometric_tolerance_modifier.each_element,
    geometric_tolerance_modifier.each_radial_element] * modifiers) = 1) OR
   ('SHAPE_ASPECT_DEFINITION_SCHEMA.COMPOSITE_GROUP_SHAPE_ASPECT' IN TYPEOF(SELF\geometric_tolerance.toleranced_shape_aspect));
  WR4: SIZEOF([
    geometric_tolerance_modifier.individually,
    geometric_tolerance_modifier.each_element,
    geometric_tolerance_modifier.each_radial_element] * modifiers) <= 1;

END_RULE;

FUNCTION acyclic_geometric_tolerance_relationship (relation : geometric_tolerance_relationship;
                                                  relatives : SET [1:?] OF geometric_tolerance;
                                                  specific_relation : STRING):BOOLEAN;
    LOCAL
      x : SET OF geometric_tolerance_relationship;
    END_LOCAL;

    IF relation.relating_geometric_tolerance IN relatives THEN
      RETURN (FALSE);
    END_IF;
    x := QUERY(geotol <* bag_to_set(
              USEDIN(relation.relating_geometric_tolerance,
              'SHAPE_TOLERANCE_SCHEMA.' + 'GEOMETRIC_TOLERANCE_RELATIONSHIP.' + 'RELATED_GEOMETRIC_TOLERANCE')) | specific_relation IN TYPEOF(geotol));
    REPEAT i := 1 TO HIINDEX(x);
      IF NOT acyclic_geometric_tolerance_relationship(x[i], relatives + relation.relating_geometric_tolerance, specific_relation) THEN
        RETURN (FALSE);
      END_IF;
    END_REPEAT;
    RETURN (TRUE);
  END_FUNCTION;

FUNCTION sts_get_product_definition_shape
 (input : geometric_tolerance_target) : product_definition_shape;
CASE TRUE OF ('SHAPE_DIMENSION_SCHEMA.DIMENSIONAL_LOCATION' IN TYPEOF(input)) :
                 RETURN(input\shape_aspect_relationship.relating_shape_aspect\shape_aspect.of_shape);
               ('SHAPE_DIMENSION_SCHEMA.DIMENSIONAL_SIZE' IN TYPEOF(input)) :
                 RETURN(input\dimensional_size.applies_to\shape_aspect.of_shape);
               ('PRODUCT_PROPERTY_DEFINITION_SCHEMA.PRODUCT_DEFINITION_SHAPE' IN TYPEOF(input)) :
                 RETURN(input);
               ('PRODUCT_PROPERTY_DEFINITION_SCHEMA.SHAPE_ASPECT' IN TYPEOF(input)) :
                 RETURN(input\shape_aspect.of_shape);
  OTHERWISE : RETURN(?);
  END_CASE;END_FUNCTION;

(*"shape_tolerance_schema"
// Note schema EXPRESS are in ..\resources\resource_name name_of_schema.xml

The *shape_tolerance_schema* provides the constructs for describing tolerances that apply to dimensions and to elements of *shape_aspect*. This schema includes two types of tolerance: plus-minus tolerance and geometrical tolerance. The plus-minus tolerance provides the constructs for specifying tolerances in one of two ways:

* the specification of upper and lower limits within which a dimension may vary;
* the specification of limits and fits as specified in ISO 286-l and ISO 286-2.

The representation of statistical tolerance may be associated with the direct specification of the upper and the lower limits of the plus-minus tolerance or with a geometric tolerance.

The geometrical tolerance provides the constructs for applying tolerance zones to elements of *shape_aspects*. A tolerance zone defines a region or an area within which a *shape_aspect* may vary and is bounded by a set of tolerance zone elements. These constructs support tolerances for the form, orientation, location, profile, and runout of a *shape_aspect*. A tolerance zone may be represented by specific geometry and is used for various tolerancing methods.

*)
(*"shape_tolerance_schema.__fund_cons"

A toleranced dimension is an exact dimension with a plus-minus tolerance. A plus-minus tolerance limits the dimensional variation of a dimension of a product. The plus-minus tolerance range is limited by one of two methods: assigned values, which define the upper bound and lower bound of a dimension, or a standard tolerance as specified in ISO 286-l and ISO 286-2. The tolerance with a statistical distribution provides an additional specification of the variation of a dimension and may be used with either a plus-minus tolerance or a geometric tolerance.

Tolerance zones as defined in ISO 1101 or an equivalent standard are represented in ISO 10303 either implicitly or explicitly. A tolerance zone is explicitly represented by *tolerance_zone*. When no explicit tolerance zone is represented, the implcit tolerance zone is included in the *geometric_tolerance*.

A key entity of the *shape_tolerance_schema* is <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance,geometric_tolerance>>. <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance,geometric_tolerance>> with subtypes and other related entities represent a *tolerance frame* as defined in ISO 1101.

[NOTE]
--
Alternatively a <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance,geometric_tolerance>> together with subtypes and other related entities can represent a *feature control frame* as defined in ASME Y14.5-2009 [11] or later editions of that standard.
--

The ISO 1101 concept of a *toleranced feature* is represented by the attribute <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance.toleranced_shape_aspect,toleranced_shape_aspect>>. The toleranced feature is either a <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>, the whole <<express:product_property_definition_schema.product_definition_shape,product_definition_shape>>, a <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_size,dimensional_size>> or a <<express:shape_dimension_schema.dimensional_location,dimensional_location>>.

The first compartment of a tolerance frame specifies the kind of geometrical characteristic. For each characteristic a specific entity is defined:

* <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.angularity_tolerance,angularity_tolerance>>;
* <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.circular_runout_tolerance,circular_runout_tolerance>>;
* <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.coaxiality_tolerance,coaxiality_tolerance>>;

* <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.parallelism_tolerance,parallelism_tolerance>>;
* <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.perpendicularity_tolerance,perpendicularity_tolerance>>;
* <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.position_tolerance,position_tolerance>>;
* <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.roundness_tolerance,roundness_tolerance>>;
* <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.straightness_tolerance,straightness_tolerance>>;
* <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.surface_profile_tolerance,surface_profile_tolerance>>;
* <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.symmetry_tolerance,symmetry_tolerance>>;
* <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.total_runout_tolerance,total_runout_tolerance>>.

The second compartment of a tolerance frame specifies a collection of information that is represented by several entities of this schema.

In the case that a *tolerance frame* has a third, and optionally, a fourth and fifth, compartment with references to one or several datums, the subtype <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance_with_datum_reference,geometric_tolerance_with_datum_reference>> shall be used. It's attribute <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance_with_datum_reference.datum_system,datum_system>> references either a <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_system,datum_system>> or a set of <<express:shape_aspect_definition_schema.datum_reference,datum_reference>>s. (*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_value"
A **tolerance_value** is the representation of plus-minus tolerances for a dimension. A **tolerance_value** specifies the numeric values added to the nominal dimension of a <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>.

The **lower_bound** and **upper_bound** are applied to the value of the dimension to determine the acceptable range of measured values. A **tolerance_value** may be either assigned by the user or specified according to ISO 286-l and ISO 286-2.
*)

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_value.__example"
Since the only constraint on the attribute values is that the upper bound be greater than the lower bound, the specification of a <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.plus_minus_tolerance,plus_minus_tolerance>> (e.g., 10.0+0.10+0.05) is permitted. In this case, the nominal dimension, 10.0, is not bounded by its associated tolerance zone.
*)

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_value.lower_bound"
the value of the tolerance that is added to the dimension value to establish the minimum deviation from the boundary toleranced from the nominal dimension.
*)


(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_value.upper_bound"
the value of the tolerance that is added to the dimension value to establish the maximum deviation from the boundary toleranced from the nominal dimension.
*)


(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_value.ubvc"
the numeric value of the **upper_bound** without unit component.
*)


(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_value.lbvc"
the numeric value of the **lower_bound** without unit component.
*)


(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_value.wr:WR1"
The value of the **upper_bound** shall be greater than the value of the **lower_bound**.
*)


(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_value.wr:WR2"
The **upper_bound** and the **lower_bound** shall have the same unit.
*)


(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_with_statistical_distribution"
A **tolerance_with_statistical_distribution** is the allocation of a tolerance in terms of a probability distribution. The <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.statistical_distribution_for_tolerance,statistical_distribution_for_tolerance>> may be associated with a tolerance value for a <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance,geometric_tolerance>> or a range of tolerances for a <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.plus_minus_tolerance,plus_minus_tolerance>>.
*)

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_with_statistical_distribution.__example"
The diameter of a shaft is toleranced by a <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.plus_minus_tolerance,plus_minus_tolerance>>. The <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.plus_minus_tolerance,plus_minus_tolerance>> specifies the range in which the diameter may vary. The <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.statistical_distribution_for_tolerance,statistical_distribution_for_tolerance>> associated to this <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.plus_minus_tolerance,plus_minus_tolerance>> specifies that the actual diameter values shall conform to a statistical distribution within the tolerance range.
*)

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_with_statistical_distribution.associated_tolerance"
the tolerance that is specified with a statistical distribution.
*)


(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_with_statistical_distribution.tolerance_allocation"
the statistical distribution that shall apply to the tolerance
*)


(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone"
A **tolerance_zone** is a type of <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>. A **tolerance_zone** is the region within which the toleranced feature shall be defined. The characteristics of the region are specified by the manner in which the toleranced feature is dimensioned.
*)

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone.__example"
A geometric location tolerance applied to a hole defines a <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone_form,tolerance_zone_form>> that may be described as cylindrical.
*)

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone.defining_tolerance"
all geometric tolerances which define a **tolerance_zone** for a <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>.
*)


(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone.form"
the representation of the applied shape that limits the specified tolerance for the **tolerance_zone**.
*)


(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone_definition"
A **tolerance_zone_definition** is a specification of the defining boundaries of a tolerance zone. A **tolerance_zone_definition** may be either a <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.projected_zone_definition,projected_zone_definition>> or a <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.non_uniform_zone_definition,non_uniform_zone_definition>>, or a <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.runout_zone_definition,runout_zone_definition>>.
*)

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone_definition.__example"
A flatness tolerance zone of a planar surface is bounded by two parallel, infinite planes separated by a distance of the tolerance magnitude.
*)

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone_definition.__note"
A pair of boundaries specified as a single *tolerance_zone_definition* may form either a partial or complete tolerance zone. When the tolerance zone is not fully bounded, it is appropriate to assume that the tolerance zone extends to infinity at the unbounded areas
*)

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone_definition.zone"
the <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone,tolerance_zone>> being defined.
*)


(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone_definition.boundaries"
a set of <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>> that define boundaries of the <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone,tolerance_zone>>.
*)

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone_definition.boundaries.__example"
A geometric location tolerance applied to a hole is defined to be a cylindrical zone in which the axis of the hole may vary. The cylindrical zone is symmetric about its axis. The two defining boundaries of this tolerance zone are the cylindrical surface and its axis. For a <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone,tolerance_zone>> defined by two parallel planes (or lines), each plane (or line) defines a boundary of the *tolerance_zone_definition*.
*)

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone_form"
A **tolerance_zone_form** is a description of the shape of the <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone,tolerance_zone>>.

"within a circle", "between two concentric circles", "between two equidistant curves", "within a cylinder", "between two coaxial cylinders", "between two equidistant surfaces", "non-uniform", "cylindrical or circular", and "spherical" are examples of descriptions of tolerance zone shapes.

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.tolerance_zone_form.name"
the description of a tolerance zone shape

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.angularity_tolerance.wr:IP1"

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.coaxiality_tolerance"
A **coaxiality_tolerance** is a type of <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance_with_datum_reference,geometric_tolerance_with_datum_reference>>. The rules governing coaxiality tolerance defined in ISO 1101, or ASME Y14.5-2018 or later editions of that standard shall apply.

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.coaxiality_tolerance.wr:WR1"
The **coaxiality_tolerance** shall contain one or two elements in its <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance_with_datum_reference.datum_system,datum_system>>.

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.cylindricity_tolerance"

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.directed_tolerance_zone"

The <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance.toleranced_shape_aspect,toleranced_shape_aspect>> shall be of invariance class surface revolute feature but not a helical shape.

The actual surface shall lie in a tolerance zone limited by two co-planar and concentric circles with a difference in radii of the tolerance value.
*)


(*"shape_tolerance_schema.roundness_tolerance.__note"

*)

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.roundness_tolerance.wr:WR1"

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.straightness_tolerance"
A **straightness_tolerance** is a type of <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance,geometric_tolerance>> that applies either to the intersection curves between the surface and the planes parallel to the reference plane, or to the extracted median curve. The rules governing straightness tolerance defined in ISO 1101, or ASME Y14.5-2009 or later editions of that standard shall apply.

The <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance.toleranced_shape_aspect,toleranced_shape_aspect>> is a surface or a straight line. Refer to the definition of straightness tolerance in ISO 1101 for a description of the different tolerance zones. In the case of intersection curves, the ideal features corresponding to the intersection curves shall be linear and there shall be another <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect,shape_aspect>>, which is related to the <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance.toleranced_shape_aspect,toleranced_shape_aspect>> by a <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship,shape_aspect_relationship>>. The <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship.name,name>> of the <<express:product_property_definition_schema.shape_aspect_relationship,shape_aspect_relationship>> shall be 'affected plane association'.

(*"shape_tolerance_schema.total_runout_tolerance"
A **total_runout_tolerance** is a type of <<express:shape_tolerance_schema.geometric_tolerance_with_datum_reference,geometric_tolerance_with_datum_reference>>. The rules governing total run-out tolerance defined in ISO 1101, or ASME Y14.5-2009 or later editions of that standard shall apply. The set of referenced datums shall contain one revolute surface feature. The tolerance zone is limited by:

* two coaxial cylinders, with a difference in radii equal to the tolerance value. In this case, the axis of the cylinders shall be the axis of the revolute surface feature, and the ideal feature corresponding to the toleranced surface is a cylinder;
* two parallel planes, separated by the distance specified by the tolerance value. In this case, the planes are perpendicular to the axis of the revolute surface feature, and the ideal feature corresponding to the toleranced surface is a plane.
* two offset revolute surfaces of any shape, with an offset distance equal to the tolerance value. In this case, the surfaces may be conic, spherical, or any other revolute shape.
*)

The *state_type_schema* represents the existence of possible states or types of state that an individual item may acquire.

(*"state_type_schema.__fund_cons"

A <<express:state_type_schema.state_type,state_type>> identifies a set of recognisable characteristics that can be used to distinguish an observed state. These characteristics specify a mode of being. When these characteristics are present for an item, the item is said to be in that state, as represented using <<express:state_observed_schema.state_observed,state_observed>>.

[NOTE]
--
An item may exhibit characteristics that match several <<express:state_type_schema.state_type,state_type>>s for a period of time.
--

In this document such a state type is recorded as an instance of the <<express:state_type_schema.state_type,state_type>> entity.

State types may be specified that are composed of multiple sub-state types. A <<express:state_type_schema.state_type,state_type>> may be related to another <<express:state_type_schema.state_type,state_type>> by a cause and effect relationship, where one <<express:state_type_schema.state_type,state_type>> causes or results from another. State types may also be related as a sequence, through which one <<express:state_type_schema.state_type,state_type>> may transition into another <<express:state_type_schema.state_type,state_type>>. The nature of the relationship between two <<express:state_type_schema.state_type,state_type>>s is defined by the role and description attributes of the <<express:state_type_schema.state_type_relationship,state_type_relationship>> entity.

Data recording the predicted or observed existence of an item in a state are the subject of the *state_observed_schema*.

// EXPRESS-G
