(*"topology_schema.__fund_cons"

The topological entities, *vertex*, *edge* etc., specified here have been defined independently of any use that may be made of them. Minimal constraints have been placed on each entity with the intention that any additional constraints will be specified by the using entity or by a defined context in which the entity is used. The intent is to avoid limiting the context or the use made of the entities. The only constraint is in the entity types provided for associating geometric information (see below, *Geometric associations*{blank}), for which specialised topological subtypes constitute the exclusive means of establishing direct associativity between geometric and topological elements at the integrated resource level.

The topological entities have been defined in a hierarchical manner with the *vertex* being the primitive entity. That is, all other topological entities are defined either directly or indirectly in terms of vertices.

Each entity has its own set of constraints. A higher-level entity may impose constraints on a lower-level entity. At the higher level, the constraints on the lower-level entity are the sum of the constraints imposed by each entity in the chain between the higher- and lower-level entities. The basic topological structures in order of increasing complexity are *vertex*, *edge*, *path*, *loop*, *face*, and *shell.*

In addition to the high-level structured topological entities *open_shell* and *closed_shell*, which are specialised subtypes of *connected_face_set*, the topology section includes the *connected_edge_set* and the general *connected_face_set*. These two entities are designed for the communication of collections of topological data where the constraints applied to shell are inappropriate.

The *poly_loop* is a loop with straight and coplanar edges and is defined as an ordered list of points. The *poly_loop* entity is used for the communication of faceted B-rep models. Many functions ensure consistency of the topology models by applying topological and geometric constraints to entities.

[[sec_5.2.1]]
==== Geometric associations

Many of the topological entities have a specialised subtype which enables them to be associated with geometric data. This association will be essential when communicating complex geometric models in clause 6 composed of both geometric and topological entities, such as boundary representation solid models. The specialised subtypes of *vertex*, *edge* and *face* are *vertex_point*, *edge_curve*, and *face_surface* respectively. For the *edge_curve* and *face_surface* the relationship between the geometric sense and the topological sense of the associated entities is also recorded. The key concept relating geometry to topology is the domain. The domain of a *point*, *curve*, or *surface* is just that point, curve, or surface. The domain of a *vertex*, *edge*, or *face* is the corresponding point, curve, or surface. The domain of a *loop* or *path* is the union of the domains of all the vertices and edges in the *loop* or *path*. (Except in the case of a vertex loop, this is a curve.) The domain of a shell is the union of the domains of all the vertices, edges, and faces in the shell. (For a *closed_shell* or *open_shell*, this is a surface.) The domain of a solid model is the region of space it occupies. The domain of a set or list is the union of the domains of the elements of that set or list. Wherever in this standard a geometrical concept such as connectedness or finiteness is discussed in relation to an entity, it is understood that the concept applies to the domain of that entity.

A key concept in describing domains is the idea of a manifold. Intuitively, a domain is a stem:[d]-manifold if it is locally indistinguishable from stem:[d]-dimensional Euclidean space. This means that the dimensionality is the same at each mathematical point, and self- intersections are prohibited. As defined in this standard, curves and surfaces may contain self-intersections, and hence need not be manifolds. However, the part of a curve or surface that corresponds to the domain of a topological entity such as an edge or face shall be a manifold.

As used in this standard, the terms "manifold", "boundary" , and " manifold with boundary" are identical to the usual mathematical definitions. A manifold with boundary differs from a manifold in that the boundary is allowed, but not required, to be non-empty.

A 1-manifold is a non-self-intersecting curve which does not include either of its end points. Examples of 1-manifolds are the real line and the unit circle. A "Y"-shaped figure is not a 1-manifold, and neither is the closed unit interval. A 2-manifold is a non-self-intersecting surface which does not include boundary curves. Examples of 2-manifolds include the unit sphere and the open disk stem:[{(x,y,0) : x^2 + y^2 < 1}] . The closed disk stem:[{(x,y,0) : x^2 + y^2 le 1}] is not a manifold. The domains of edges and paths, if present, are 1-manifolds. The domains of faces and closed shells, if present, are 2-manifolds.

Any curve which does not self-intersect is a 1-manifold with boundary. The closed disk stem:[{(x,y,0) : x^2 + y^2 le 1}] is a 2-manifold with boundary. The domain of an open shell, if present, is a 2-manifold with boundary. The domain of a manifold solid boundary representation or a faceted manifold boundary representation is a 3-manifold with boundary.

The boundary of a stem:[d]-manifold with boundary is a stem:[(d-1)]-manifold. For example, the boundary of a curve is the set of 0, 1, or 2 end points contained in that curve. The boundary of the closed disk stem:[{(x,y,0) : x^2 + y^2 le 1}] is the unit circle. The boundary of the domain of an open shell is the domain of the set of loops that bound holes in the shell. The boundary of a manifold solid boundary representation or a faceted manifold boundary representation is the domain of the set of bounding shells.

Curves and surfaces which are manifolds with boundary are classified as either open or closed. The terms "open" and "closed", when applied to curves or surfaces in this standard, should not be confused with the notions of "open set" or "closed set" from point set topology. The term "closed surface" is identical to the usual definition of a closed, connected, orientable 2-manifold. Examples of a closed surface are a sphere and a torus. The domain of a closed shell, if present, is a closed surface. Examples of open surfaces are an infinite plane, or a surface with one or more holes. The domain of an open shell, if present, is an open surface.

All closed surfaces that are physically manufacturable are orientable. Face domains, because they are always embeddable in the plane, are orientable. Open surfaces need not be orientable. For example, the Möbius strip is an open surface. Also, some manifolds are neither open nor closed as defined in this standard. The Klein bottle is an example. It is finite and its boundary is empty, but the surface is not orientable, and hence does not divide space into two regions. However, the domain of an open shell as defined in this standard must be orientable.

The term "genus" refers to an integer-valued function used to classify topological properties of an entity. This standard defines two different types of genus.

For an entity which can be described as a graph of edges and vertices, for example a loop, path, or wire shell, genus is equivalent to the standard technical term "cycle rank" in graph theory. It is _not_ equivalent to the standard usage of the term "genus" in graph theory. Intuitively, it measures the number of independent cycles in a graph. For example, a graph with exactly one vertex, joined to itself by stem:[n] self-loops, has genus stem:[n].

The genus of a closed surface stem:[X] is the number of handles that must be added to a sphere to produce a surface homeomorphic to stem:[X]. For example, the genus of a sphere is 0, and the genus of a torus is 1. This is identical to the standard technical term "genus of a surface" from algebraic topology. Adding a handle to a closed surface is the operation that corresponds to drilling a tunnel through the three-dimensional volume bounded by that surface. This can be viewed as cutting out two disks and connecting their boundaries with a cylindrical tube. Handles should not be confused with holes. As used in this standard, the term "hole" corresponds to the intuitive notion of punching a hole in a two-dimensional surface.

The surface genus definition is extended to orientable open surfaces as follows. Fill in every hole in the domain with a disk. The resulting surface is a closed surface, for which genus is already defined. Use this number for the genus of the open surface.

[[sec_5.2.2]]
==== Associations with parameter space geometry

A fundamental assumption in this clause is that the topology being defined is that of model space. The geometry of curves and points can also be defined in parameter space but, in general, the topological structure of, for example a *face*, will not be the same in the parametric space of the underlying surface as it is in model space.

Parametric space modelling systems differ from real space systems in the methodology used to associate geometry to topology. Parametric space modelling systems typically associate a different parametric space curve with each edge use (i.e., *oriented_edge* ). Every one of the parametric space curves associated with a given edge (by way of an edge use) describe the same point set in real space. The parametric space curves are defined in different parametric spaces. The parametric spaces are the surfaces which underlay the faces bordering on the edge. In a manifold solid the geometry of every *edge* is defined twice, once for each of the two *face* s which border on that *edge*.

Associating a parametric space curve with each edge use extends naturally to the use of degenerate edges (i.e., edges with zero length in real space). For example, a parametric space modelling system could represent a face that is triangular in real space as a square in parametric space. A straight forward way to do this is to represent one of the triangular face's vertices as a degenerate edge (but having two vertices); then there is a one-to-one mapping between edges in real space and model space. The degenerate edge has zero length in real space, but greater than zero length in parametric space. Degenerate edges also may be used for creating bounds around singularities such as the apex of a cone.

Real space modelling systems do not associate parametric space curves with each edge use nor do they allow degenerate edges. Since the parametric space modelling systems treatment of topology is an implementation convenience, this standard requires the use of real space topology. The parametric space modelling system's unique information requirements are satisfied using techniques at the geometric level.

[[sec_5.2.2.1]]
===== Edge_curve associations with parametric space curves

Techniques that can be used to associate parametric space curves with an *edge_curve* are:

[type=a]
. The *edge_geometry* attribute of an *edge_curve* may reference directly one *pcurve*, then only one *pcurve* is associated with that *edge_curve*.
. The *edge_geometry* attribute of an *edge_curve* can reference a *surface_curve*, or a subtype of *surface_curve* ; then associated with that *edge_curve* are the **pcurve**s (one or two) referenced by the *associated_geometry* attribute of the *surface_curve*. The curve referenced by the *curve_3d* attribute of the *surface_curve* is also associated with the *edge_curve* but that curve cannot be a parametric space curve and represents the model space geometry of the *edge*.
. The *edge_geometry* attribute of an *edge_curve* can reference a curve (not a *pcurve* ), then associated with the *edge_curve* are the **pcurve**s (zero or more) referenced by the *associated_geometry* attribute of every *surface_curve* whose *curve_3d* attribute references the same curve (i.e., is instance equal to, :=:) as the *edge_geometry* attribute of the *edge_curve*.

These techniques are formally defined in EXPRESS as the function *edge_curve_pcurves* which can be used to determine all the parametric space curves associated with a particular *edge*.

[NOTE]
--
For applications where the real space modelling systems are not required to understand parametric space curves, the parametric space modelling systems should be required to use only the third technique described above. Then, even if the *pcurve* s are ignored, the real space modelling system will have the correct geometry associated with all *edge_curve* s.
--

[NOTE]
--
Given the *pcurve* s of an *edge_curve*, determining which *oriented_edge* a pcurve shall be associated with is a matter of matching (:=:) the *basis_surface* of the *pcurve* with the *face_geometry* of the face bound by that *oriented_edge*. If two or more *pcurve* s are associated with the same *edge_curve* and are defined in the parametric space of the same surface, determining which *oriented_\-edge* the *pcurve* is associated with requires checking connectivity of the *pcurve* s in parametric space.
--

[[sec_5.2.3]]
==== Graphs, cycles, and traversals

A connected component of a graph is a connected subset of the graph which is not contained in any larger connected subset. We denote by stem:[M] the _multiplicity_ of a graph, that is, the number of connected components. Thus, a graph is connected if and only if stem:[M = 1].

Each component of a graph can be completely traversed, starting, and ending at the same vertex, such that every edge is traversed exactly twice, once in each direction, and every vertex is "passed through" the same number of times as there are edges using the vertex. If an (edge + edge traversal direction) is considered as a unit, each unique (edge + direction) combination shall occur once and only once in the traversal of a graph. During the traversal of a graph it will be found that there are one or more sets of alternating vertices and (edge + direction) units that form closed cycles.

The symbol stem:[G] will denote the _graph genus_ , which is, intuitively, the number of independent cycles in the graph. (Technically, stem:[G] is the rank of the fundamental group of the graph.)

Every graph satisfies the following Euler equation

[stem]
++++
(V - E) - (M - G) = 0
++++

where _*V*_ and _*E*_ are the numbers of unique vertices and edges in the graph.

[NOTE]
--
The following _graph traversal_ algorithm, [16], may be used to traverse a graph and compute _*M*_ and _*G*_ .

[type=a]
. Set _*M*_ and _*G*_ to zero.
. Start at any (unvisited) vertex. If there is no unvisited vertex, STOP. Mark the vertex as _visited_ . Increment _*M*_ . Traverse any edge at the vertex, marking the edge with the travel direction.
. After traversing an edge PQ to reach the vertex Q, do the following:

** When reaching a vertex for the first time, mark the edge just travelled as the _advent edge_ of the vertex. The advent edge is marked so that it can only be selected once in this direction.
** Mark the vertex as _visited_ .
** If this is the first traversal of the edge and the vertex Q has previously been visited, increment _*G*_ .
** Select an exit edge from the vertex according to the following rules:

[type=1]
... No edge may be selected that has previously been traversed in the direction away from the vertex Q.
... Select any edge, except the advent edge of Q, that meets rule (c1).
... If no edge meets rule (c2), select the advent edge.

** Traverse the selected exit edge and mark it with the travel direction.

. If no edge was selected in the previous step, go to step b, else go to step c
--

(*"topology_schema.shell"
The **shell** type collects together, for reference when constructing more complex models, the subtypes which have the characteristics of a shell.

A **shell** is a connected object of fixed dimensionality stem:[d = 0], 1, or 2, typically used to bound a region. The domain of a shell, if present, includes its bounds and stem:[0 le Xi < infty]

A shell of dimensionality 0 is represented by a graph consisting of a single vertex. The vertex shall not have any associated edges.

A shell of dimensionality 1 is represented by a connected graph of dimensionality 1.

A shell of dimensionality 2 is a topological entity constructed by joining faces along edges. Its domain, if present, is a connected, orientable 2-manifold with boundary, that is, a connected, oriented, finite, non-self-intersecting surface, which may be closed or open.
*)

*)

*)

(*"topology_schema.topological_representation_item.wr:IP1"
For each **topological_representation_item**, consider the set of <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> instances, <<express:topology_schema.edge_curve,edge_curve>>, and <<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>> instances that are referenced, either directly or recursively, from that **topological_representation_item**. (Do not include in this set oriented edges or faces, but do include the non-oriented edges and faces on which they are based.) Then no two distinct elements in this set shall have domains that intersect.
*)


(*"topology_schema.vertex"
A **vertex** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.topological_representation_item,topological_representation_item>>, and is the topological construct corresponding to a point. It has dimensionality 0 and extent 0. The domain of a vertex, if present, is a point in stem:[m] dimensional real space stem:[RR^m]; this is represented by the <<express:topology_schema.vertex_point,vertex_point>> subtype.
*)


(*"topology_schema.vertex.wr:IP1"
The **vertex** has dimensionality 0. This is a fundamental property of the vertex.
*)


(*"topology_schema.vertex.wr:IP2"
The extent of a **vertex** is defined to be zero.
*)


(*"topology_schema.vertex_point"
A **vertex_point** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.vertex,vertex>>, which has its geometry defined as a point.
*)


(*"topology_schema.vertex_point.vertex_geometry"
the geometric point which defines the position in geometric space of the vertex;
*)


(*"topology_schema.vertex_point.wr:IP1"
The domain of the vertex is formally defined to be the domain of its **vertex_geometry**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge"
An **edge** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.topological_representation_item,topological_representation_item>>, corresponding to the connection between two vertices. More abstractly, it may stand for a logical relationship between the two vertices. The domain of an edge, if present, is a finite, non-self-intersecting open curve in stem:[RR^m], that is, a connected 1-dimensional manifold. The bounds of an **edge** are two vertices, which need not be distinct. The edge is oriented by choosing its traversal direction to run from the first to the second vertex. If the two vertices are the same, the edge is a self-loop. The domain of the edge does not include its bounds, and stem:[0 < Xi < infty].

Associated with an edge may be a geometric <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>> to locate the edge in a coordinate space; this is represented by the **edge_curve** subtype. The curve shall be finite and non-self-intersecting within the domain of the edge. An **edge** is a graph, so its multiplicity M and graph genus stem:[G^e] may be determined by the graph traversal algorithm. Since stem:[M = bb E = 1], the Euler equation reduces in this case to

[[eqn2]]

[stem]
++++
V - (2 - G^{e}) = 0
++++

where stem:[V = 1] or 2, and stem:[G^e = 1] or 0.

Specifically, the topological edge defining data shall satisfy:

* An edge has two vertices, stem:[|E[V]| = 2 ]
* The vertices need not be distinct, stem:[1 le |E{V}| le 2]
* Equation <<eqn2>> shall hold stem:[|E{V}| - 2 + G^e = 0]
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge.edge_start"
start point (<<express:topology_schema.vertex,vertex>>) of the **edge**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge.edge_end"
end point (<<express:topology_schema.vertex,vertex>>) of the **edge**. The same <<express:topology_schema.vertex,vertex>> can be used for both **edge_start** and **edge_end**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge.wr:IP1"
The **edge** has dimensionality 1.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge.wr:IP2"
The extent of an **edge** shall be finite and nonzero.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_curve"
An **edge_curve** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>>, which has its geometry fully defined. The geometry is defined by associating the edge with a <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>> which may be unbounded. As the topological and geometric directions may be opposed, an indicator ({blank} **same_sense** {blank}) is used to identify whether the edge and curve directions agree or are opposed. The Boolean value indicates whether the <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>> direction agrees with (TRUE) or is in the opposite direction (FALSE) to the <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> direction. Any geometry associated with the vertices of the edge shall be consistent with the edge geometry. Multiple edges can reference the same curve.
*)

(*"topology_schema.edge_curve.__figure"
[[figure-topology_schema-Topfig23]]
.Edge_curve
====
image::Topfig23.gif[]
====
*)

(*"topology_schema.edge_curve.edge_geometry"
the <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>> which defines the shape and spatial location of the edge. This curve may be unbounded and is implicitly trimmed by the vertices of the edge; this defines the edge domain.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_curve.same_sense"
a logical flag which indicates whether (TRUE), or not (FALSE) the senses of the <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> and the <<express:geometry_schema.curve,curve>> defining the edge geometry are the same. The sense of an edge is from the edge start vertex to the edge end vertex; the sense of a curve is in the direction of increasing parameter.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_curve.same_sense.__note"
See <<figure-topology_schema-Topfig23>> for illustration of attributes.
*)

(*"topology_schema.edge_curve.wr:IP1"
The domain of the **edge_curve** is formally defined to be the domain of its **edge_geometry** as trimmed by the vertices. This domain does not include the vertices.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_curve.wr:IP2"
The extent of an **edge_curve** shall be finite and nonzero.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_curve.wr:IP3"
An **edge_curve** is a manifold.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_curve.wr:IP4"
An **edge_curve** is arcwise connected.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_curve.wr:IP5"
The edge start is not part of the edge domain.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_curve.wr:IP6"
The edge end is not part of the edge domain.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_curve.wr:IP7"
Vertex geometry shall be consistent with edge geometry.
*)


(*"topology_schema.oriented_edge"
An **oriented_edge** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>>, constructed from another <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> and contains a BOOLEAN orientation flag to indicate whether or not the orientation of the constructed <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> agrees with the orientation of the original <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>>. Except for possible re-orientation, the **oriented_edge** is equivalent to the original <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>>.
*)


(*"topology_schema.oriented_edge.__note"
A common practice in solid modelling systems is to have an entity that represents the " use" or " traversal " of an <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>>. This "use" entity explicitly represents the requirement in a manifold solid that each edge must be traversed exactly twice, once in each direction. The "use" functionality is provided by the <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> subtype *oriented_edge*.
*)

(*"topology_schema.oriented_edge.edge_element"
an <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> entity used to construct this **oriented_edge** ;
*)


(*"topology_schema.oriented_edge.orientation"
a BOOLEAN, if TRUE, the topological orientation as used coincides with the orientation, from start vertex to end vertex, of the **edge_element**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.oriented_edge.edge_start"
the start vertex of the oriented edge, this is derived from the vertices of the **edge_element** after taking account of the **orientation**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.oriented_edge.edge_end"
the end vertex of the oriented edge, this is derived from the vertices of the **edge_element** after taking account of the **orientation**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.oriented_edge.wr:WR1"
The **edge_element** shall not be an **oriented_edge**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.seam_edge"
A **seam_edge** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>>, which, additionally, identifies a corresponding <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>>. A **seam_edge** is always related to an <<express:topology_schema.edge_curve,edge_curve>> having a <<express:geometry_schema.seam_curve,seam_curve>> as <<express:topology_schema.edge_curve.edge_geometry,edge_geometry>>. The <<express:topology_schema.seam_edge,seam_edge>> identifies which, of the two <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>> instances defining the <<express:geometry_schema.seam_curve,seam_curve>>, is appropriate for this <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>>.
*)


(*"topology_schema.seam_edge.__note"
The inherited <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge.orientation,orientation>> attribute refers to the relationship to the <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge.edge_element,edge_element>> and not to the sense of the <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>>.
*)

(*"topology_schema.seam_edge.pcurve_reference"
the <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>> associated with the current orientation of the <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge.edge_element,edge_element>>;
*)


(*"topology_schema.seam_edge.wr:WR1"
the <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge.edge_element,edge_element>> attribute of this type of oriented edge shall be a <<express:geometry_schema.seam_curve,seam_curve>>.
*)


(*"topology_schema.seam_edge.wr:WR2"
The **pcurve_reference** shall be one of the <<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>> instances in the <<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve.associated_geometry,associated_geometry>> list of the <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge.edge_element,edge_element>>.
*)


(*"topology_schema.subedge"
A **subedge** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>>, whose domain is a connected portion of the domain of an existing <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>>. The topological constraints on a **subedge** are the same as those on an <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>>.
*)


(*"topology_schema.subedge.parent_edge"
the <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>>, or **subedge**, which contains the **subedge**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.subedge.wr:IP1"
The domain of the **subedge** is formally defined to be the domain of the **parent_edge**, as trimmed by the **subedge.edge_start** and **subedge.edge_end**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.subedge.wr:IP2"
The <<express:topology_schema.edge.edge_start,edge_start>> and <<express:topology_schema.edge.edge_end,edge_end>> shall be within the union of the domains of the vertices of the **parent_edge** and the domain of the **parent_edge**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.subedge.wr:WR1"
An instance of **subedge** shall not also be the instance of <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> in the role of **parent_edge**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.path"
A **path** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.topological_representation_item,topological_representation_item>>, consisting of an ordered collection of <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>> instances, such that the <<express:topology_schema.edge.edge_start,edge_start>> vertex of each edge coincides with the <<express:topology_schema.edge.edge_end,edge_end>> of its predecessor. The path is ordered from the <<express:topology_schema.edge.edge_start,edge_start>> of its first <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>> to the <<express:topology_schema.edge.edge_end,edge_end>> of its last <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>>.

The BOOLEAN value <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge.orientation,orientation>> in the <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>> indicates whether the edge direction agrees with the direction of the path (TRUE) or is in the opposite direction (FALSE).

An individual <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> can only be referenced once by an individual **path**.

An <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> can be referenced by multiple **path** instances. An <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> can exist independently of a **path**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.path.edge_list"
the list of <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>> entities which are concatenated together to form this **path**.;
*)


(*"topology_schema.path.wr:WR1"
The end vertex of each <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>> shall be the same as the start vertex of its successor.
*)


(*"topology_schema.path.wr:IP1"
A **path** has dimensionality 1.
*)


(*"topology_schema.path.wr:IP2"
A **path** is arcwise connected.
*)


(*"topology_schema.path.wr:IP3"
The edges of the path do not intersect except at common vertices.
*)


(*"topology_schema.path.wr:IP4"
A path has a finite, non-zero extent.
*)


(*"topology_schema.path.wr:IP5"
No **path** shall include two oriented edges with the same edge element and the same orientation.
*)


(*"topology_schema.subpath"
A **subpath** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.path,path>>, whose domain is a connected portion of the domain of an existing <<express:topology_schema.path,path>>. An instance of **subpath** may contain a combination of <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> and <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> such that the resulting domain of <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> and <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>>, together with their bounding vertices, is an arcwise connected, non-intersecting (except at common vertices), and 1-dimensional subdomain of the domain defined by the **parent_path**. The topological constraints on a **subpath** are the same as on a <<express:topology_schema.path,path>>.
*)


(*"topology_schema.subpath.parent_path"
the <<express:topology_schema.path,path>>, which contains the **subpath**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.subpath.wr:WR1"
An instance of **subpath** shall not also be the instance of <<express:topology_schema.path,path>> in the role of **parent_path**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.subpath.wr:WR2"
An instance of **subpath** that is an <<express:topology_schema.edge_loop,edge_loop>> shall not reference an instance of <<express:topology_schema.open_path,open_path>> in the role of **parent_path**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.subpath.wr:IP1"
The domain of the **subpath** shall be within the domain of the **parent_path**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.subpath.wr:IP2"
If the **subpath** is an <<express:topology_schema.edge_loop,edge_loop>>, the domain of the **subpath** shall be the same as the **parent_path**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.subpath.wr:IP2.__note"
The domain of the *subpath* that is an <<express:topology_schema.edge_loop,edge_loop>> is not a proper subset of the domain of the *parent_path* when that *parent_path* is also an edge_loop.
*)

(*"topology_schema.subpath.wr:IP3"
If the **subpath** is an <<express:topology_schema.edge_loop,edge_loop>> and the **parent_path** is an <<express:topology_schema.oriented_path,oriented_path>>, the <<express:topology_schema.oriented_path,oriented_path>> shall be closed to form a loop.
*)


(*"topology_schema.subpath.wr:IP3.__note"
The orientation of the *subpath* and *parent_path* loops can be different if the *subpath* is an <<express:topology_schema.edge_loop,edge_loop>> and the *parent_path* is an <<express:topology_schema.oriented_path,oriented_path>>.
*)

(*"topology_schema.oriented_path"
An **oriented_path** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.path,path>>, constructed from another <<express:topology_schema.path,path>> and contains a BOOLEAN orientation flag to indicate whether or not the orientation of the constructed <<express:topology_schema.path,path>> agrees with the orientation of the original <<express:topology_schema.path,path>>. Except for perhaps orientation, the **oriented_path** is equivalent to the other <<express:topology_schema.path,path>>.
*)


(*"topology_schema.oriented_path.path_element"
the <<express:topology_schema.path,path>> entity used to construct this **oriented_path** ;
*)


(*"topology_schema.oriented_path.orientation"
a BOOLEAN, if TRUE, the topological orientation as used coincides with the orientation of the **path_element** ;
*)


(*"topology_schema.oriented_path.edge_list"
the list of <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>>s which form the **oriented_path** ; this list is derived from the **path_element** after taking account of the **orientation** attribute;
*)


(*"topology_schema.oriented_path.wr:WR1"
The **path_element** shall not be an **oriented_path**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.open_path"
An **open_path** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.path,path>>, such that a traversal of the path visits each of its vertices exactly once. In particular, the start vertex and end vertex are different. An **open_path** is a graph for which stem:[M = 1] and stem:[bb G^p = 0], so the Euler equation link:6_schema.xml#eqnGM1 reduces in this case to

[[eqn3]]

[stem]
++++
(V - E) - 1 = 0
++++

where stem:[bb V] and stem:[bb E] are the number of unique vertices and edges in the path. Specifically, the topological attributes of a <<express:topology_schema.path,path>> shall meet the following constraints:

* The edges in the Path are unique,
[stem]
++++
(P)[E] = (P){E}
++++

* In the list ((P)[E])[V], two vertices appear once only and every other vertex appears exactly twice.
* The graph genus of the path is zero.
* Equation <<eqn3>> is interpreted as
[stem]
++++
|((P)[E]){V}| - |(P){E}| - 1 = 0
++++
*)


(*"topology_schema.open_path.ne"
the number of elements in the edge list of the path supertype;
*)


(*"topology_schema.open_path.wr:WR1"
The start vertex of the first edge shall not coincide with the end vertex of the last edge.
*)


(*"topology_schema.open_path.wr:IP1"
An **open_path** visits its <<express:topology_schema.vertex,vertex>>s exactly once. This implies that if a list of vertices is constructed from the edge data the first and last vertex will occur once in this list and all other vertices will occur twice.
*)


(*"topology_schema.loop"
A **loop** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.topological_representation_item,topological_representation_item>>, constructed from a single vertex, or by stringing together connected (oriented) edges, or linear segments beginning and ending at the same vertex. A loop has dimensionality 0 or 1. The domain of a 0-dimensional loop is a single point. The domain of a 1-dimensional loop is a connected, oriented curve, but need not be a manifold. As the loop is a cycle, the location of its beginning/ending point is arbitrary. The domain of the loop includes its bounds, and stem:[0 le Xi < infty]

A loop is represented by a single vertex, or by an ordered collection of <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>> instances, or by an ordered collection of points.

A loop is a graph, so M and the graph genus stem:[G^l] may be determined by the graph traversal algorithm. Since M = 1, the Euler equation reduces in this case to

[[eqn4]]

[stem]
++++
(V - E_{l}) - (1 - G^{l}) = 0
++++

where stem:[bb V] and stem:[bb E] are the number of unique vertices and oriented edges in the loop and stem:[G^l] is the genus of the loop.
*)


(*"topology_schema.loop.wr:IP1"
A **loop** has a finite, or, in the case of the <<express:topology_schema.vertex_loop,vertex_loop>>, zero extent.
*)


(*"topology_schema.loop.wr:IP2"
A **loop** describes a closed (topological) curve with coincident start and end vertices.
*)


(*"topology_schema.vertex_loop"
A **vertex_loop** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.loop,loop>>, of zero genus consisting of a single <<express:topology_schema.vertex,vertex>>. A <<express:topology_schema.vertex,vertex>> can exist independently of a **vertex_loop**. The topological data shall satisfy the following constraint:

Euler equation <<eqn4>> shall be satisfied:

[stem]
++++
|(L){V}| - 1 = 0
++++
*)


(*"topology_schema.vertex_loop.loop_vertex"
the <<express:topology_schema.vertex,vertex>> which defines the entire <<express:topology_schema.loop,loop>>;
*)


(*"topology_schema.vertex_loop.wr:IP1"
A **vertex_loop** has zero extent and dimensionality.
*)


(*"topology_schema.vertex_loop.wr:IP2"
The **vertex_loop** has genus 0.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_loop"
An **edge_loop** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.loop,loop>>, with nonzero extent. It is a <<express:topology_schema.path,path>> in which the start and end vertices are the same. Its domain, if present, is a closed curve. An **edge_loop** may overlap itself.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_loop.ne"
the number of elements in the edge list of the <<express:topology_schema.loop,loop>> supertype.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_loop.wr:WR1"
The start vertex of the first edge shall be the same as the end vertex of the last edge; this ensures that the path is closed to form a loop.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_loop.wr:IP1"
The Euler formula shall be satisfied: (number of vertices) + genus - (number of edges) = 1.
*)


(*"topology_schema.edge_loop.wr:IP2"
No <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> may be referenced more than once by the same **edge_loop** with the same <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge.orientation,orientation>>.
*)


(*"topology_schema.poly_loop"
A **poly_loop** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.loop,loop>>, with straight edges bounding a planar region in space. A **poly_loop** is a <<express:topology_schema.loop,loop>> of genus 1 where the <<express:topology_schema.loop,loop>> is represented by an ordered coplanar collection of <<express:geometry_schema.point,point>>s forming the vertices of the loop. The loop is composed of straight-line segments joining a point in the collection to the succeeding point in the collection. The closing segment is from the last to the first point in the collection. The direction of the loop is in the direction of the line segments. Unlike the <<express:topology_schema.loop,loop>> entity, the edges of the **poly_loop** are implicitly defined by the **polygon** points.

A **poly_loop** shall conform to the following topological constraints:

* The loop has a genus of one.
* Euler equation <<eqn4>> shall be satisfied:
[stem]
++++
|(L){V}| - |(L){E_{l}}| = 0
++++
*)


(*"topology_schema.poly_loop.__note"
This entity exists primarily to facilitate the efficient communication of faceted boundary representation models.
*)

(*"topology_schema.poly_loop.__note"
The *poly_loop* has vertices and <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>>s which are implicitly created. If, for example, A and B are consecutive points in the *polygon* list, there is an implicit <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>> from vertex point A to vertex point B with orientation value TRUE. It is assumed that when the higher-level entities such as shell and B-rep require checks on edge usage that this check will recognise, for example, a straight oriented edge from point B to point A with orientation TRUE as equal to an oriented edge from A to B with orientation FALSE.
*)

(*"topology_schema.poly_loop.polygon"
a list of <<express:geometry_schema.point,point>>s defining the loop; there are no repeated <<express:geometry_schema.point,point>>s in the list;
*)


(*"topology_schema.poly_loop.wr:IP1"
All the points in the **polygon** defining the **poly_loop** shall be coplanar.
*)


(*"topology_schema.poly_loop.wr:IP2"
The implicit edges of the **poly_loop** shall not intersect each other. The implicit edges are the straight lines joining consecutive <<express:geometry_schema.point,point>>s in the **polygon**.
*)


(*"topology_schema.face_bound"
A **face_bound** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.topological_representation_item,topological_representation_item>>, and is a loop which is intended to be used for bounding a face.
*)


(*"topology_schema.face_bound.bound"
the <<express:topology_schema.loop,loop>> which will be used as a face boundary;
*)


(*"topology_schema.face_bound.orientation"
indicates whether (TRUE), or not (FALSE) the loop has the same sense when used to bound the face as when first defined; if **orientation** is FALSE, the senses of all its component oriented edges are implicitly reversed when used in the face;
*)


(*"topology_schema.face_outer_bound"
A **face_outer_bound** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.face_bound,face_bound>>, which carries the additional semantics of defining an outer boundary on the face. A **face_outer_bound** shall separate the interior of the <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> from the exterior and shall enclose the interior domain of the <<express:topology_schema.face,face>>.

No more than one boundary of a <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> shall be of this type.
*)

(*"topology_schema.face_outer_bound.__example"
Any <<express:topology_schema.edge_loop,edge_loop>> on a plane surface may be used to define a *face_outer_bound* provided it is not enclosed in any other loop in the <<express:topology_schema.face,face>>.
*)
(*"topology_schema.face_outer_bound.__example"
A circular loop on a cylindrical surface cannot define a *face_outer_bound* since it does not enclose a closed domain in the surface.
*)

(*"topology_schema.face"
A **face** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.topological_representation_item,topological_representation_item>>, of dimensionality 2 corresponding to the intuitive notion of a piece of surface bounded by loops. Its domain, if present, is an oriented, connected, finite 2-manifold in stem:[RR^m]. A face domain shall not have handles, but it may have holes, each hole bounded by a loop. The domain of the underlying geometry of the face, if present, does not contain its bounds, and stem:[0 < Xi < infty]. A face is represented by its bounding loops, which are defined as <<express:topology_schema.face_bound,face_bound>> instances. A face shall have at least one bound, and the bounds shall be distinct and shall not intersect. One <<express:topology_schema.loop,loop>> is optionally distinguished, using the <<express:topology_schema.face_outer_bound,face_outer_bound>> subtype, as the "outer" loop of the face. If so, it establishes a preferred way of embedding the face domain in the plane, in which the other bounding loops of the face are "inside" the outer loop. Because the face domain is arcwise connected, no inner loop shall contain any other loop. This is true regardless of which embedding in the plane is chosen.

A geometric <<express:geometry_schema.surface,surface>> may be associated with the face. This may be done explicitly through the <<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>> subtype, or implicitly if the faces are defined by <<express:topology_schema.poly_loop,poly_loop>> instances. In the latter case, the surface is the plane containing the points of the <<express:topology_schema.poly_loop,poly_loop>> instances. In either case, a topological normal **n** is associated with the face, such that the cross product stem:[n xx t] points toward the interior of the face, where **t** is the tangent to a bounding loop. That is, each loop runs counter-clockwise around the face when viewed from above, if we consider the normal **n** to point up. Each loop is associated through a **face_bound** entity with a BOOLEAN flag to signify whether the loop direction is oriented correctly with respect to the face normal (TRUE) or should be reversed (FALSE). For a face of the subtype <<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>>, the topological normal **n** is defined from the normal of the underlying surface, together with the BOOLEAN attribute <<express:topology_schema.face_surface.same_sense,same_sense>>, and this in turn, determines on which side of the loop the face interior lies, using the cross-product rule described above.

When a <<express:topology_schema.vertex_loop,vertex_loop>> is used as a <<express:topology_schema.face_bound,face_bound>> the sense of the topological normal is derived from any other bounding loops, or, in the case of a <<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>>, from the <<express:topology_schema.face_surface.face_geometry,face_geometry>> and the <<express:topology_schema.face_surface.same_sense,same_sense>> flag. If the **face** has only one bound and this is of type <<express:topology_schema.vertex_loop,vertex_loop>>, then the interior of the **face** is the domain of the <<express:topology_schema.face_surface.face_geometry,face_geometry>>. In such a case the underlying surface shall be closed (such as a spherical surface.)

The situation is different for a face on an implicit planar surface, such as one defined by <<express:topology_schema.poly_loop,poly_loop>> instances, which has no unique surface normal. Since the face and its bounding loops lie in a plane, the outer loop can always be found without ambiguity. Since the face is required to be finite, the face interior must lie inside the outer loop, and outside each of the remaining loops. These conditions, together with the specified loop orientations, define the topological normal **n** using the cross-product rule described above. All <<express:topology_schema.poly_loop,poly_loop>> orientations for a given face shall produce the same value for **n**.

The edges and vertices referenced by the loops of a face form a graph, of which the individual loops are the connected components. The Euler equation for this graph becomes:

[[eqn5]]

[stem]
++++
(V - E) - (L - Sigma^{L}_{i=1} (G_{i}^{l})) = 0
++++

where stem:[G_i^l] is the graph genus of the stem:[i"th"] loop.

More specifically, the following topological constraints shall be met:

* The loops are unique (F){L} = (F)[L]
* In the list ((F)[L])[E] an individual edge occurs no more than twice.
* Each <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>> shall be unique
[stem]
++++
((F)[L])\{E_{l}} = ((F)[L])[E_{l}]
++++

* Equation <<eqn5>> shall be satisfied
[stem]
++++
|(((F)[L^{e}]){E}){V}| + |((F)[L^{v}]){V}| - |((F)[L]){E}| - |(F)[L]| + Sigma G^{l} = 0
++++
*)

(*"topology_schema.wire_shell"
A **wire_shell** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.topological_representation_item,topological_representation_item>>, which is a <<express:topology_schema.shell,shell>> of dimensionality 1. A **wire_shell** can be regarded as a graph constructed of vertices and edges. However, it is not represented directly as a graph, but indirectly, as a set of loops. It is the union of the vertices and edges of these loops that form the graph. The domain of a wire shell, if present, is typically not a manifold.

Two restrictions are placed on the structure of a wire shell.

(a) The graph as a whole shall be connected.

(b) Each edge in the graph shall be referenced exactly twice by the set of loops.

Writing stem:[G^w] for the graph genus, and setting the number of connected components M =1, the Euler graph equation becomes:

[[eqn6]]

[stem]
++++
(V - E) - (1 -G^{w}) = 0
++++

More specifically, the following topological constraints shall be met:

* The loops shall be unique.
[stem]
++++
(S^{w}){L} = (S^{w})[L]
++++

* Each edge shall either be referenced by two loops, or twice by a single loop. That is, in the list stem:[((S^w)[L\])[E\]], each edge appears exactly twice.
[stem]
++++
|((S^{w})[L])[E]| = 2|((S^{w})[L]){E}|
++++

* Each oriented edge shall be unique.
[stem]
++++
((S^{w})[L]){E_{l}} = ((S^{w})[L])[E_{l}]
++++

* Equation <<eqn6>> shall be satisfied.
[stem]
++++
|(((S^{w})[L]){E}){V}| - |((S^{w})[L]){E}| - 1 +G^{w} = 0
++++
*)

Two main applications of wire shells are contemplated.

The set of loops referenced by the faces of a closed shell automatically obey condition (b), but need not be connected. (*"topology_schema.open_shell"
An **open_shell** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.connected_face_set,connected_face_set>>, which is a <<express:topology_schema.shell,shell>> of dimensionality 2. Its domain, if present, is a finite, connected, oriented, 2-manifold with boundary, but is not a closed surface. It can be thought of as a <<express:topology_schema.closed_shell,closed_shell>> with one or more holes punched in it. The domain of an open shell satisfies stem:[0 < Xi < infty]. An open shell is functionally more general than a <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> because its domain can have handles. The shell is defined by a collection of <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> instances, which may be **oriented_face** instances. The sense of each face, after taking account of the orientation, shall agree with the shell normal as defined below. The **orientation** can be supplied directly as a BOOLEAN attribute of an <<express:topology_schema.oriented_face,oriented_face>>, or be defaulted to TRUE if the shell member is a <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> without the orientation attribute.

The following combinatorial restrictions on open shells and geometrical restrictions on their domains are designed, together with the informal propositions, to ensure that any domain associated with an open shell is an orientable manifold.

* Each face reference shall be unique.
* An **open_shell** shall have at least one <<express:topology_schema.face,face>>.
* A given <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> may exist in more than one **open_shell**.

The boundary of an open shell consists of the edges that are referenced only once by the <<express:topology_schema.face_bound,face_bound>> instances (loops) of its faces, together with all of their vertices. The domain of an open shell, if present, contains all edges and vertices of its faces.

The surface genus and topological normal of an open shell are those that would be obtained by filling in the holes in its domain to produce a closed shell. The topological normal can also be derived from the face normals after taking account of their orientation. The following Euler equation is satisfied by open shells. It is the most general form of Euler equation for connected, orientable surfaces.

[[eqn7]]

[stem]
++++
(V - E - L_{l} + 2F) - (2 - 2H - B) = 0
++++

where stem:[V], stem:[E],  stem:[bb(L)_l], stem:[F] are, respectively, the numbers of distinct vertices, edges, face bounds, and faces, H is the surface genus, and stem:[B] is the number of holes. stem:[B] can be determined directly from the graph of edges and vertices defining the bounds of the face, in the following manner:

Delete all edges from the graph that are referenced twice by the face bounds of the face.

Delete all vertices that have no associated edges.

Compute stem:[B] = the genus of the resulting graph.

If known a priori, the surface genus H may be used to check equation <<eqn7>> as an exact equality. Typically, this will not be the case, so equation <<eqn7>> or some equivalent formulation shall be used to compute the genus. Since H shall be a non-negative integer, this leads to the following inequality, a necessary condition for well-formed open shells.

[[eqn8]]
[stem]
++++
V - E - L_{l} + B "shall be even and" le 2-2F
++++

Specifically, the following topological constraints shall be met:

* Each face in the shell is unique. stem:[(S^o){F} = (S^o)[F\]]
* Each face bound in the shell is unique.
+
[stem]
++++
((S^{o})[F]){ L_{l}} = ((S^{o})[F])[L_{l}]
++++

* Each <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>> in the shell is unique.
+
[stem]
++++
((S^{o})[F])[L_{l}]){E_{l}} = ((S^{o})[F])[L_{l}])[E_{l}]
++++

* In the list stem:[(((S^o)[F\])[L_l\])[E\]] there is at least one edge that only appears once and no edges appear more than twice; the singleton edges are on the boundary of the shell.
* The Euler condition <<eqn8>>, and equation <<eqn7>> shall be satisfied.
+
[stem]
++++
|((((S^{o})[F]){ L_{l}^{e}}){E\}){V\}| + |(((S^{o})[F]){ L_{l}^{v}}){V}| - |(((S^{o})[F]){L_{l}})\{E\}|
++++
+
[stem]
++++
- |((S^{o})[F])[L_{l}]| + B "is even and" le 2 - 2|(S^{o})[F]|
++++
+
[stem]
++++
2 - 2H - B = |((((S^{o})[F]){ L_{l}^{e0}){E}){V}| + |(((S^{o})[F]){ L_{l}^{v}}){V}|
++++
+
[stem]
++++
- |(((S^{o})[F]){ L_{l}}){E}| - |((S^{o})[F])[L_{l}]| + 2|(S^{o})[F]|
++++
*)

*)

(*"topology_schema.closed_shell"
A **closed_shell** is a type of <<express:topology_schema.connected_face_set,connected_face_set>>, which is a <<express:topology_schema.shell,shell>> of dimensionality 2 which typically serves as a bound for a region in stem:[RR^3]. A closed shell has no boundary, and has non-zero finite extent. If the shell has a domain with coordinate space stem:[RR^3], it divides that space into two connected regions, one finite and the other infinite. In this case, the topological normal of the shell is defined as being directed from the finite to the infinite region.

The shell is defined by a collection of <<express:topology_schema.face,face>> instances, which may be <<express:topology_schema.oriented_face,oriented_face>> instances. The sense of each face, after taking account of the orientation, shall agree with the shell normal as defined above. The combinatorial restrictions on closed shells and geometrical restrictions on their domains ensure that any domain associated with a closed shell is a closed, orientable manifold. The domain of a closed shell, if present, is a connected, closed, oriented 2-manifold. It is always topologically equivalent to an H-fold torus for some stem:[H ge 0]. [stem]
++++
V - E - L_{l} " shall be even and" le 2 - 2F
++++

* Each face bound in the shell is unique. stem:[((S^c)[F\]){L_l} = ((S^c)[F\])[L_l\]]
* Each <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>> in the shell is unique.
[stem]
++++
((S^{c})[F])[L_{l}]){E_{l}} = ((S^{c})[F])[L_{l}])[E_{l}]
++++

* Each edge in the shell is either used by exactly two face bounds or is used twice by one face bound.
[stem]
++++
|(((S^{c})[F])[L_{l}])\{E_{l}}| = 2|(((S^{c})[F])[L_{l}]){E}|
++++

That is, in the list stem:[(((S^c)[F\])[L_l\])[E\]] each edge appears exactly twice.
* The Euler conditions <<eqn9>>, or optionally <<eqn7>> shall be satisfied.
[stem]
++++
2 - 2H = |((((S^{c})[F]){ L_{l}^{e0}){E}){V}| + |(((S^{c})[F]){ L_{l}^{v}}){V}|
++++

[stem]
++++
- |(((S^{c})[F]){ L_{l}}){E}| - |((S^{c})[F])[L_{l}]| + 2|(S^{c})[F]|
++++

[stem]
++++
|((((S^{c})[F]){ L_{l}^{e}}){E\}){V\}| + |(((S^{c})[F]){ L_{l}^{v}}){V}| - |(((S^{c})[F]){L_{l}}){E}|
++++

[stem]
++++
- |((S^{c})[F])[L_{l}]| + B "is even and" le 2 - 2|(S^{c})[F]|
++++
*)


(*"topology_schema.closed_shell.wr:IP1"
Every <<express:topology_schema.edge,edge>> shall be referenced exactly twice by the <<express:topology_schema.face_bound,face_bound>> instances of the faces.
*)


(*"topology_schema.closed_shell.wr:IP2"
Each <<express:topology_schema.oriented_edge,oriented_edge>> reference shall be unique.
*)


(*"topology_schema.closed_shell.wr:IP3"

(*"topology_schema.advanced_face"
An **advanced_face** is a type of
// face_surface
<<express:topology_schema.face_surface,face_surface>> that has additional constraints to ensure that the geometry is directly and completely defined. The **advanced_face** is the top level entity that is used to formulate the precise definition of a face with explicit topological bounds and fully defined geometry.

An **advanced_face** is required to be fully bounded by
// edge_loop
<<express:topology_schema.edge_loop,edge_loop>> instances or by
// vertex_loop
<<express:topology_schema.vertex_loop,vertex_loop>> instances.

At most one of the <<express:topology_schema.face.bounds,bounds>> instances of the face may be of type
// face_outer_bound
<<express:topology_schema.face_outer_bound,face_outer_bound>>.
*)

(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.__example"
Any
// edge_loop
<<express:topology_schema.edge_loop,edge_loop>> on a plane surface may be used to define a
// face_outer_bound
<<express:topology_schema.face_outer_bound,face_outer_bound>> provided it is not enclosed in any other loop in the
// face
<<express:topology_schema.face,face>>.
*)
(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.__example"
A circular loop on a
// cylindrical_surface
<<express:geometry_schema.cylindrical_surface,cylindrical_surface>> cannot define a
// face_outer_bounds
<<express:topology_schema.face_outer_bound,face_outer_bound>> since it does not enclose a closed domain in the surface.
*)

(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.__note"
For some types of closed or partially closed surfaces, it may not be possible to identify a unique outer bound.
*)

(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.face_geometry"
one of:
// elementary_surface
<<express:geometry_schema.elementary_surface,elementary_surface>>,
// swept_surface
<<express:geometry_schema.swept_surface,swept_surface>>, or
// b_spline_surface
<<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_surface,b_spline_surface>>.
*)


(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.wr:WR1"
The geometry of all bounding edges of the face shall be fully defined as
// edge_curve
<<express:topology_schema.edge_curve,edge_curve>> instances.
*)


(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.wr:WR2"
The types of curve used to define the geometry of edges shall be restricted to
// line
<<express:geometry_schema.line,line>> instances,
// conic
<<express:geometry_schema.conic,conic>> instances,
// polyline
<<express:geometry_schema.polyline,polyline>> instances,
// surface_curve
<<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve,surface_curve>> instances, or
// b_spline_curve
<<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_curve,b_spline_curve>> instances.
*)


(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.wr:WR3"
All vertices used in the face definition shall be of type
// vertex_point
<<express:topology_schema.vertex_point,vertex_point>> with geometry defined by a
// cartesian_point
<<express:geometry_schema.cartesian_point,cartesian_point>>.
*)


(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.wr:WR4"
The use of oriented paths in the definition of the
// edge_loop
<<express:topology_schema.edge_loop,edge_loop>> instances of the
// advanced_face
<<express:topology_schema.advanced_face,advanced_face>> is prohibited.
*)


(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.wr:WR5"
If the face geometry is of type
// swept_surface
<<express:geometry_schema.swept_surface,swept_surface>> then the
// swept_surface.swept_curve
<<express:geometry_schema.swept_surface.swept_curve,swept_curve>> used in the definition shall be of type
// line
<<express:geometry_schema.line,line>>,
// conic
<<express:geometry_schema.conic,conic>>,
// polyline
<<express:geometry_schema.polyline,polyline>>, or
// b_spline_curve
<<express:geometry_schema.b_spline_curve,b_spline_curve>>.
*)


(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.wr:WR6"
For any
// vertex_loop
<<express:topology_schema.vertex_loop,vertex_loop>> used to bound the face the
// loop_vertex
<<express:topology_schema.vertex_loop.loop_vertex,loop_vertex>> shall be of type
// vertex_point
<<express:topology_schema.vertex_point,vertex_point>> and the geometry shall be defined by a
// cartesian_point
<<express:geometry_schema.cartesian_point,cartesian_point>>.
*)


(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.wr:WR7"
The face bounds shall be defined by either
// edge_loop
<<express:topology_schema.edge_loop,edge_loop>> instances or
// vertex_loop
<<express:topology_schema.vertex_loop,vertex_loop>> instances.
*)


(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.wr:WR8"
If a
// surface_curve
<<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve,surface_curve>> is used as part of a face bound then the
// surface_curve.associated_geometry
<<express:geometry_schema.surface_curve.associated_geometry,associated_geometry>> attribute shall reference
// pcurve
<<express:geometry_schema.pcurve,pcurve>> instances not
// surface
<<express:geometry_schema.surface,surface>> instances.
*)


(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.wr:WR9"
If a
// polyline
<<express:geometry_schema.polyline,polyline>> is used either to define a
// swept_surface
<<express:geometry_schema.swept_surface,swept_surface>> or as part of a face bound, it shall contain at least three points.
*)


(*"topology_schema.advanced_face.wr:IP1"
Any instance of **advanced_face** which has the geometry of a complete
// spherical_surface
<<express:geometry_schema.spherical_surface,spherical_surface>> shall be bounded by a
// vertex_loop
<<express:topology_schema.vertex_loop,vertex_loop>> located at the point where the z axis of the placement coordinate system leaves the surface of the sphere, (i.e at the 'North Pole' of the sphere).
*)

data/resource_docs/geometric_and_topological_representation/resource.xml
*)
